text: You have said that, / as he took money from you many times, / he owes you / five thousand rupees all together.
options: as he took money from you many times
explanation: ‘All together’ must be replaced with ‘altogether’, which means totally. Hence, ‘five thousand rupees altogether’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I stayed in my hometown with my parents on the pandemic.
explanation: ‘On’ is used to indicate a specific occasion or day. ‘During’ is used to indicate a specific period of time. Similarly, ‘pandemic’ is a specific period of time. Hence, ‘during’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In August, she will be / enjoying / all the fruits her grandmother / will plant last January.
explanation: The phrase ‘last January’ indicates the use of simple past tense. ‘Will plant’ must be replaced with the past form ‘planted’. Hence, ‘planted last January’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The compensation that the [A] / Government agreed to provide to [B] / the dependents of the [C] / train accident is fairly less [D].
explanation: ‘Less’ must be replaced with ‘low’ as there is no comparison in this sentence. Hence, ‘train accident is fairly low’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The more it rains,/ worse/ the roads become/ No error
explanation: ‘Worse’ must be replaced with ‘the worse’. When change in one thing causes the change in the other and two comparative degrees are used to indicate this relationship, it is called successive comparison. Article ‘the’ is used before both the comparative degrees. Hence, ‘the worse’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mr. Unkerton glanced / to the inspector, / who merely snorted / and looked at the ceiling.
explanation: ‘To’ must be replaced with ‘at’ as we use ‘at’ with ‘glance’ for a person. Hence, ‘at the inspector’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She spotted the novel [A] / and shouted, "Here the book lies [B] / that we were searching for[C] / all around."[D]
explanation: ‘That’ is a relative pronoun which takes a noun or pronoun as its antecedent. In the given sentence, ‘the book’ is the antecedent, which will be used before ‘that’. Hence, and shouted, “Here lies the book is the most appropriate answer.

text: Raghu did not get the job / because he did not have / experience enough for the post.
options: Raghu did not get the job
explanation: ‘Enough’ is an adjective which describes the noun ‘experience’, therefore ‘enough’ will be used before ‘experience’. Hence, ‘enough experience for the job’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If there is an error in the given sentence, choose the correct answer from the options without changing the tense. One of the four options has same response as the original sentence, which can be chosen in case of agreement with the original sentence. I will have been studying English for three years by the end of this course.
options: I had been studying English for three years by the end of this course.
I have been studying English for three years by the end of this course.
I will have been studying English for three years by the end of this course.
I was studying English for three years by the end of this course.
explanation: end of this course. Pinnacle Spot the Error There is no error in the given sentence. Hence, the sentence given in option (c) is the most appropriate answer.

text: Identify the error in the following sentence. The police are searching about the missing jewellery.
explanation: ‘For’ is the fixed preposition used after the verb ‘search’. Hence, ‘for’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: John is really / good in/ playing/ the piano.
explanation: The structure ‘good + at + Ving’ is used to show that you are very skilful and clever at doing something. Hence, ‘good at’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The Supreme Court set away / the verdict of the High Court / and agreed to hear the plea / of the complainant.
options: and agreed to hear the plea
the verdict of the High Court
explanation: ‘Set away’ must be replaced with ‘set aside’. The phrasal verb ‘set aside’ means to deprive of legal effect because it has been proved wrong. The given sentence states that the Supreme Court set aside the verdict of the High Court. Hence, ‘The Supreme Court set aside’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mrs. Premlatha asked / Malini to hand down / all the / payment slips.
explanation: ‘Hand down’ must be replaced with ‘hand out’. The phrasal verb ‘hand out’ means to give a slip or document to someone. The given sentence talks about giving all the payment slips. Hence, ‘Malini to hand out’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She is / as more intelligent as / her brothers are.
explanation: ‘As + adjective/adverb + as’ is a comparative structure in which the adjective or the adverb is always in the positive degree. Therefore, ‘more’ will be replaced with ‘much’. Hence, ‘as much intelligent as’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He is waiting / at airport to receive / Mr. Smith, who is / coming from South Africa.
explanation: Article ‘the’ is used to refer to a specific or particular noun. ‘Airport’ given in the sentence is specific as the person is waiting there. Hence, ‘at the airport to receive’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I hope that / yesterday's lunch / at Rahul's place / was at your liking.
explanation: “To one’s liking” is the correct phrase, which means appealable or enjoyable to someone. Therefore, ‘at your liking’ must be replaced with ‘to your liking’. Hence, ‘was to your liking’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She forbade / him not / to enter that / room.
explanation: ‘Not’ must be removed from this sentence. ‘Forbade’ is the past form of ‘forbid’, which means to not allow someone to do something. The use of ‘not’ with ‘forbade’ is superfluous. Hence, ‘forbade him to’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He climbed of / the steep mountain trail, / his backpack heavy / with supplies for the journey.
explanation: ‘Climbed of’ must be replaced with ‘climbed up’. ‘Up’ is used to indicate upwards movement. Hence, ‘he climbed up’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Sam and Teena / had wondering / what to do this weekend.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of present continuous tense and the subject ‘Sam and Teena’ is plural. ‘Plural Subject + are + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure for it. Hence, ‘are Pinnacle Spot the Error wondering’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: You know that I am fond of reading / and also that all books are my favourite / but you don’t know that this is one of / my favourite book.
options: but you don’t know that this is one of
and also that all books are my favourite
You know that I am fond of reading
explanation: ‘One of + plural noun’ is the correct grammatical structure. Therefore, the plural noun ‘books’ will be used. Hence, ‘my favourite books’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: This is a very difficult task to accomplish.
A young boy offered her his seat.
I wish I had eraser to erase all the mistakes in my life.
I have a lot of work to complete.
explanation: Article ‘an’ will be used before the noun ‘eraser’ as it starts with a vowel sound. Hence, the correct sentence is- ‘I wish I had an eraser to erase all the mistakes in my life.’

text: In addition with / the existing crisis in economy, / the rise of hunger index / is another cause of worry.
explanation: ‘In addition to’ is the correct phrase. Hence, ‘in addition to’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: She usually walks her dog in the park every morning.
The train leaves the station at 8:00 a.m. every day.
They play chess together on weekends.
explanation: ‘The given sentence is in the simple present tense and ‘Singular Subject(He) + does + not + V1’’ is the correct grammatical structure for it. Hence, the correct sentence is- ‘He doesn’t like spicy food.’

text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: An intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft plays the crucial role in neural communication.
An intricate dance of neurotransmitters in a synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication.
The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication.
The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in a synaptic cleft plays the crucial role in neural communication.
explanation: synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication. ‘Dance’ and ‘cleft’ mentioned in the sentence are specific and we generally use the definite article ‘the’ before a specific or particular noun. The noun ‘role’ is not specific and we generally use an indefinite article before a non-specific noun. The word ‘crucial’ starts with a consonant sound, therefore, article ‘a’ will be used before it. Hence, the sentence given in option (c) is correct.

text: He will have to / knuckle up really seriously, / if he wants to / crack the upcoming deal.
explanation: ‘Knuckle up’ must be replaced with ‘knuckle down’. The phrasal verb ‘knuckle down’ means to put in serious effort. The given sentence states that he will have to knuckle down really seriously if he wants to crack the upcoming deal. Hence, ‘knuckle down really seriously’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
options: A lot of books and notes place in order look most fascinating.
A lot of books and notes placed in order look fascinating.
A lot of books and notes placed on order looks most fascinating.
A lot of book and notes placed in order looks most fascinating.
explanation: fascinating. ‘A lot of books and notes’ is a plural subject that will take ‘look’ as a plural verb. The phrase ‘in order’ means arranged systematically. We can not use the superlative degree of ‘fascinating’ as there is no comparison with any other thing. Hence, the sentence given in option (b) is grammatically correct.

text: He missed the college bus / because he woke up / unpardonably lately in the morning.
explanation: ‘Lately’ must be replaced with ‘late’. ‘Late’ means after the usual or expected time. ‘Lately’ means in the recent times. The given sentence is talking about waking up after the expected time in the morning. Hence, ‘unpardonably late in the morning’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: After the match, / the stadium was the messiest / it’s ever been.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Gita got onto / the book / she was reading / this morning.
explanation: ‘Got onto’ must be replaced with 'got into'. The phrasal verb ‘got into’ means became interested in a subject or activity. The given sentence talks about the interest of Gita in the book she was reading. Hence, ‘Gita got into’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Although experts are worried / that retail inflation is rising / at a steep rate, / the crisis will soon blow away.
options: the crisis will soon blow away
explanation: ‘Blow away’ must be replaced with ‘blow over’. The phrasal verb ‘blow over’ means to pass by or to end. The given sentence states that the crisis will soon end. Hence, ‘the crisis will soon blow over’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the option that has an error in the use of present tense.
options: The painter is painting the wall right now.
The mother cooks delicious food for her children.
I am observing your mischievous activities for half an hour.
I have performed all my duties with utmost sincerity.
explanation: hour. Present perfect continuous tense will be used in this sentence as a fixed period of time is mentioned with the preposition ‘for’. Therefore, ‘am observing’ must be replaced with ‘have been observing’. Hence, the correct sentence is - ‘I have been observing your mischievous activities for half an hour.’

text: My mother is 51 years old, / and my uncle is 48 years old. / So my mother is old than my uncle.
options: and my uncle is 48 years old.
So my mother is old than my uncle
explanation: ‘Old’ must be replaced with the comparative degree ‘older’ as the given sentence compares the age of mother and uncle. Hence, ‘So my mother is older than my uncle’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My sister is allergic with peanuts, so be cautious when preparing her meal
explanation: ‘To’ is the fixed preposition used after the adjective ‘allergic’. Hence, ‘allergic to peanuts’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: They have an information about the event.
The cat is sleeping on a mat.
She is an artist at a local gallery.
Can you bring me the keys to the car?
explanation: ‘Information’ is an uncountable noun and we generally do not use indefinite articles (a/an) with uncountable nouns. Therefore, ‘an’ will be removed. Hence, the correct sentence is- ‘They have information about the event.’

text: Whenever she is coming / here, she brings / many gifts for everyone.
explanation: ‘Whenever’ is used when one action is always followed by another action. Simple present tense is used with ‘whenever’. ‘She’ is a singular subject that will take ‘comes’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘Whenever she comes’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
options: She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes was dirtier.
She was not allow to enter the hotel as her clothes were dirty.
She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes were dirtier.
She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes were dirty.
explanation: were dirty. ‘Singular Subject + was + V3’ is the correct passive structure for simple past tense. ‘Clothes’ is a plural subject that will take ‘were’ as a plural verb. Hence, the sentence given in option (d) is correct.

text: My aunt came from Switzerland by the flight which was landing at 5:00 a.m. yesterday.
explanation: We generally do not use article ‘the’ after ‘by’ when we mention the means of transport such as bus, train, bike, car, flight, etc. Therefore, article ‘the’ will be removed. Hence, ‘Switzerland by’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: (1) We knocked across (2) early on Saturday (3) to enjoy (4) the beautiful weather.
explanation: ‘Knocked across’ must be replaced with the phrasal verb ‘knocked off’. ‘Knock off’ means to stop work. The given sentence states that we stopped work early on Saturday to enjoy the beautiful weather. Hence, ‘We knocked off’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He bought strange vintage car on auction from the customs department.
explanation: We generally use an indefinite article (a/an) before a non-specific noun. In the given sentence, the word ‘strange’ starts with a consonant sound. Therefore, article ‘a’ will be used. Hence, ‘a strange vintage car’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I thought of this idea / just when you called / me yesterday.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Meenu looks / much better / today.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Mr. Abhilash and his family / have received / no informations / about the incident.
explanation: ‘Informations’ must be replaced with ‘information’ as ‘information’ is an uncountable noun and its plural cannot be formed. Hence, 'no information' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Every students in the hostel decided to travel to Delhi to witness the Republic Day parade.
explanation: ‘Everyone/each/ every/ nothing/ everything/ anything/ either/ neither’ represents a singular noun. Therefore, ‘students’ must be replaced with the singular noun ‘student’. Hence, ‘Every student in the hostel’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: By this time next year / I will had graduated from college / and starting my first job / in the field of marketing.
options: I will had graduated from college
explanation: ‘Subject + will have + V3’ is the correct grammatical structure for a sentence which is in the future perfect tense. Therefore, ‘will had’ must be replaced with ‘will have’. Hence, ‘I will have graduated from college’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I are dancing with my husband at my sister’s wedding.
explanation: ‘Am’ is the correct helping verb to use with ‘I’ in present continuous tense. Hence, ‘I am dancing’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: After the concert was over, / they go to a restaurant, / had dinner together / and talked until midnight.
explanation: Pinnacle Spot the Error The given sentence is in the past tense, so it must have the verb in the past form (V2), not the present form (go). Hence, ‘they went to a restaurant’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Renewable energy / sources like solar and wind power / will replaced traditional fossil fuels / and help reduce carbon emissions.
options: sources like solar and wind power
explanation: ‘Modal verbs’ are auxiliary verbs(also called helping verbs) like can, will, could, shall, must, would, might, and should. However, after a modal verb, we generally use the first form of the verb (V1). Hence, ‘will replace(V1) traditional fossil fuels’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: No other place in this country is so better as Gulmarg, Kashmir.
explanation: Positive degree adjective is used in the structure ‘as…as’ or ‘so…as’ to make a comparison. Therefore, ‘better’ must be replaced with ‘good’. Hence, ‘so good as’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Our family is planning / a trip to Europe next summer / where we should visit several famous / landmarks and enjoy local cuisine.
options: where we should visit several famous
a trip to Europe next summer
explanation: ‘Should’ must be replaced with ‘will’ as the action of visiting several famous landmarks will happen in the future (next summer). Hence, ‘where we will visit several famous’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It is he who work for the company for more than a decade.
explanation: ‘Who work’ must be replaced with ‘who has been working’ as we use the perfect continuous tense with ‘for/since’ to indicate time period. Hence, ‘who has been working’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The windows / violent banged / during the / storm yesterday.
explanation: ‘Violent’ must be replaced with ‘violently’ as the given sentence needs an adverb to modify the verb ‘banged’. Hence, ‘violently banged’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Neither my brother nor my brothers-in-law / attended the meeting / as his health is not more good.
options: Neither my brother nor my brothers-in-law
as his health is not more good
explanation: ‘More’ must be removed as we use comparative degree adjective to make a comparison but there is no comparison between the health of two people. The first part of the sentence is in the past tense, so the verb in the second clause will also be in the past tense(V2). Hence, ‘as his health was not good’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Rahul thinks he is as smarter as his friends in the class.
explanation: ‘As + adjective/adverb + as’ is a comparative structure in which we always use positive degree. Therefore, ‘smarter’ must be replaced with ‘smart’. Hence, ‘he is as smart as’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Solutions to the country’s interior problems are still a long way away.
explanation: The correct word to use in this sentence is ‘internal’, not ‘interior’. ‘Internal’ means occurring inside a country. Hence, the country’s internal is the most appropriate answer.

text: They secret / decided / to leave / the town.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adverb ‘secretly’ to modify the verb ‘decided’, not the noun ‘secret’. Hence, ‘They secretly’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He ran quick to catch the bus.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adverb ‘quickly’ to modify the verb ‘ran’, not the adjective ‘quick’. Hence, ‘quickly’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mrs. Sreelakshmi’s / musical intelligence / is superior than / Mrs. Suma’s.
explanation: There are some words that take the preposition ‘to’ after them. For example:- superior to, inferior to, prior to, elder to, junior to, senior to, etc. Hence ‘is superior to’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The employees were comfortable / with me and they talked about / their problems since / I has worked there as a manager.
options: I has worked there as a manager.
with me and they talked about
explanation: The given sentence is in the past tense, so it must have the verb of past tense. ‘Had’ will be used instead of ‘has’. Hence, ‘I had worked there as a manager’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an adverbial usage error. Mr. Arun / will pay dear / for his / financial mistake.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adverb ‘dearly’ to modify the verb ‘pay’, not the adjective ‘dear’. Hence, ‘will pay dearly’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My brother received / his MBA degree into / the university last year.
explanation: ‘Into’ must be replaced with 'from' as we use ‘from’ to indicate the source of something. Hence, ‘his MBA degree from’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He replied / in a dry tone, / “Ouch! I will not work / for you anymore.”
explanation: ‘Ouch!’ is used to express pain. However, in the given sentence, the speaker replied in a dry tone. So, the correct interjection to use is ‘Ugh!’. Hence, ‘Ugh! I will not work for you anymore’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mr. Surya / have no interior / motive in offering / you support.
explanation: ‘Have no interior’ must be replaced with ‘has no ulterior’. ‘Mr. Surya’ is a singular subject that will take ‘has’ as a singular verb. Also, the correct word to use here is ‘ulterior’. ‘Ulterior motive’ means a secret reason for doing something. Hence, ‘has no ulterior’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: By the end of / this month, he / will been working / for five years.
explanation: ‘Will been’ must be replaced with ‘will have been’. Future perfect continuous tense (will have been + Ving) is used to talk about the duration of an action that has happened until some point in the future and will still be happening. Hence, ‘will have been working’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I have the hundred reasons to not attend the meeting tomorrow.
explanation: The reasons given in the sentence are not specific and we use indefinite article for a non-specific noun. Article ‘a’ will be used as the word ‘hundred’ begins with a consonant sound. Hence, ‘I have a hundred reasons’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: After I retire, I started a second career / as a writer and published several books / which allowed me to share my stories / and insights with a wider audience.
options: and insights with a wider audience
After I retire, I started a second career
as a writer and published several books
which allowed me to share my stories
explanation: If two actions took place in the past then the 1st action must be in the Past perfect tense(Had + V3) and the 2nd action must be in the Simple Past tense(V2). However, the V3 form of ‘retire’ is ‘retired’. Hence, ‘After I had retired (V3)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. Identify the part that has an error. Select 'No error' if there is no error. Although the team had trained diligently for months, they had still overwhelmed by the opponent's unexpected tactics.
explanation: ‘Had’ must be replaced with ‘were’ as the given sentence is an example of a passive voice of simple past tense and ‘Plural subject (they) + were + V3’ is the correct grammatical structure for it. Hence, ‘were still overwhelmed(V3)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Due to the pandemic, / the prices of / medicines increased / every day since / last December.
explanation: We use present continuous tense with ‘for/since’ to show that something has been happening for a period of time. ‘Plural subject (prices) + have been + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure for it. Hence, ‘medicines have been increasing’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment in which the article has been used INCORRECTLY. UNESCO works to / strengthen an intellectual / and moral solidarity / of humankind.
explanation: Indefinite article ‘a/an’ is not used for an abstract noun(solidarity). The definite article ‘the’ is used before a specific or particular noun. The given sentence is referring to a specific type of solidarity. Hence, ‘strengthen the intellectual and Pinnacle Spot the Error moral solidarity’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Dr. Sinha has / brought about a new / book on social / impact of child labour.
explanation: ‘Brought out’ is the correct phrasal verb here, which means ‘published’. The given sentence is talking about publishing a new book. Hence, ‘brought out a new’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: It is said that Joseph was not ready to go to war.
Karl Marx was a renowned social scientist.
Indian force are known for their loyalty and integrity.
It is impossible to wake Christine up in the morning.
explanation: ‘Forces’ will be used instead of ‘force’ according to the plural verb ‘are’ and the plural adjective ‘their’. Hence, the correct sentence is: “Indian forces are known for their loyalty and integrity.”

text: Brr, the city view from the Eiffel Tower is amazing !
explanation: An interjection is a word or phrase used to express a sudden feeling. ‘Brr’ is used to express the sensation of cold. ‘Wow’ is used to express a sudden feeling of amazement. Hence, ‘Wow’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Having known that / the train was already on the platform, / they ran fastly / to catch it.
options: the train was already on the platform
explanation: ‘Fast’ is already an adverb. The word ‘fastly’ does not exist. Hence, ‘they ran fast’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the option that spots the error in the use of preposition in the given sentence. Deepa and Seema are both good with running, but Deepa is also good at catching the ball and throwing it to the right corner in time.
explanation: Preposition ‘at’ is used to show that someone is good at doing something. ‘Good + at + Ving’ is the correct structure. Hence, ‘good at running’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: People admired him, for / he lived by the same principals / that he preached.
options: he lived by the same principals
explanation: ‘Principals’ must be replaced with ‘principles’ as the given sentence talks about a kind of belief or idea that guides you. Hence, ‘he lived by the same principles’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We were on the way/ to the party;/ suddenly, there/ will a heavy downpour.
explanation: The given sentence is in the past tense, not in the future tense, so it must have the verb in the past form ‘was’, . Hence, ‘was a heavy downpour’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He never talks / for anybody. / He is alone / all day.
explanation: ‘To’ is used to denote the person to whom someone is talking. Hence, ‘to anybody’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The police told the agitators to back in, else they would lathi-charge.
explanation: ‘Back out’ is the correct phrasal verb to use here. ‘Back out’ means to withdraw or decide not to do something that was planned to do. Hence, ‘the agitators to back out’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We took dinner in a Chinese restaurant and were amazed to see the interior of a restaurant.
explanation: Article ‘the’ is used when we refer to the same noun again because it becomes specific. Hence, ‘the interior of the restaurant’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mr. Ali’s shop / is further to / the hospital.
explanation: ‘Farther than’ will be used instead of ‘further to’. ‘Further’ is used for metaphorical distance where ‘farther’ is used for physical distance. The given sentence is talking about the physical distance between Mr. Ali’s shop and the hospital. Hence, ‘farther than’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the option that corrects the error in the given sentence. She sings good.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adverb(well) to modify the verb (sings) and not an adjective(good). Hence, ‘Rahul sings well’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In some countries, you are not able to drink until you are 21
explanation: The correct word to use here is ‘allowed’ instead of ‘able’. The given sentence states that you are not allowed to drink until you are 21. Hence, ‘allowed to drink’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Two of the world’s / best forwards / has played alongside / David Beckham.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a plural subject always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘Two of the world’s best forwards’ is a plural subject that will take ‘have’ as a plural verb. Hence, ‘have played alongside’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Ourselves should not boast of one’s knowledge.
explanation: ‘Ourselves’ must be replaced with 'We' as we use a subjective case pronoun (I/we/you) as the subject of a sentence. Hence, 'We' is the most appropriate answer.

text: He always wants to be in the company of those who are intellectually superior than him.
explanation: There are some words that imply comparison but do not take ‘than’. Rather, ‘to’ is used with them. For example:- superior to, inferior to, prior to, senior to, junior to, elder to, etc. Hence, ‘superior to him’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I have sing ‘Let It Go’ before a crowd of thousands of people.
explanation: With ‘has/have/had’, the third form of the verb is used. However, ‘sung’ is the third form of ‘sing’. Hence, 'I have sung' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mr. Suman / asked me / to pack / my luggages.
explanation: ‘Luggage’ is an uncountable noun, we cannot form its plural. Hence, ‘my luggage’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Camels tend to move slowly than other domestic animals in the plains.
explanation: We use comparative degree with ‘than’ to compare two persons, things or animals. The given sentence makes a comparison between the movement of camels and other domestic animals. ‘Slower’ will be used instead of ‘slowly’. Hence, ‘move slower’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Deepak is studying B.tech. at IIT Delhi to become the engineer.
explanation: Indefinite articles (a/an) are used when we refer to something in general. Article ‘an’ will be used here as the word ‘engineer’ begins with a vowel sound. Hence, ‘an engineer’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment in which the article has been used INCORRECTLY. Master Sam / is a heaviest / boy in / grade twelve.
explanation: ‘Heaviest’ is a superlative degree and we always place the definite article ‘the’ before any superlative degree. Hence, ‘is the heaviest’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Jerry driving / home late / when the incident / took place.
explanation: Helping verb is missing in this sentence. The given sentence is in the past tense, so it must have the helping ‘was’ denoting past continuous tense. Hence, ‘Jerry was driving’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The lions became violently / when the visitors / started throwing / stones at them.
explanation: ‘Became’ is a stative verb and we generally use an adjective after a stative verb. Therefore, 'violently' must be replaced with 'violent'. Hence, 'The lions became violent' is the most appropriate answer.

text: My dog / barks / very louder / at night.
explanation: ‘Louder’ must be replaced with 'loudly'. The given sentence needs an adverb to modify the verb ‘barks’, not the adjective ‘louder’. Hence, ‘very loudly’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The company specialises at / designing, crafting and manufacturing / exquisite, high-quality furniture / of exceptional craftsmanship.
explanation: ‘At’ must be replaced with ‘in’ we use ‘in’ to talk about skill, proficiency or specialisation in a field. Hence, ‘The company Pinnacle Spot the Error specialises in’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He and his friends / does not / want to / attend the meeting.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a plural subject always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘He and his friends’ is a plural subject that will take ‘do’ as a plural verb. Hence, ‘do not’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment in which the article has been used INCORRECTLY. In the recent past, the IT industry has emerged / as a major contributor to an industry revenue / as well as employment / opportunity provider in the country.
options: In the recent past, the IT industry has emerged
as a major contributor to an industry revenue
explanation: ‘Industry’ mentioned in the sentence is specific and we generally use the definite article ‘the’ with a specific or particular noun. Hence, ‘as a major contributor to the industry revenue’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: While I was walking to the store, my friend calls me and ask for a favour.
options: my friend calls me and ask
explanation: The given sentence is in the past tense, so it must have the verbs in the past form(V2). Hence, ‘my friend called(V2) me and asked(V2)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Please go and meet the chairperson. / She will be / away for the / few next days.
options: Please go and meet the chairperson.
explanation: The order of adjectives is wrong in this phrase. The correct order would be ‘next few days’. Hence, 'next few days' is the most appropriate answer.

text: The teacher asked him not to keep disturbing the class, but it had no affect.
explanation: ‘Affect’ must be replaced with ‘effect’ as we need a noun here to make the sentence meaningful. Hence, ‘but it had no effect’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This is the book whom I wanted to buy.
explanation: ‘Whom’ must be replaced with ‘which’. ‘Whom’ is used for a person whereas ‘which’ is used for things(book). Hence, ‘which I’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My colleague always works latest than me.
explanation: We use a comparative degree with ‘than’ to make a comparison between two things. ‘Later’ is the correct comparative degree of ‘late’. Hence, ‘later’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He was / bad injured / in the / last match.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adverb ‘badly’ to modify the adjective ‘injured’, not the adjective ‘bad’. Hence, ‘badly injured’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My sister and I / work very hard / nevertheless my brother does not do / any task assigned to him.
options: nevertheless my brother does not do
explanation: ‘Nevertheless’ must be replaced with ‘but’ as we generally use ‘but’ when two statements differ from or contrast with each other. There is a contrast between working hard and not doing any task. Hence, ‘but my brother does not do’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The couple /preferred to walk / until the last house / of the town.
explanation: ‘Until’ must be replaced by ‘to’ because when referring to a destination or endpoint, ‘to’ is used. Hence, ‘to the last house’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Ramayana is an ancient Sanskrit epic; it is believed to be written around 500 BC to 100 BC.
explanation: The definite article 'the' is used before holy books. For example:- The Ramayana, The Mahabharata, The Quran, The Bible, etc. Hence, 'The Ramayana is an ancient' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Hard had she /thrown the basketball /when it fell /on the ground.
explanation: ‘Hardly…when’ is a fixed pair of conjunctions. Hence, ‘Hardly had she’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The project was completed / more quicker / than expected
explanation: We don’t use ‘more or very’ with the comparative degree because it becomes a case of superfluousness (not necessary). ‘More’ will be removed from the given sentence . Hence ‘quicker’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The following sentence has an error in its tense. Identify the error and select the correct sentence from the options. If you had apprised me about your problem earlier, I would have allow you to go.
options: If you apprised me about your problem earlier, I would have allowed you to go.
If you can apprise me about your problem earlier, I would have allowed you to go.
If you had apprised me about your problem earlier, I would have allowed you to go.
If you had apprised me about your problem earlier, I would allow you to go.
explanation: would have allowed you to go. The given sentence is an example of a third conditional sentence and the correct grammatical structure for it is “If + past perfect (had + V3)…….. Would have + V3”. Hence, ‘would have allowed (V3)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: There is an error in the given sentence. From the options given, identify the sentence that corrects the error to make it a grammatically accurate sentence. Harmit is not innocent such as Uday.
options: Harmit is not as innocent as Uday.
Harmit is not as innocent more than Uday.
Harmit is not as much as innocent as Uday.
Harmit is not innocent than Uday.
explanation: "As...as" is a comparative structure used to compare two things. The given sentence is comparing Harmit with Uday. Hence, option (a) is the most appropriate answer.

text: When it / come to football, / my brother is / an addict.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. At the end of a singular verb, s/es is used. In the given sentence, ‘it’ is a singular subject that will take ‘comes’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘comes to football’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Throw of / the old shoes; / nobody will wear / them now.
explanation: ‘Throw off’ is the correct phrasal verb to use here. ‘Throw off’ means to rid oneself of something. The given sentence talks about getting rid of the old shoes. Hence, ‘Throw off’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: They have decided / to wind out / their business / without delay.
explanation: ‘To wind out’ must be replaced with ‘to wind up’. ‘Wind up’ means to close or conclude a business. Hence ‘to wind up’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Since the little girl answers / a few simple questions, / her parents say that / she is too intelligent.
explanation: ‘Too’ must be replaced with ‘very’. ‘Too’ is used in a sentence with a negative sense. Hence ‘she is very intelligent’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It is difficult to live in / the societal expectations / when one has / fewer resources. A B C D
explanation: ‘Live in’ must be replaced by ‘Live up to’. ‘Live up to’ means to meet or match the expectations set by someone or something. Hence ‘It is difficult to live up to’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The teacher was / taken back by / the audacity of / the new student. A B C D
explanation: ‘Taken back by’ must be replaced with ‘taken aback by’. The phrase ‘to be taken aback’ means to be very shocked or surprised. The given sentence states that the teacher was shocked by the audacity of the new student. Hence, ‘taken aback by’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: His mother’s transfer from a small town to Delhi brought up a huge change in his schooling.
options: from a small town to Delhi
explanation: ‘Brought up’ must be replaced with ‘brought about’. The phrasal verb ‘brought about’ is the past form of ‘bring about’, which means to cause something to happen. The given sentence talks about the huge change that happened due to his mother’s transfer. Hence, ‘brought about a huge change’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mrs. Meera and family / received his letter / a week ago
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Identify the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the given options. Petrified wood is type of fossilised wood that exhibits the original details of the wood
options: The petrified wood is the type of fossilised wood that exhibits a original details of the wood
A petrified wood is type of fossilised wood that exhibits an original details of the wood.
Petrified wood is a type of fossilised wood that exhibits the original details of the wood.
Petrified wood is the type of fossilised wood that exhibits a original details of the wood
explanation: exhibits the original details of the wood. There is an error of article in the given sentence. The ‘type’ mentioned in the given sentence is not specific and we generally use the indefinite article ‘a’ before a non-specific noun. Therefore, ‘a type of fossilied fuel’ is the corrected part. Hence, the sentence given in option (c) is the most appropriate answer.

text: (1) When Christy (2) grew out, (3) he turned out (4) to be a gentleman.
explanation: ‘Grew out’ must be replaced with ‘grew up’ which means to mature or become an adult. The given sentence talks about Christy becoming an adult. Hence, ‘grew up’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The meeting / will taking / place next / Wednesday.
explanation: ‘Modal verbs’ are auxiliary verbs(also called helping verbs) like can, will, could, shall, must, would, might, and should. However, after a modal verb, we generally use the first form of the verb (V1). Hence ‘will take(V1)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Rashmi was / quite amusing when / she heard about / what had happened.
explanation: The given sentence needs a past participle ‘amused’ as it is in the passive voice. Rashmi was amused by what she heard. Hence, ‘quite amused when’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an INCORRECT preposition. Please remember to take / your notice to the reception area / if you want it to be displayed / upon the bulletin board.
options: if you want it to be displayed
your notice to the reception area
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the sentence . ‘Upon’ must be replaced with ‘On’ . We use ‘on’ when an object is in contact with the surface of something. Similarly, the notice will be in contact with the bulletin board. Hence ‘on the bulletin board’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Today she said to her friend, “You’re the sweetest person I have met ever”.
explanation: ‘Ever’ is an adverb of frequency. An adverb of frequency is generally placed before the main verb and after the helping verb. Therefore, ‘ever’ will be placed before the main verb ‘met’. Hence ‘I have ever met’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The class / teacher was / wounded in / a leg.
explanation: ‘Leg’ mentioned in the given sentence is specific and we generally use the definite article ‘the’ before any specific or particular noun. Hence, ‘in the leg’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I had seen / her with her mother / in the cinema hall / yesterday.
explanation: ‘Had seen’ must be replaced with 'saw'. We generally use ‘simple past tense(V2)’ to describe actions, events, or states that occurred and were completed in the past. Similarly, in the sentence, the action was completed yesterday. Hence, ‘I saw’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mr. Narayanan / is a rather / lazy man.
explanation: Pinnacle Spot the Error The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: My students are / waiting for / their flights / at the gate no. 6.
explanation: Use of definite article ‘the’ is incorrect. We generally do not use definite article ‘the’ when referring to specific numbered gates, rooms or sections. Hence ‘at gate no. 6’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. She will being studying for her exams tomorrow.
explanation: ‘Will be + V-ing’ is the correct grammatical structure for the sentence which is in the future continuous tense. Hence, ‘will be’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an INCORRECT preposition. I am writing to invite you / to give a presentation / for our Jobs and Careers Conference / for engineering graduates.
options: I am writing to invite you
for our Jobs and Careers Conference
explanation: Preposition ‘at’ is used to indicate a specific occasion or event. Similarly, in the given sentence, ‘Jobs and Careers Conference’ is a specific event. Hence, ‘at our jobs and careers conference’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The companies were / giving in the prizes / to attract customers / during the festive season.
explanation: ‘Giving in’ must be replaced with ‘giving out’ . The phrasal verb ‘giving out’ means to distribute or handing over something. While ‘giving in’ means to surrender. The given sentence talks about distributing the prizes. Hence ‘giving out the prizes’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This artwork / are a wonderful example / of the period's vogue / for realistic style.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘This artwork’ is a singular subject that will take ‘is’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘is a wonderful example’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Identify the error in the following sentence and select the option with the correct use of the phrasal verb. Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he blacked out.
options: Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he broke in.
Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he chickened out.
Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he checked out.
Prateek was planning to ask Shreya for a favour. But he could not muster up the courage. So, he turned down.
explanation: he could not muster up the courage. So, he chickened out. ‘Blacked out’ must be replaced with ‘chickened out’. The phrasal verb ‘chickened out’ means to fail to do something due to fear. While ‘blacked out’ means to lose consciousness. Hence ‘chickened out’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She was singing / beautifully in / the concert hall / last night.
explanation: The word ‘last’ indicates the use of simple past tense(V2). Therefore, ‘was singing’ will be replaced with ‘sang’. Hence, ‘She sang(V2)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Identify the error in the following sentence and select the option with the correct use of the phrasal verb. The police inspector was trying to give out the contradicting stories in the scene of the accident.
options: The police inspector was trying to lighten up the Pinnacle Spot the Error contradicting stories in the scene of the accident.
The police inspector was trying to sign up the contradicting stories in the scene of the accident.
The police inspector was trying to sort out the contradicting stories in the scene of the accident.
The police inspector was trying to rush out the contradicting stories in the scene of the accident.
explanation: contradicting stories in the scene of the accident. The phrasal verb ‘sort out’ means to understand something such as a reason or solution by thinking. The given sentence talks about understanding the contradictory stories. Hence, the sentence given in option (c) uses the correct phrasal verb.

text: The aeroplane took down / without the passengers after / making a sudden announcement.
explanation: ‘Took down’ must be replaced with ‘took off’. ‘Took off’ means to begin flight. While ‘took down’ means to defeat someone. The given sentence talks about the flight of the aeroplane. Hence ‘The aeroplane took off’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Emily is a American living in Paris for her work.
explanation: Article ‘A’ is used before the words starting with a consonant sound - (a conversation, a story). Whereas, the article ‘An’ is used before the words starting with a vowel sound(an imminent danger, an apple). Hence, ‘an American’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This is / a doll / and there is / a umbrella.
explanation: Article ‘A’ is used before the words starting from a consonant sound - (a conversation, a story). Whereas, the article ‘An’ is used before the words starting from a vowel sound(an imminent danger, an apple). Hence, ‘an umbrella’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Even in cold weather, the reliable car always started on the first try.
The soldiers / were selected / on the section / of ‘gallantry of spirits’.
explanation: Use of the word ‘section’ is incorrect here. Rather, we will use the word ‘basis’ to make the sentence meaningful. ‘Basis’ means a particular condition that is used as a reference. Hence, ‘on the basis’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a spelling error. The make-up room was filled / with incadescent lights / which added to the misery / of those subjected to make-up.
explanation: ‘Incandescent’ is the correct spelling.

text: If she exercises daily, / she would / remain energetic / and fit forever.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of the first conditional sentence and the correct grammatical structure is “if + simple present…….will +V1”. Hence ‘she will’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: A owl is a bird which has wide eyes, asymmetrical ears and is found mostly in forests.
options: and is found mostly in forests.
explanation: Article ‘A’ is used before the words starting from a consonant sound - (a conversation, a story). Whereas, the article ‘An’ is used before the words starting from a vowel sound(an imminent danger, an apple). In the given sentence, the word ‘owl’ starts with a vowel sound. Hence, ‘An owl is a bird’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I am going /to buy a red car/ with a leather seats/ and a sunroof.
explanation: Article ‘a’ must be removed as ‘seats’ is a plural noun. Hence, ‘with leather seats’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mrs. Arunima / speaks / Telugu well.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: That day we reached late for the competition and even though the competition went on smooth, I felt bad about Shivani losing it.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adverb(smoothly) to modify the verb ‘went on’, not the adjective ‘smooth’. Hence, ‘the competition went on smoothly’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: During winters, most of the trains are not running on time in North India.
explanation: Simple Present Tense will be used in the given sentence as it is used to state a habitual or repeated action. ‘Plural subject + do not + V1’ is the correct structure for it. Hence, ‘do not run(V1)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In this cold weather, / there’s nothing / like good / cup of coffee.
explanation: We generally use indefinite articles with singular countable nouns. In the given sentence, article ‘a’ will be used before the adjective ‘good’ for the singular noun ‘cup’. Hence ‘like a good’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: There’s an quiet street down the left that you can use for your dance practice.
explanation: Article ‘an’ must be replaced with ‘a’. We use article ‘a’ before words starting with a consonant sound (ship , car, train). In the given sentence, the word ‘quiet’ starts with a consonant sound. Hence, ‘There’s a quiet street’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: A part / of an / apple is / rotten
explanation: Article ‘an’ must be replaced with ‘the’ as we generally use the definite article ‘the’ before any specific or particular noun. The given sentence is talking about a particular apple. Hence, ‘of the’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: How long are you working / for your current employer / and why don’t you / look for better opportunities?
explanation: ‘How long are you working’ must be replaced with ‘How long Pinnacle Spot the Error have you been working’ as we use present perfect continuous tense to talk about the duration of an action that started in the past and is still ongoing. Hence, ‘how long have you been working’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The judges eliminated the / classical singer, as she dropped of / in the middle of the competition.
options: in the middle of the competition.
classical singer, as she dropped of
explanation: ‘Dropped of’ must be replaced with ‘dropped out’. ‘Dropped out’ is a phrasal verb which means to quit or leave something before completion. Hence, ‘classical singer, as she dropped out’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In geography class,/ the teacher told the students, / "Switzerland lies / inside Germany, France, Austria, and Italy."
options: inside Germany, France, Austria, and Italy
explanation: There is a preposition error in this sentence. ‘Between’ is used for geographical location. The given sentence talks about the geographical location of Switzerland. Hence, ‘between Germany, France, Austria, and Italy’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: ‘You expressed your opinion/ very clearly /but I am sorry/ I cannot agree to you’.
explanation: ‘With’ is used after ‘agree’ in the case of a person. Hence, ‘I cannot agree with you’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Identify the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the given options. This is the story of eight round planets, the few rocks in between, and some comets.
options: This is story of eight round planets, few rocks in between, and some comets.
This is the story of eight round planets, few rocks in between, Pinnacle Spot the Error and some comets.
This is the story of eight round planets, a few rocks in between, and some comets.
This is a story of eight round planets, few rocks in between, and some comets.
explanation: in between, and some comets. ‘The few’ must be replaced with ‘a few’. ‘The few’ is used for something specific or particular. But the rocks are not specific. Hence, ‘a few rocks’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Our plane / arrived at / the Mumbai airport / at the right time.
explanation: Article ‘the' will be removed as we generally do not use any article before proper nouns. Hence, 'Mumbai airport' is the most appropriate answer.

text: The workers called out / the strike because / the management acceded to / all their demands.
explanation: ‘Called off’ is the correct phrasal verb to use here. ‘Called off’ means to cancel an event or agreement. Similarly, the workers cancelled the strike. Hence, ‘The workers called off’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The given sentence is divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a spelling error. When the famous businessman / faced a huge loss / in his business, / no one expressed simpathy.
explanation: ‘Sympathy’ is the correct spelling.

text: A great / culture of hospitality of / the Spanish / is well - known.
explanation: The ‘culture’ mentioned in the given sentence is specific and we generally use the definite article ‘the’ before any specific or particular noun. Hence, ‘The great culture’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The volunteer gave on to / the food packets to the / children of the orphanage.
explanation: The phrase ‘gave on to’ must be replaced with the phrasal verb ‘gave out’ which means to distribute something among a number of people. The given sentence talks about the distribution of food packets. Hence, ‘The volunteer gave out’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It was my niece / who was leaving college / last year, and / not my son.
explanation: The word ‘last year’ indicates the use of simple past tense. ‘Left’ is the past form(V2) of ‘leave’. Hence, ‘who left (V2) college’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Since childhood, Monty / ate his food / fast and he / will not change.
explanation: Monty will not change. This means Monty has been eating his food fast and he will keep eating. Therefore, the first part of the sentence will be written in present perfect continuous tense. ‘Monty’ is a singular subject that will take ‘has been’ as a singular helping verb. Hence, ‘has been eating his food’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It is sad / that you / are believing / in superstitious rituals.
explanation: Stative verbs are those verbs which express a state or condition. They do not refer to a physical action. Sense and emotions like hear, smell, see, love, hate etc are different types of stative verbs. Verbs denoting thoughts and opinions include know, believe, think, understand, consider, etc. However, these verbs can’t be used in (-ing form) for example, Hear, Smell (Correct) and Hearing, Smelling (Incorrect). Hence, ‘you believe’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: After your insistence, / my sister / checked / a mailbox again.
explanation: ‘Mailbox’ mentioned in the given sentence is specific and we generally use the definite article ‘the’ before any specific or particular noun. Hence, ‘the mailbox again’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In order to connect / these themes to a wider / historical context, Rahul go / beyond aesthetic analysis.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘Rahul’ is a singular subject that will take ‘goes’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘historical context, Rahul goes’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mathematics help/ in developing/ the logical mindset /of students.
explanation: statics, physics) seem plural but they are actually singular forms. According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, singular subject takes singular verb. Hence, ‘helps’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The chief guest gave out prizes to the meritorious students of the school.
explanation: ‘Gave out’ must be replaced with ‘gave away’. The phrasal verb ‘give away’ means to give something away as a gift. The given sentence talks about giving away gifts. Hence, ‘gave away prizes’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the option with the correct use of article
options: William Wordsworth was a romantic poet. He did things in an unusual manner.
William Wordsworth was a romantic poet. He did things in a unusual manner.
William Wordsworth was the romantic poet. He did things in a unusual manner.
William Wordsworth was romantic poet. He did things in an unusual manner.
explanation: things in an unusual manner. Article ‘A’ is used before the words starting from a consonant sound - (a conversation, a story). Whereas, the article ‘An’ is used before the words starting from a vowel sound (an imminent danger, an apple). The word ‘romantic’ starts with a consonant sound and the word ‘unusual’ begins with a vowel sound. Hence, the sentence given in option (a) correctly uses the articles.

text: She was fond of walking along the path besides the lake.
explanation: ‘Besides’ must be replaced by ‘beside’. ‘Beside’ means at the side of something while ‘besides’ means in addition to or apart from. Hence, ‘beside the lake’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Father took the newspaper / in his hand to/go through it once again.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Policeman came to my village and asked about a person who burgled a house last night.
explanation: Article ‘a’ must be used before the noun ‘policeman’ as it is singular and begins with a consonant sound. Hence, ‘A policeman’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It is his job / to chase out / clients with / outstanding debts.
explanation: ‘Chase out’ must be replaced with ‘chase down’. The phrasal verb ‘chase down’ means to follow and catch someone. The given sentence states that it is his job to chase down clients with outstanding debts. Hence, ‘to chase down’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My Vice-Chancellor works / eighteen hours / a day, / seven days week.
explanation: Article ‘a’ is used to indicate the frequency of an action. The frequency of the action means how many days in a week. Hence, ‘seven days a week’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It was possible to achieve anything, / if one has the grit and determination / to keep going.
options: It was possible to achieve anything,
if one has the grit and determination
explanation: The given sentence is in the simple present tense so the verb must be used in the present form. ‘It‘ is a singular subject that will take the singular verb ‘is’. Hence, ‘it is possible’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The manager asked / the cooking team, “Who / among you is to baked the / Christmas cake this year?”
options: among you is to baked the
explanation: ‘To + V1’ is the grammatically correct structure. Hence, ‘among you is to bake (V1)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We were grateful for a book they gave us.
explanation: ‘Book’ mentioned in the given sentence is specific and we generally use the definite article ‘the’ before specific or particular nouns. Hence, 'the book' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Can we go visit a Statue of Liberty on our trip to the United States ?
explanation: ‘Statue of Liberty’ is a historical monument and we generally use the definite article ‘the’ before the names of historical monuments. Hence, ‘visit the Statue of Liberty’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I am understanding;/ you like her/ because she has /a generous nature.
explanation: ‘Understand’ is a stative verb and stative verbs are generally not written in continuous tense. Rather, simple present tense will be used here. The first form of the verb is used in the simple present tense with ‘I’. Hence, ‘I understand(V1)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Three segments of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the option that contains the error. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer. Since his son has not yet completed the age of eighteen, he was reluctant to fulfil his son's demand of getting a motorbike.
explanation: The given sentence is in the present tense, therefore the present form of the verb will be used here. ‘Was’ must be replaced with ‘is’. Hence, ‘he is reluctant’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: When he resigned, / the company offered him / a huge sum of money but / he refused to agree to it.
options: he refused to agree to it.
a huge sum of money but
explanation: The use of the verb ‘agree’ after ‘refused’ is superfluous. ‘Refuse’ means to not agree to accept something. The phrase ‘to agree to it’ must be replaced with ‘offer’. Hence, ‘he refused the offer’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an adverbial usage error. Mrs. Gomathi was / that tired and weak / that she could / scarcely walk.
explanation: Use of ‘that’ with ‘that’ is incorrect here. ‘So…that’ is the correct conjunction pair. Hence, ‘so tired and weak’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The following sentence has an error in its tense. Identify the error and select the correct sentence from the given options. I will be arrange all the necessary materials for the programme.
options: I is arrange all the necessary materials for the programme.
I was arrange all the necessary materials for the programme.
I would arranging all the necessary materials for the programme.
I will be arranging all the necessary materials for the programme.
explanation: programme. The given sentence is an example of ‘Future continuous Tense’ and follows the structure, “Will/shall + be + Ving”. Hence, the sentence given in option (d) is correct.

text: We were driving home when suddenly a deer runs across the road.
options: a deer runs across the road
explanation: The given sentence is in the past tense, therefore, the past form(V2) of the verb will be used. Hence, ‘a deer ran (V2) across the road’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate option that rectifies the error
options: in the following sentence. One must do his/her duty proparly.
One must do once duty proparly.
One must do ones duty properly.
One must do one’s duti proprly.
One must do one's duty properly
explanation: One’s is the correct possessive used for the pronoun ‘one’. Hence, the sentence given in option (d) is correct.

text: His energetic attitude / showed that he had / soundly slept / the previous night.
explanation: ‘Soundly slept’ must be replaced with ‘slept soundly’ as the adverb (soundly) will be used after the verb ‘slept’. Hence, ‘slept soundly’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It is a cheap reasonably / restaurant in this part of the town / where you can eat / delicious food.
options: restaurant in this part of the town
explanation: ‘Reasonably’ is an adverb which modifies the adjective ‘cheap’ and the adverb is generally used before the adjective. Hence, ‘It is a reasonably cheap’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mr. Vinu / has never / slept in / a igloo.
explanation: Article ‘an’ is used before the words beginning with a vowel sound (an apple, an umbrella, an MBA). Similarly, in the given sentence, the word ‘igloo’ begins with a vowel sound. Hence, ‘an igloo’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. The art historian argued that the painting's value has been greatly underestimated, and that its unique style and technique deserved recognition from the art community and the public alike.
explanation: The given sentence is in the past tense, so the helping verb of past perfect tense (had) will be used in place of ‘has’. Hence, ‘had been greatly underestimated’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My neighbours were serious injured in the car accident.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adverb ‘seriously’ to modify the verb (injured), not the adjective ‘serious’. Hence, ‘seriously injured’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I am working with him since 2002, / but even today / I am unable / to understand his motives.
options: I am working with him since 2002,
explanation: Present perfect continuous tense is used with ‘for/since’ to indicate the duration or starting point of an action. ‘I + have been + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure for this sentence. Hence, ‘I have been working with him since 2002’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Ms. Malathi is living lonely in an apartment.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adverb ‘lonely’ to modify the verb ‘lives’, not the adjective ‘lonely’. Hence, ‘alone in’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: By the time I reaching / the metro station, / the train had departed.
explanation: If two actions happened in the past, 1st action is written in past perfect tense(had + V3) and 2nd action is written in simple past tense(V2). In the given sentence, reaching the metro station is the 2nd action. Hence, ‘By the time I reached(V2)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mr. Thomas / is going / to buy / horse.
explanation: We generally use an indefinite article before a singular noun. Article ‘a’ will be used before ‘horse’ as it begins with a consonant sound. Hence, ‘a horse’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My father is comparatively better today.
explanation: ‘Better’ is the comparative degree of ‘good’. The use of ‘comparatively’ with ‘better’ is superfluous, so it will be removed. Hence, ‘better’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If I have recovered from fever, / I will start going / for swimming classes / from tomorrow.
options: If I have recovered from fever
explanation: The given sentence is an example of the first conditional sentence and ‘If + Simple present … will + V1’ is the correct grammatical structure for it. Hence, ‘If I recover from fever’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Last night I dreamed that / I am looking for the/ abominable snowman high / up in the Himalayas.
explanation: The given sentence is in the past tense, therefore, ‘am’ will be replaced with ‘was’ to indicate past continuous tense. Hence, ‘I was looking for the’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Three segments of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the option that contains the error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. When my father will come, I will make sure that I discuss the possibilities of a new business venture with him.
explanation: ‘When’ is used to introduce a time clause, which is not written in the future tense. Rather, simple present tense is used to indicate the time of the main event. Hence, ‘When my father comes’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Soldiers in / the Indian Armed Forces are / trained never to / fight cowardly.
explanation: The position of ‘never’ is incorrect in this sentence. Here, ‘never’ is used to modify the infinitive ‘to fight’, therefore it will be used between ‘to’ and ‘fight’. Hence, ‘trained to never’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the incorrect form of the verb.
explanation: ‘Stricken’ is the correct verb form.

text: Identify the error in the verb form in the following sentence and choose the correct sentence from the given options (Present Tense). The committee work diligently to ensure fair and unbiased decision.
options: The committee is work diligently to ensure fair and unbiased decision.
The committee worked diligently to ensure fair and unbiased decision.
The committee has work diligently to ensure fair and unbiased decision.
The committee works diligently to ensure fair and unbiased decision.
explanation: unbiased decision. The given sentence is an example of simple present tense and follows the structure, ‘Singular subject + V-s/es’. Hence, option (d) is the most appropriate answer.

text: The people of / Jammu and Kashmir / has emphasised and / appreciated transparency.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘people’ is a plural subject that will take ‘have’ as a plural verb. Hence, ‘have emphasized and’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Himalayas include the highest mountains in the world and feed almost 20% of the earth’s population.
explanation: Article ‘the’ is used before mountain ranges. ‘Himalayas’ is a mountain range. Hence, ‘The Himalayas include the’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an adverbial usage error. Mr. Sukesh and / his family / ate the / food greedy.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adverb ‘greedily’ to modify the verb ‘ate’, not the adjective ‘greedy’. Hence, ‘food greedily’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Ramesh licked
explanation: ‘Taste’ is a stative verb and we generally use an adjective with stative verbs. For example:- tastes sweet, smells nice, looks great, etc. Therefore, the adverb ‘sweetly’ will be replaced with the adjective ‘sweet’. Hence, ‘it tasted sweet’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mrs. Rani / works for / a international / school.
explanation: Article ‘an’ is used before the words beginning with a vowel sound (an apple, an umbrella, an American). Similarly, in the given sentence, the word ‘international’ begins with a vowel sound. Hence, ‘an international’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: I will be driving into town later on.
I might drive into town later on.
I could be driving into town later on.
I will be drive into town later on.
explanation: ‘Will be + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure for the sentence which is in the future continuous tense. ‘Drive’ must be replaced with 'driving'. Hence, the sentence given in option (d) has an error.

text: Most of the committee / are here to / decide the fate of / this ancient building.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘Most of the committee’ is a singular subject that will take ‘is’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘is here to’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: When Ramu was working / as a clerk, / he asked me money.
explanation: ‘Asked me money’ must be replaced with ‘asked me for money’. The phrasal verb ‘ask for’ means to try to obtain something by requesting. Similarly, Ramu tried to obtain some money by requesting. Hence, ‘he asked me for money’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Identify the proper explanation of the error in the given sentence. Mohan insisted to go there.
options: Error is in the sentence formation. Preposition and gerund are required. The correct sentence should read like this: Mohan insisted on going there.
Error is with the verb. The correct sentence should read like this: Mohan insist to going there.
Error is with the tense. The correct sentence should read like this: Mohan insisting to go there.
Error is with the preposition. The correct sentence should read like this: Mohan insisted go there.
explanation: gerund are required. The correct sentence should read like this: Mohan insisted on going there.

text: There are four tributaries of Ganga and it is ranked as the fifth most polluted river of the world.
options: most polluted river of the world.
explanation: ‘Ganga’ is a river and we generally use the definite article ‘the’ before the names of rivers. Hence, ‘of the Ganga and it’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The sons of the old farmer / fell off after their father / breathed his last / in the village.
options: The sons of the old farmer
explanation: ‘Fell off’ must be replaced with ‘fell apart’. The phrasal verb ‘fall apart’ means to become separated. The given passage talks about separation of the sons. Hence, ‘fell apart after their father’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I had done / my cooking when / Vishnu came to see me.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Had you been / working regularly, / you had completed / the project yesterday.
explanation: ‘Would have’ is used to indicate the result of a past unreal condition. In the given sentence, ‘working regularly’ is the past unreal condition and ‘completing the project’ is its result. Hence, ‘you would have completed’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Raveena has made / up her mind to / carried minimum / luggage with her.
explanation: ‘To + V1’, also known as infinitive, is the correct grammatical structure. Hence, ‘carry(V1) minimum’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: For the past / three years, / my uncle is /away from home
explanation: ‘My uncle is’ must be replaced with ‘my uncle has been’. Present perfect tense (Singular Sub. + has + V3) is used to indicate a state that has existed for some time. Hence, ‘my uncle has been(V3)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mr. Raghav / brushes his / teeth four / times the day
explanation: Article ‘a’ is used to indicate the frequency of an action. For example:- twice a day, four times a day, etc. Hence, ‘times a day’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mr. Prabhakar was first man to arrive at the venue.
explanation: The article “the” is used before adjectives denoting rank, order or position. Therefore, article ‘the’ will be used before ‘first’. Hence, ‘was the first man’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Although there is no proven data, the Centre for Policy Research estimate that India has the largest stock of iron ore in the world.
options: Although there is no proven data,
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always Pinnacle Spot the Error takes a plural verb. At the end of a singular verb, s/es is used. In the given sentence, ‘Centre for Policy Research’ is a singular subject that will take ‘estimates’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘Centre for Policy Research estimates’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He has been (1) watered the plants (2) for one hour. (3) No error
explanation: ‘Watered’ must be replaced with ‘watering’ as ‘Singular Sub + has been + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure for the sentence which is in present perfect continuous tense. The subject ‘he’ is singular. Hence, ‘watering the plants’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The toast was raised in honour of the chairman yesterday at hall.
explanation: ‘Hall’ given in the sentence is specific and we use the definite article ‘the’ before specific or particular nouns. Hence, ‘yesterday at the hall’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Identify the error in the verb form in the following sentence and choose the correct sentence from the given options (Present Tense). Earth revolve around the sun.
options: Earth has revolve around the sun.
Earth are revolve around the sun.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb. At the end of a singular verb, s/es is used. In the given sentence, ‘Earth’ is a singular subject that will take ‘revolves’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘Earth revolves around the sun.’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Hiking across an Himalayas is going to be a tough task for a beginner.
explanation: ‘Himalayas’ is a mountain range and we use the definite article ‘the’ before mountain ranges. Hence, ‘the Himalayas is’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Children should watch TV from distance as it will affect their eyesight.
explanation: We use simple present tense to state a scientific fact. It is a scientific fact that TV affects eyesight. Therefore, ‘will’ must be removed and the singular verb ‘affects’ will be used for the singular subject ‘it’. Hence, ‘as it affects’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My friends / and their family members / have gone to the beach / two days ago.
explanation: The given sentence is in the past tense, so it must have the verb in the past form (V2). ‘Went’ is the past form. Hence, ‘went to the beach’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: By the time she retires, / she has been teaching / at the university for 30 years.
explanation: The future perfect tense is used to express an action that will be completed before another point in the future. The correct structure for future tense is ‘By the time + Simple present tense, … Future perfect tense’. Hence, ‘she will have taught’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Can we make sure we have a lots of fun on the trip?
explanation: The correct phrase is ‘a lot of’. Its plural form is ‘lots of’. Therefore, ‘lot’ will be used in place of ‘lots’. Hence, ‘a lot of’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Paul and I played tennis yesterday. He’s much better than me, so he win easily.
