explanation: The given sentence is in the past tense, so it must have the verbs in the past form(V2), not in the present form(V1). Therefore, ‘won’ will be used in place of ‘win’. Hence, ‘so he won(V2) easily’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: King Solomon of Israel is said to be one of a wisest man who ruled the earth.
explanation: ‘One of + the + superlative adjective + plural noun’ is the correct grammatical structure. Therefore, article ‘the’ will be used in place of article ‘a’ and the plural noun ‘men’ will be used in place of ‘man’. Hence, ‘of the wisest men’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He was consulted seldom by his colleagues while making important decisions on financial matters.
explanation: An adverb of frequency is generally placed after the helping verb and before the main verb in a sentence. Examples are :- often, always, seldom, never, etc. Therefore, ‘seldom’ will be placed after the helping verb ‘was’. Hence, ‘He was seldom consulted’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The Prime Minister and a President are visiting the town day to see the preparations of International Seminar.
options: the town day to see the
explanation: ‘President’ is a specific person and we always use the definite article ‘the’ before specific or particular nouns. Hence, ‘the President are visiting’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The following sentence may have an error of article. Choose the correct sentence from the given options. Choose ‘No error’ if the sentence has no error. The festivals are celebrated everywhere to rejuvenate the minds of people
options: An festivals are celebrated everywhere to rejuvenate the minds of people
Festivals are celebrated everywhere to rejuvenate the minds of people.
The festivals are celebrated everywhere to rejuvenate minds of people.
explanation: minds of people. We do not use any article when we refer to something in general. Therefore, article ‘the’ will be removed before the noun ‘festival’ as the given sentence is stating a general truth about festivals. Hence, the sentence given in option (c) has the correct use of article.

text: Identify the INCORRECT section of the given sentence. Four people / were / witnesses of / that event.
explanation: The preposition ‘to’ is used after the nouns ‘witness’ or ‘testimony’. And the correct structure is ‘witness/testimony to an event’. Hence, ‘witnesses to’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We have to be cautius regarding the impact of global warming.
explanation: ‘Cautious’ is the correct spelling.

text: Due to its fragrance, the petals of an rose are often used in perfumes and cosmetics.
explanation: Article ‘a’ is used before words beginning with the consonant sound. For example:- a conversation, a story. Similarly, in the given sentence, the word ‘rose’ begins with a consonant sound. Hence, ‘the petals of a rose’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She is enough wise not to interfere in their matter, once being insulted publicly by them.
explanation: The adverb ‘enough’ is always used after the adjective. Similarly, in the given sentence, ‘enough’ will be used after the adjective ‘wise’. Hence, ‘She is wise enough’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Generally, a cycle has an seat and handle along with two pedals and a bell, sometimes a carrier too.
options: a bell, sometimes a carrier too.
explanation: Article ‘a’ is used before words beginning with consonant sound. For example:- a car, a man, a cycle, etc. Similarly, in the given sentence, the word ‘seat’ begins with a consonant sound. Hence, ‘Generally, a cycle has a seat’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Netaji, a hero of Modern India, is remembered for his contribution in the establishment of Indian Army.
explanation: Article ‘the’ is used before the title given to an important personality. ‘Hero of Modern India’ is a title given to ‘Netaji’. Hence, ‘Netaji, the Hero of Modern’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Sincere students / like you and he should study / regularly to pass the examination.
options: like you and he should study
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: While astrology has/ a long history / it is generally/ considered pseudoscience.
explanation: The ‘pseudoscience’ mentioned in the given sentence is not specific and we generally use the indefinite article ‘a’ before a non-specific noun. Hence, ‘considered a pseudoscience’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I have three sisters: / Meera is the elder / and Charu is the youngest.
explanation: ‘Elder’ must be replaced with ‘eldest’. The definite article ‘the’ is used before a superlative degree. Hence, ‘Meera is the eldest’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: A man who has been accused of fraud / in an earlier job, he will never be / welcome in any other organisation.
options: A man who has been accused of fraud
in an earlier job, he will never be
explanation: ‘A man’ is already mentioned as a subject of this sentence. We cannot use ‘he’ in the sentence as it becomes the case of superfluousness(not necessary). Therefore, ‘he’ must be removed from the sentence. Hence, ‘in an earlier job, will never be’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It is a well-known fact/ that the Monarchy is / not the best form /of governance.
explanation: Article ‘the’ must be removed. No article is used before the forms of government such as democracy, plutocracy, dictatorship, monarchy. Hence, ‘that Monarchy is’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Specialists say that this method speeds up language learning tremendously.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Two elderly gentlemen told the rather improbable story to mislead the police personnel.
explanation: ‘The’ must be replaced with ‘a’. Article ‘the’ is used for specific or particular nouns but the ‘story’ mentioned in the sentence is not specific. Hence, ‘told a rather improbable’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We cannot postpone discussion on this issue although it is urgent.
explanation: ‘Although’ must be replaced with ‘as / because’. The issue is urgent, that is why discussion on it can not be postponed. Here, we need a connector to show the cause or reason. Hence, ‘because it is urgent’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Are you yet afraid of going out in the dark?
explanation: ‘Yet’ must be replaced with ‘still’. ‘Yet’ is used to show contrast between two events. ‘Still’ is used to show that an action was happening in the past and continuing in the present. Hence, ‘Are you still’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Rohit Sharma’s century was very acclaimed in the media.
explanation: ‘Very’ must be replaced with ‘much’. ‘Very’ is used with present participles(Ving), not with past participles(V3). Hence, ‘much acclaimed’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: You can take a horse to the water but you cannot make it to drink.
explanation: ‘To’ must be removed. There are some verbs that take a bare infinitive(without ‘to’) after them. These are ‘make, let, bid, see, watch, observe’. Hence, ‘make it drink’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate option that rectifies the error
options: in the following sentence. One must do his/her duty proparly.
One must do ones duty properly.
One must do one’s duty properly.
One must do once duty proparly.
One must do one’s duti proprly.
explanation: Each pronoun has its own possessive adjective. For example - (I/my), (he/his), (she/her), (one/one’s). Hence, option (b) is the correct sentence.

text: It is time someone takes concrete steps to alleviate the problem of unemployment in the country.
explanation: Simple Past Tense(Subject + V2) is used after phrases such as “It is time / It is about time / It is high time”. Therefore, ‘takes’ will be replaced with ‘took(V2)’. Hence, ‘It is time someone took’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The food was not as delicious as we had expected.
explanation: correct.

text: None than you deserve credit for the success of this project.
explanation: ‘Than’ must be replaced with ‘but’. The correct phrase is ‘none but’ or ‘none other than’, which means ‘only’. Hence, ‘none but you’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Hold my hand lest you should not get lost in the huge crowd at the fair.
explanation: ‘Lest’ is used without ‘not’. Hence, ‘lest you should’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I will definitely accept the responsibility while the time comes.
explanation: ‘While’ must be replaced with ‘when’. The phrase ‘when the time comes’ is used to state an action that will be done in the suitable circumstances. Hence, ‘when the time comes’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Let us work out the details of our endeavour, shouldn’t we?
explanation: ‘Shall we’ is the correct question tag for an imperative sentence starting with ‘let us’. Hence, ‘shall we’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This is the book whom I wanted to buy.
explanation: ‘Whom’ must be replaced with ‘which’. ‘Whom’ is used for a person whereas ‘which’ is used for things(book). Hence, ‘which I’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Everyone should respect those parents, teachers, and elders.
explanation: ‘His’ is used with ‘everybody / everyone / somebody / someone / nobody / no one’ if the gender is unknown. Similarly, the given sentence talks about every single person, both male and female. Hence, ‘respect his’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: They were / married happily / before she / quit her job.
explanation: ‘Happily’ is an adverb that will be used before the adjective ‘married’ to modify its meaning. Hence, ‘happily married’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The speaker’s emphasiss is on the present-day problems that are being faced by ordinary men of India.
explanation: ‘Emphasis’ is the correct spelling.

text: They want to live in first floor of this building.
explanation: ‘Live in first floor’ must be replaced with ‘live on the first floor’. Definite article ‘the’ is used before a superlative degree adjective. ‘First’ is a superlative adjective. ‘On’ is used to indicate the surface on which something rests. ‘Floor’ is the bottom surface of a room. Hence, ‘live on the first floor’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We / has seen / that movie / before.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘we’ is a plural subject that will take ‘have’ as a plural verb. Hence, ‘have seen’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The given sentence has an error. Choose the option that corrects the error Throw a rounder stone to create ripples in the water.
options: Throw the roundest stone to create ripples in the water.
Throw a more round stone to create ripples in the water.
Throw a more rounder stone to create ripples in the water.
Throw a round stone to create ripples in the water.
explanation: water.(Correct) (a) Throw the roundest stone to create ripples in the water.(Incorrect Adjective) (b) Throw a more round stone to create ripples in the water.(Incorrect Adjective) (c) Throw a more rounder stone to create ripples in the Pinnacle Spot the Error water.(Incorrect Adjective)

text: The dancers swayed dainty on the stage last night.
explanation: ‘Dainty’ must be replaced with ‘daintily’. The given sentence needs an adverb to modify the verb (swayed) and not an adjective(dainty). Hence, ‘swayed daintily’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We feed the horse oats for a week because it had eaten all the hay.
options: it had eaten all the hay
explanation: ‘Feed’ must be replaced with ‘fed’. The given sentence is in the past tense so it must have the verb in the past form(V2) and not in the present form(feed). Hence, ‘We fed the horse oats(V2)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She will have participate / in the dance competition / by the time her father / returns from the tour.
explanation: ‘Participate’ must be replaced with ‘participated’. When we talk about something that will be completed before a specific time in the future, ‘Future perfect tense’(will/shall have + V3) is used. Hence, ‘She will have participated’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: They will not attend / the event / as they’re going / away at end of April.
explanation: We always place the definite article ‘the’ before ‘beginning’ and ‘end’. Hence, ‘away at the end of April’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I wanted to buy a candle holder, / but the store didn't have one. / So, I got a cake.
options: I wanted to buy a candle holder
but the store didn't have one
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: You arrived two days ago. By the time you leave, you will have spent nine days here.
options: you will have spent nine days here
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The simple mistake which was committed by the boy haunted her for years
An simple mistake which was committed by the boy haunted her for years.
The simple mistake which was committed by an boy haunted her for years.
A simple mistake which was committed by an boy haunted her for years.
explanation: boy haunted her for years.(Correct) (b) An simple mistake which was committed by the boy haunted her for years.(Incorrect Article) (c) The simple mistake which was committed by an boy haunted her for years.(Incorrect Article) (d) A simple mistake which was committed by an boy haunted her for years.(Incorrect Article)

text: There is a spectrum / of seas around that /land which attracts/tourists of all aging.
explanation: ‘Aging’ must be replaced with ‘ages’. ‘Of all ages’ is a phrase which means people belonging to all age groups. Hence, ‘tourists of all ages’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Neem tastes / a little bitterly, / but is very useful.
explanation: ‘Bitterly’ must be replaced with the adjective ‘bitter’. ‘Taste’ is a stative verb and stative verbs require an adjective after them, not an adverb. Hence, ‘a little bitter’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Rani was extreme upset with her results this year.
explanation: ‘Extreme’ must be replaced with ‘extremely’. The given sentence requires an adverb to modify the meaning of the adjective ‘upset’. Hence, ‘extremely upset’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The postman / delivers the letters / through hand, / door to door.
explanation: ‘By’ is used to show the means or method used to do something whereas ‘through’ is used to talk about the process by which something happens. Similarly, the given sentence shows that the postman delivers the letters using his hands. Hence, ‘by hand’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Luckily, I managed to get a room in the college hostel, and I move in there.
options: Luckily, I managed to get a room
explanation: ‘Move’ must be replaced with ‘moved’. The given sentence is in Past Tense, so the verb must be used in the past form(moved). Hence, ‘and I moved there’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: There was no other book / in the English language / which is as interesting as this one
options: which is as interesting as this one
explanation: ‘Was’ must be replaced with ‘is’ as the given sentence is in present tense. Hence, ‘there is no other book’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I have never / come to / such a kind person / like my friend.
explanation: ‘Come across’ is a phrasal verb which means to meet or find by accident. Hence, ‘come across to’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Anant was telling a story about his most recent exploits when a tree branch break the living room window.
options: when a tree branch break the living room window
explanation: ‘Break’ must be replaced with ‘broke’. The given sentence is in Past Tense, so the verb will be used in the past form (broke). Hence, ‘when a tree branch broke the living room window’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We should / not make an noise / in the class.
explanation: ‘An noise’ must be replaced with ‘a noise’. Article ‘A’ is used before the words starting from a consonant sound - (a conversation, a story). Hence, ‘not make a noise’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I was wish / to meet her / on her birthday.
explanation: ‘I was wish’ must be replaced with ‘I wish’ as we generally use the expression ‘I wish’ to express wishes or desires. Hence, ‘I wish’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We have being / arranged the stay / for the guests at / a hillside resort.
explanation: ‘We have being’ must be replaced with ‘We have’. The given sentence is in Present Perfect Tense and ‘Plural Sub. + have + V3(arranged)’ is the correct grammatical structure for it. Hence, ‘We have’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The students / are expected / to come/ in the right time.
explanation: ‘In’ must be replaced with ‘at’. ‘At’ is used to indicate the specific time of an action. Hence, ‘at the right time’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We will / have been know the result / of the CAT exam by next week.
options: of the CAT exam by next week
explanation: ‘Have been know’ must be replaced with ‘have known’. Future Perfect Tense is used when the time of completion of an event is given using the preposition ‘by’. ‘Will have + V3’ is the correct grammatical structure for this sentence. Hence, ‘have known(V3) the result’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I am sure Helena / would passes / with flying colours.
explanation: Pinnacle Spot the Error ‘Modal verbs’ are auxiliary verbs(also called helping verbs) like can, will, could, shall, must, would, might, and should. However, after a modal verb, we generally use the first form of the verb (V1). Hence, ‘would pass(V1)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: One of their freighters, / a Neptune,/ will be leaving/ in two weeks.
explanation: Article ‘a’ must be replaced with article ‘the’. ‘Neptune’ mentioned in the given sentence is a specific ship and we generally use the definite article ‘the’ before any specific or particular noun. Hence, ‘the Neptune’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Roger went / to an United Kingdom / with his wife / to celebrate Christmas.
explanation: Article ‘an’ must be replaced with article ‘the’ as we generally use article ‘the’ with the name of the countries that are plural like The U.S.A, The Philippines etc. Hence, ‘to the United Kingdom’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I have a dog and a cow. / A dog is black / but the cow is / black and white.
options: I have a dog and a cow
explanation: Article ‘a’ must be replaced with ‘the’ as we generally use article ‘the’ when talking about specific or known things. Hence, ‘the dog is black’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: (1) He could / (2) be pass his exams / (3) if he studied harder. / (4) No error
explanation: ‘Be pass’ must be replaced with ‘have passed’ as the given sentence is an example of a third conditional sentence and the correct grammatical structure for it is “If + Simple past(V2) / past perfect(had + V3)…….. Would have + V3”. Hence, ‘would have passed his exams’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. The boy told his mother that he saw the most tall giraffe at the zoo.
options: The boy told his mother that he saw the tallest giraffe at the zoo.
The boy told his mother that he saw the most taller giraffe at the zoo.
The boy told his mother that he saw the most tallest giraffe at the zoo.
The boy told his mother that he saw the more taller giraffe at the zoo.
explanation: giraffe at the zoo.(Correct) (b) The boy told his mother that he saw the most taller giraffe at the zoo.(Incorrect Degree) (c) The boy told his mother that he saw the most tallest giraffe at the zoo.(Incorrect Degree) (d) The boy told his mother that he saw the more taller giraffe at the zoo.(Incorrect Degree)

text: Throughout my career as a journalist, / I covered many important stories and / interviewed numerous individuals, which allow me / to share important information and insights with my readers.
options: to share important information and insights with my readers
I covered many important stories and
Throughout my career as a journalist,
interviewed numerous individuals, which allow me
explanation: ‘Allow’ must be replaced with ‘allowed’. The given sentence is in past tense, so it must have the verb in the past form(allowed), not in the present form(allow). Hence, ‘which allowed me’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She performed / the dance routine / perfect, / impressing everyone.
explanation: ‘Perfect’ must be replaced with ‘perfectly’ as we generally use adverbs to modify the meaning of the verb(performed). Hence, ‘perfectly’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In America, / most of the people / can speak / the English well.
explanation: The definite article 'the' is not used before the name of language. Hence, 'English well’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Al fiction is a constantly / evolving genre that gives us an peek / into the potential upsides and downsides / of intelligent machines.
options: into a potential upside and downside
evolving genre that gives us a peek
explanation: Article ‘A’ is used before the words starting from a consonant sound - (a conversation, a story, a peek). Whereas, the article ‘An’ is used before the words starting from a vowel sound(an imminent danger, an apple). Hence ‘evolving genre that gives us a peek’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. If he will come early, we will leave on time.
explanation: ‘Will come’ must be replaced with ‘comes’. The given sentence is an example of the first conditional sentence and the correct grammatical structure is “if + simple present…….will +V1”. Hence ‘comes’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Guard over / making mistakes / by carefully checking / the assigned task.
explanation: ‘Guard over’ must be replaced with ‘guard against’ as the verb ‘guard’ is followed by the preposition ‘against’ when it means to protect something from harm or damage. Hence, ‘guard against’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
options: The Mona Lisa is a famous painting by Leonardo da Vinci.
She is the only person who can speak five languages fluently.
He is a doctor who specialises in the treating rare diseases
I saw the movie that won the Academy Award for Best Picture.
explanation: diseases.(Incorrect) He is a doctor who specialises in treating rare diseases. (Correct) The definite article 'the' is not used before gerunds.

text: After I complete my training program / I will have been joining a team of astronauts / and preparing to / embark on a mission to Mars.
options: I will have been joining a team of astronauts
embark on a mission to Mars
After I complete my training program
explanation: ‘Will have been’ must be replaced with ‘will be’ as the given sentence is in the Future Continuous Tense and the correct grammatical structure is “Subject + will + be + V-ing”. Hence, ‘I will be joining a team of astronauts’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the bad.
options: Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the worst.
Earlier, he was feeling good, but things took a turn for the bad.
Earlier, he was feeling well, but things took a turn for the ill.
Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the ill.
explanation: for the worst.(Correct) (b) Earlier, he was feeling good, but things took a turn for the bad.(Incorrect Word) (c) Earlier, he was feeling well, but things took a turn for the ill.(Incorrect Degree) (d) Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the ill.(Incorrect Word)

text: Why don't / you throw this / paper on the dust bin?
explanation: ‘On’ must be replaced with ‘in’. ‘In’ is used to indicate the location or position of something inside of something else. Preposition ‘On’ is used to indicate that something is touching the surface of something. Hence, ‘in’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: A night alone / in a hotel / can be lonely prospect.
explanation: Article ‘a’ must be used before ‘lonely prospect’ as the adjective ‘lonely’ describes a noun and we need to use an article before the adjective to indicate that it's a singular, countable noun. Hence, ‘can be a lonely prospect’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. The new restaurant on Main Street is cheap than the old one.
explanation: We generally use a comparative degree before ‘than’ and the correct comparative degree of ‘cheap’ is ‘cheaper’. Hence, ‘is cheaper than’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. My relatives shall have reached Amritsar by now.
explanation: ‘Shall’ must be replaced with ‘will’ as we generally use ‘will’ with ‘He/She/It/You/they’ or a noun and ‘shall’ with ‘I’ and ‘we’ only. Hence, ‘will’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: They will start their journey after the breakfast.
explanation: ‘The’ must be removed before ‘breakfast’ as we generally do not use any article before the names of meals(breakfast, dinner, lunch, etc). Hence, ‘after breakfast’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: They had been dancing / for an hour / when our dance teacher/ had arrived.
explanation: 'When + Simple Past Tense(Subject + V2)' is used to indicate the time of occurrence of an event that started in the past. Therefore, ‘had’ must be removed from this part. Hence, 'arrived' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. For an all-too-brief period between the late 1980s and the late 2000s, a world was characterised by convergence.
explanation: ‘A world’ must be replaced with ‘the world’ as we generally use article ‘the’ with a specific place or thing. Hence, ‘the world was’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Shelley and Keats are great writers, but I prefer the last.
explanation: ‘The last’ must be replaced with ‘the latter’ as the word ‘latter’ is used to refer to the second of two things or people. Hence, ‘the latter’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This is the first time / I ate such / a tasty cake.
explanation: Present Perfect Tense(Has/Have + V3) is used when something happens for the first time in the present. Hence, ‘I have eaten(V3) such’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Existentialism has a reputation for being angst-ridden and gloomy mostly because of its emphasis on pondering the meaningless of existence.
options: on pondering the meaningless of existence
explanation: Adjective ‘Meaningless’ must be replaced with the noun ‘meaning’ as we need to use a noun to refer to the concept or state of existence. Hence, ‘on pondering the meaning of existence’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I want to give you / an information about / the missing necklace.
explanation: Article ‘an’ must be removed as we do not use indefinite articles (a/an) before uncountable nouns such as information, luggage, evidence, furniture. Hence, ‘information about’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The mother exclaimed / when she saw her son / stumble on the race track, / "Look, he fells!"
explanation: Pinnacle Spot the Error ‘Fells’ must be replaced with ‘fell’ as the correct past form of the verb ‘fall’ is ‘fell’. Hence, ‘Look, he fell!’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Manisha saw an old elephant / in the wildlife reserve / while she was / on safari tour.
explanation: Article ‘A’ is used before the words starting from a consonant sound - (a conversation, a story). Similarly, in the given sentence, ‘safari’ starts with a consonant. Hence, ‘on a safari tour’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She is very good / in playing / the guitar/ and singing songs.
explanation: Preposition 'At' is usually used to indicate a particular skill or ability. Preposition 'In' is used to indicate being inside something or during a period of time. Hence, 'at playing' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
options: I saw a movie that was directed by Steven Spielberg
She is the only person who can solve this difficult math problem.
He is an lawyer who works for a prestigious law firm.
The Great Wall of China is a popular tourist attraction.
explanation: firm. Article ‘an’ must be replaced with ‘a’ as we generally use article ‘a’ before the words starting with a consonant sound. Similarly, in the given sentence, the noun ‘lawyer’ starts with a consonant sound. Hence, ‘a lawyer’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Four divided by / two is coming / out to / be two.
explanation: ‘Two is coming’ must be replaced with ‘Two comes’. We generally use Simple Present Tense(Singular Sub. + V-s/es) to state a fact or universal truth. Hence, ‘two comes’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This scripture / has been /translated in / seventy languages.
explanation: ‘In’ must be replaced with ‘Into’. Preposition ‘into’ is used to indicate a change from one form or state to another. Similarly, the given sentence talks about the change in scripture from one language to another. Hence, ‘translated into’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She was writing / a letter to her grandmother / when the power / gone out.
explanation: 'When + Simple Past Tense' is used to indicate the time of occurrence of an event that started in the past. 'Subject + V2' is the correct grammatical structure for this sentence. Hence, 'went out(V2)' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mr Sharma would have left / the station / by this time / tomorrow.
explanation: ‘Would’ must be replaced with ‘will’ as we generally use future perfect tense (will/shall + have + V3) to express an action which will be completed before a certain point in the future. Hence, ‘Mr sharma will have left’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The viable of life / depends on a pair of conflicting realities.
explanation: Adjective ‘viable’ must be replaced with the noun ‘viability’ as we need to use a specific noun after the article ‘the.’ Hence, ‘the viability of life’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I shall be playing for four hours.
explanation: ‘Shall be playing’ must be replaced with ‘shall have been playing’ as the given sentence mentions a period of time ‘for four hours’, so we need to use future perfect continuous tense (will/shall + have + been + V1-ing). Hence, ‘shall have been playing’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I had / a bad habit of / waking up / lately.
explanation: Lately means recently while ‘late’ means after the usual or expected time. Adverb ‘late’ is the correct choice here as it denotes the person’s habit of waking up after the expected time in the past. Hence, ‘late’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: As they driven through the dark, twisting lane / down which they had walked earlier, Lucius heard / the whistling of the night air in his ears.
options: down which they had walked earlier, Lucius heard
the whistling of the night air in his ears.
As they driven through the dark, twisting lane
explanation: If two actions took place in the past then the 1st action must be in the Past perfect tense(Had + V3- walked) and the 2nd action must be in the Simple Past tense(V2). However, the V2 form of ‘drive’ is ‘drove’. Hence, ‘as they drove(V2) through the dark, twisting lane’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The platinum is a precious metal.
explanation: Article ‘the’ must be removed as the definite article 'the' is not used before the name of materials like Gold, Silver, Platinum etc. Hence, ‘platinum’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. What most off us want most is to move forward.
explanation: ‘Off’ must be replaced with ‘of’ as ‘Off’ is usually used as a preposition to indicate separation (going away from something) or disconnection. Preposition ‘Of’ is used to indicate something being part of something. Therefore, ‘most of’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This is the eldest standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
options: This is the more older standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
This is the most old standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
This is the more elder standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
This is the oldest standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
explanation: architecture in India. ‘Eldest’ must be replaced with ‘oldest’. We use superlative degree 'eldest' for blood relations of the same generation or lower generation & 'oldest' for something that was created first of all. Hence, ‘option (d)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: They decided to / travel in train / instead of driving / to New Delhi.
explanation: Preposition ‘in’ must be replaced with ‘by’ as preposition ‘by’ is used with the means or method of transportation. For example- by train, by bus, by car, etc. Hence, ‘travel by train’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Radha will have learnt cooking by the time she will have married.
explanation: ‘Will have’ must be replaced with ‘will be’. Simple Present Tense(Singular Sub. + V-s/es) is used with the phrase ‘by the time’ to indicate the point of time in the future when some action will have been completed. Hence, ‘she marries’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The SNAP-10 A / was launched on 3 April 1965 / on a Atlas-Agena D rocket / from Vandenberg Air Force Base.
explanation: Article ‘a’ must be replaced with ‘article ‘an’ as we generally use article ‘an’ with the nouns starting with a vowel sound. Similarly, in the given sentence, ‘Atlas-Agena D’ starts with a vowel sound. Hence, ‘an’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. This car is lesser expensive than the one I had come to buy.
explanation: ‘Lesser’ is used to indicate something of lower importance or significance & ‘less’ used to indicate a lower amount or degree. Hence, ‘less’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
options: I love the taste of fresh strawberries in the summer.
She is the winner of the Nobel Peace Prize.
He is chef who specialises in Italian cuisine.
The Earth revolves around the Sun.
explanation: The article ‘the’ is used to refer to specific or particular nouns. Similarly, in the given sentence, ‘chef’ is a specific person. Hence, ‘He is the chef who specialises in Italian cuisine’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. We think of the past history of the world as fixed but of the future as undecided and open to a wealth off possibilities.
explanation: ‘Wealth of something’ is the correct phrase which means a lot of something. Hence, ‘wealth of’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My teacher told me that / all that /glitters was not gold.
explanation: ‘Was’ must be replaced with ‘is’ as we generally use Simple Present Tense to write proverbs or old sayings. ‘All that glitters is not gold’ is a proverb which means everything that shines is not necessarily good from inside. Hence, ‘glitters is not gold’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It is a / state of chaos / since the/ chairman resigned.
explanation: ‘Is’ must be replaced with ‘has been’ as we generally use present perfect tense(has/have + V3) to discuss a situation that began in Pinnacle Spot the Error the past and continues into the present. Similarly, in the given sentence, a state of chaos began in the past and still exists in the present. Hence, ‘it has been a’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Henry is known / as an excellent writer / and good communicator/in English.
explanation: Use of the adjective 'good' is superfluous in this sentence as there is already an adjective(excellent) which qualifies the meaning of both the nouns, 'writer' and 'communicator'. Therefore, 'good' must be removed. Hence, 'and communicator' is the most appropriate answer.

text: With cloud streaming, people can play games from a / internet-connected device, avoiding the need for pricey / dedicated hardware such as a game console.
options: dedicated hardware such as a game console
With cloud streaming, people can play games from a
internet-connected device, avoiding the need for pricey
explanation: The article ‘An’ is used before the words starting from a vowel sound(an imminent danger, an apple). Similarly, the word ‘internet’ starts with a vowel sound. Hence, ‘With cloud streaming, people can play games from an’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This fridge/ comes including / a 5-year / warranty.
explanation: We use the phrase 'including' to give further examples of people or things that we are talking about. The phrase 'come with' means having something as an essential part. Similarly, warranty is an essential part of the fridge. ’Hence, 'comes with' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. To much seriousness hardens the world, pinning it down with rules.
explanation: ‘To’ must be replaced with ‘too’ as ‘too’ is used to indicate an excessive or more than necessary amount. Hence, ‘too much’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The boy whose the sister is ill has left.
explanation: Article ‘the’ must be removed before ‘sister’ as the word ‘whose’ is used to indicate possession or association, and it should be followed directly by the noun it is describing. Hence, ‘whose sister’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The space agency wanted / to test with a chimp / before orbiting a astronaut / in a Mercury capsule.
explanation: Article ‘A’ is used before the words starting from a consonant sound - (a conversation, a story). Whereas, the article ‘An’ is used before the words starting with a vowel sound(an imminent danger, an apple). Similarly, in the given sentence, ‘astronaut’ is a noun starting with a vowel sound. Hence, ‘an astronaut’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If he had paid / attention to the announcement, / he had not / missed the train.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of a third conditional sentence and the correct grammatical structure is “If + past perfect(had + V3)…….. Would have + V3”. Hence, ‘he would not have’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He is the better-looking hero in the entire film industry.
options: He is the best-looking hero in the entire film industry.
He is the good-looking hero than the entire film industry.
He is the best-looking hero more than the entire film industry.
He is the good-looking hero in the entire film industry.
explanation: industry.(Correct) (b) He is the good-looking hero than the entire film industry.(Incorrect Degree) (c) He is the best-looking hero more than the entire film industry.(Incorrect Word) (d) He is the good-looking hero in the entire film industry.(Incorrect Degree)

text: When Nisha will have finished her task?
explanation: ‘Nisha will’ must be replaced with ‘will Nisha’ as the correct grammatical structure to form interrogative sentences is “Wh. Word + Helping Verb + Subject + Main Verb”. Hence, ‘when will Nisha’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My daughter was / invited to lunch / hosted by the Governor / at his residence.
explanation: When we talk about a meal(lunch/dinner/breakfast) as a special event, we use the article 'the' before the meal. For ex- the lunch with the president of India. Hence, ‘invited to the lunch’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The new software / consists from /several features / and tools.
explanation: ‘Of’ is a fixed preposition used after the verb ‘consist’. Hence, ‘consists of’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If you work hard, you secure good marks.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of the first conditional sentence and the correct grammatical structure is “if + simple present…….will +V1”. Hence,‘you will secure’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The cholera is a frightful disease.
explanation: Article ‘the’ must be removed before ‘cholera’ as we generally don’t use the definite article ‘the’ before the names of illnesses or diseases. Hence, ‘cholera’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The twins are / often told that / they are resembling / each other.
explanation: We generally use Simple Present Tense(Plural Sub. + V1) for generally held beliefs or opinions. Similarly, the given sentence states an opinion about twins. Hence, 'they resemble(V1)' is the most appropriate answer.

text: He / lives / in 45 Church Street / with his family.
explanation: ‘In’ must be replaced with ‘at’ as we generally use the preposition ‘at’ for smaller or specific locations. Hence, ‘at 45 Church Street’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He sang / beautifully but / the judges were / unimpress at the end.
explanation: ‘Unimpress’ must be replaced with the adjective ‘unimpressed’ as we generally use adjectives after stative verbs(‘were’ in the given sentence). Hence, ‘unimpressed at the end’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Identify the error in the use of preposition in the given sentence and select the correct option. Radhika is not capable on participating in a national level competition.
explanation: Use of ‘on’ after the word ‘capable’ is incorrect. ‘On’ must be replaced with ‘of’ as ‘of’ is a fixed preposition used after the word ‘capable’ to denote capability. Hence, ‘of’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In course by time, / he was wise enough to realise / the mistakes of his past life.
options: he was wise enough to realise
the mistakes of his past life.
explanation: ‘By’ must be replaced with ‘of’ as ‘in course of time’ is the correct phrase. This phrase is used when something happens over a period of time. Hence, ‘in course of time’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the grammatically correct version of the following sentence. I like my puppies, Mac and Matt, but I like Matt best.
options: I like my puppies, Mac and Matt, but I like Matt better.
I like my puppies, Mac and Matt, but I like Matt the best.
I like my puppies, Mac and Matt, but I like Matt much.
I like my puppies, Mac and Matt, but I like Matt most.
explanation: better. (Correct) (b) I like my puppies, Mac and Matt, but I like Matt the best. (Incorrect Degree) (c) I like my puppies, Mac and Matt, but I like Matt much. (Incorrect Degree) (d) I like my puppies, Mac and Matt, but I like Matt most. (Incorrect Degree)

text: The current state of the literature / on the efficacy under cognitive-behavioural therapy / for individuals with generalised anxiety disorder / suggests that it is a promising treatment option.
options: The current state of the literature
suggests that it is a promising treatment option
on the efficacy under cognitive-behavioural therapy
for individuals with generalised anxiety disorder.
explanation: ‘Under’ must be replaced with ‘of’. ‘Under’ is used to denote the position of something/somebody at a lower level. ‘Of’ is used to mention the parts or characteristics of something. Hence, ‘on the efficacy of cognitive-behavioural therapy’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The rich / should / help / poor.
explanation: Article ‘the’ is used when we use an adjective to represent the whole class. Similarly, in the given sentence, we are referring to the whole class of poor people. Hence, ‘the poor’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He was / that angry / that he slammed the book / on the table.
explanation: ‘That angry’ must be replaced with ‘so angry’ as ‘so…that’ is a fixed conjunction pair. Hence, ‘so angry’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: After working so much / in the fields yesterday / did you took a break?
explanation: ‘Took’ must be replaced with ‘take’ as we generally use the first form of the verb(V1) after ‘did’. Hence, ‘did you take a break’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Do you want / to visit a zoo / when you / go to Ahmedabad?
explanation: Article ‘a’ must be replaced with ‘the’ to specify a particular zoo. Hence, ‘to visit the zoo’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Suman has bought / a black and a white shawl / to wear with / her new dress.
options: a black and a white shawl
explanation: Article ‘a’ must be removed before ‘white’. We use article ‘a’ once when there is only one person or thing. Hence, ‘a black and white shawl’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Nobody from the gathering / of odd people could guess / the accident occurring blast.
explanation: ‘Occurring’ must be replaced with ‘that caused the’ as ‘caused’ means to make something happen. The phrase "that caused the blast" is used to clarify that the accident was responsible for the blast. Hence, ‘that caused the blast’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I have read that / a Leaning Tower of Pisa is a / popular tourist attraction / in the world.
options: a Leaning Tower of Pisa is a
explanation: Article ‘A’ must be replaced with article ‘the’ as we generally use article ‘the’ with a specific and well-known structure. Hence, ‘the leaning tower of Pisa is a’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Sita spotted golden / deer and / requested Rama / to capture it.
explanation: Article ‘A’ is used before the words starting from a consonant sound - (a conversation, a story). Therefore, article ‘a’ must be used before the word ‘golden’. Hence, ‘Sita spotted a golden’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The investigation conducting by the research team / yielded statistically significant results / providing substantial evidence / to support the hypothesis.
options: The investigation conducting by the research team
explanation: A participle phrase is a group of words which includes a past participle form (V3) and functions as an adjective, providing additional information about the subject. Similarly, In the given sentence, the participle phrase "conducted(V3) by the team" provides additional information about the subject ‘the investigation’. Hence, 'the investigation conducted by the research team' is the most appropriate answer.

text: It was Ravi, not his friends, / who were shouting / at late hours last night.
options: It was Ravi, not his friends,
explanation: ‘Were’ must be replaced with ‘was.’ According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. ‘Ravi’ is a singular subject that will take ‘was’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘who was shouting’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Washington Irving's writing career started at / the tender age of nineteen when he joined / his brother Peter's newspaper The Morning Chronicle / as journalist.
options: his brother Peter's newspaper The Morning Chronicle
Washington Irving's writing career started at
the tender age of nineteen when he joined
explanation: Article ‘a’ is used before the words starting from a consonant sound (a conversation, a story). Therefore, article ‘a’ must be used before the word ‘journalist’. Hence, ‘as a journalist’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: There was a saying that they’re their own enemies with negligble reason to be shared.
explanation: ‘Negligible’ is the correct spelling.

text: Can you make / sure you have / a correct address / before you start driving?
explanation: ‘’A correct address’ must be replaced with ‘the correct address’ as we generally use article ‘the’ before definite or particular nouns. Similarly, the given sentence is talking about a particular address. Hence, ‘the correct address’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The food container / is not enough big to meet / the demands of the affected people.
options: is not enough big to meet
the demands of the affected people
explanation: ‘Enough big’ must be replaced with ‘big enough’ as ‘enough’ is a special adverb and always used after the adjective(‘big’ in the given sentence). Hence, ‘is not big enough to meet’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: By virtue off / the power given to the leader / the followers accepted his decision
options: the power given to the leader
explanation: ‘By virtue of’ is the correct preposition and it is used to provide reason. Hence, ‘by virtue of’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The team of scientists / were conducting / experiments to test / their hypothesis
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. ‘Team’ is a singular subject that will take ‘was’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘was conducting’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This region / was struck by unusual / wave of violence / last year.
explanation: Article ‘An’ is used before the words starting from a vowel sound(an imminent danger, an apple). Therefore, article ‘an’ must be used before the word ‘unusual’. Hence, ‘was struck by an unusual’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: With reference of your letter, / the organisation wishes to hire you / for the security services.
options: the organisation wishes to hire you
explanation: ‘Of’ must be replaced with ‘to’ as ‘with reference to’ is the correct phrase which means about or concerning(something). Hence, ‘with reference to your letter’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It is imperative in understanding / the rising importance of artificial intelligence / in the public sector to increase the efficacy / and impact of the work done for public welfare.
options: the rising importance of artificial intelligence
and impact of the work done for public welfare.
in the public sector to increase the efficacy
explanation: ‘In understanding’ must be replaced with ‘to understand’. We generally use the phrase ‘it is imperative/important + to + V1’ when the infinitive(to + V1) tells us what is important. Hence, ‘it is imperative to understand(V1)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The soldier met / a fearless death / fighting on behalf at his country.
options: fighting on behalf at his country
explanation: ‘On behalf at his country’ must be replaced with ‘on behalf of his country’. The phrase ‘on behalf of’ is used to indicate that someone is acting or speaking for another person, group or organisation. Hence, ‘fighting on behalf of his country’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
options: I need to buy an new iPhone.
The cat sat on the windowsill
She is the best singer in the choir.
He is an artist who paints landscapes.
explanation: I need to buy a new iPhone.(Correct) Article ‘A’ is used before the words starting from a consonant sound - (a conversation, a story).

text: The man / is a / social animal.
explanation: No article is used when a noun is used in the general sense. Therefore, article ‘the’ must be removed before ‘man’. Hence, ‘man’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The poor undergoes / several problems in life / that could be / solved with money.
explanation: An adjective represents the whole class of people when article ‘the’ is used before it. Similarly, ‘the poor’ represents all the poor people. We always use a plural verb after such adjectives. Hence, ‘The poor undergo’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: I could not find it anywhere.
explanation: (a) He ate the sweets greedy.(‘Greedily’ will be used) (c) I haven't got none.(‘Have’ will be used) (d) He is much weak.(‘Weaker’ will be used)

text: Hurray! Here is the toy / what I was looking for / as my birthday gift.
explanation: ‘What’ must be replaced with ‘that’ as when we introduce a relative clause that provides more information about a noun, we typically use "that" or "which" instead of "what". Hence, ‘that i was looking for’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The politician was accused / of accepting bribes / and lied about it / to the public.
explanation: According to the ‘Rule of Parallelism’, two or more verbs must be in the same form if they are connected with one another. Similarly, in the given sentence, ‘and’ connects two verbs 'accepting(Ving)’ and ‘lied’. Therefore, ‘lying(Ving)’ must be used in place of ‘lied’. Hence, ‘and lying about it’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The news / is / very good / to be true.
explanation: ‘Very’ must be replaced with ‘too’ as ‘too good to be true’ is an idiom that means something is so positive or favorable. Hence, ‘too good’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Identify the error in the use of preposition in the given sentence and select the correct option. Her family lost their way on Daman.
explanation: The preposition ‘on’ must be replaced with ‘in’ as ‘In’ is used to indicate location or position within a place or area. Similarly, in the sentence, ‘Daman’ is a location and we need to use the preposition ‘in’ before it. Hence, ‘in’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
explanation: Rama can bowl fast.(Correct) ‘Fast’ is already an adverb. We can not add ‘ly’ to it.

text: I brought / an apple from a place you recommended / me earlier.
explanation: The article ‘the’ is used to refer to specific or particular nouns & articles ‘a/an’ are used for non-specific or non-particular nouns. For example, if someone says, "Let's buy the book," it means a specific book but if someone says, "Let's buy a book," it means any book rather than a specific book. Similarly, the given sentence talks about a specific place. Hence, ‘the place you recommended’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: A crocodile / was swimming / in a river.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Select the grammatically correct version of the following sentence. He was youngest than his brother.
options: He was younger than his brother.
He was youngest to his brother.
He was too young than his brother
He was young to his brother.
explanation: (b) He was youngest to his brother.(Incorrect Degree and Word) (c) He was too young than his brother.(Incorrect Word and Degree) (d) He was young to his brother.(Incorrect Degree and Word)

text: Sudharshan came.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of passive voice of Past Continuous Tense and the subject ‘they’ is plural. ‘Plural Sub. + were + Ving‘ is the correct grammatical structure for this sentence. ‘Laid’ must be replaced with ‘lying’ as ‘lying’ means resting in a horizontal position. Hence, ‘they were lying’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The participants of the competition are waiting for their turn curiously.
The participants of the competition has been waiting for their turn curiously.
A participants of the competition is waiting for their turn curiously.
The participants of the competition is waiting for their turn curiously.
explanation: their turn curiously.(Correct) (b) The participants of the competition has been waiting for their turn curiously.(Incorrect Tense) (c) A participants of the competition is waiting for their turn curiously.(Incorrect Article and Verb) (d) The participants of the competition is waiting for their turn curiously.(Incorrect Helping Verb)

text: After knowing truth, / the jury took the right decision / in the case.
options: The jury took the right decision
explanation: Article ‘the’ will be used before ‘truth’ as we generally use the definite article ‘the’ with a specific noun. Hence, ‘after knowing the truth’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The availability of funds will be / ensured if they all tried to / submit the proposals on time.
options: The availability of funds will be
ensured if they all tried to
explanation: ‘Tried’ must be replaced with ‘try’ as the given sentence is an example of the first conditional sentence. According to it, when the main clause is in the future tense, the verb in the subordinate clause (the part after "if") should be in the present tense. Hence, ‘ensured if they all try to’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the grammatically correct statement from among the given options. A. It is a nice party. I am enjoying the party. B. It is a party. I am enjoying an party. C. It is party. I am enjoying a party. D. It is the party. I am enjoying an party.
explanation: (a) D. It is the party. I am enjoying an party. (Incorrect Article) (b) C. It is party. I am enjoying a party. (Incorrect Article) (c) B. It is a party. I am enjoying an party. (Incorrect Article)

text: I can't talk right now. / I am being really busy. / I'll call you later.
explanation: Use of ‘being’ is superfluous as we need to use only simple present tense in the given sentence. Hence, ‘I am really busy’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The following sentence has been divided into three segments, A, B, C. One of them may contain a grammatical error. Select the segment that contains the error, form the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Aniket lives
explanation: Article ‘the’ must be replaced with ‘a’ as ‘small apartment’ mentioned in the given sentence is not specific and we generally use the indefinite article ‘a’ before a non-specific noun. Hence, ‘in a small apartment’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The present-century threats to our environment, / which include interfering species, ailments, pollution and / a boiling temperature, were putting wildlife populations at peril.
options: which include interfering species, ailments, pollution and
The present-century threats to our environment
a boiling temperature, were putting wildlife populations at peril
explanation: populations at peril. 'Were' must be replaced with 'are' as the given sentence states an action in present tense, clearly indicated by the term 'The present-century'. So we need to use present continuous tense(are + V1-ing). Hence, 'are putting wildlife populations at peril' is the most appropriate answer.

text: "Do you want to join us for lunch?" / "I'm sorry / my physics class will start at 1 p.m. / and doesn't finish till 3 p.m."
options: my physics class will start at 1 p.m.
Do you want to join us for lunch?
explanation: ‘Will start’ must be replaced with ‘starts’ as we generally use simple present tense(V1-s/es) to indicate routines that happen regularly. Hence, ‘starts(V1-s)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Sky appears blue / as it absorbs / all colours and /reflects only blue.
explanation: ‘Sky appears’ must be replaced with ‘The sky appears’ as we generally use definite article (the) before a specific or particular noun. Hence, ‘The sky appears blue’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: A celestial body or astronomical object is / a naturally occurring physical thing, association, / or configuration that happens in the visible universe.
options: A celestial body or astronomical object is
or configuration that happens in the visible universe
a naturally occurring physical thing, association
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: The following sentence has been divided into three segments, A, B, C. One of them may contain a grammatical error. Select the segment that contains the error, from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer. It was
options: / he saw a movie in a theatre
explanation: Article ‘a‘ must be removed as ‘by chance’ is the correct phrase. ‘By chance’ means accidentally, without plan or intent. Hence, ‘by chance’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: One of these / boxes have / the portrait / of the heiress.
explanation: ‘Have’ must be replaced with ‘has.’ According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, ‘One of/ Each of/ Most of/ Either of + Plural Subject + Singular verb’ is grammatically the correct structure. Hence, ‘boxes has’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: You can fool some of the people all the time, and all the people some of the time; but you cannot fool all the people all the time.
options: You can fool some of the people all the time
and all the people some of the time
but you cannot fool all the people all the time.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Hardik's horoscope says / that the stars / will be exercised/ a benign influence on his life.
options: a benign influence on his life
explanation: ‘Will be exercised’ must be replaced with ‘will exercise’ as we generally use active voice when the subject is the doer of the action. In the given sentence, the subject(‘stars’) is the doer of the action(exercise an influence). Hence, ‘will exercise’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I had gone to Siliguri before I go to Raiganj .
explanation: ‘Go’ must be replaced with ‘went’. If two actions took place in the past then the 1st action must be in the Past perfect tense(Had + V3) and the 2nd action must be in the Simple Past tense(V2). Hence, ‘went(V2)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If things were not going to be normal / after the pandemic, mankind will / have to accept the New Normal.
options: have to accept the New Normal
If things were not going to be normal
explanation: ‘Were’ must be replaced with ‘are’ as the given sentence is an example of the mixed conditional sentence and the correct grammatical structure is “If + Present Tense…….will +V1”. Hence ‘If things are not going to be normal’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The decision to change a hospital saved an life of the daughter of the doctor.
The decision to change the hospital saved the life of the daughter of the doctor.
The decision to change an hospital saved the life of the daughter of the doctor.
A decision to change a hospital saved the life of the daughter of the doctor.
explanation: the daughter of the doctor.(Correct) (a) The decision to change a hospital saved an life of the daughter of the doctor.(Incorrect Article) (c) The decision to change an hospital saved the life of the daughter of the doctor.(Incorrect Article) (d) A decision to change a hospital saved the life of the daughter of the doctor.(Incorrect Article)

text: I am sure that / the postman would be / coming shortly / to deliver the letter.
explanation: ‘Would be’ must be replaced with ‘will be’. Modal ‘would’ is used to talk about the future as seen from the past. Modal ‘will’ is used to talk about the future as seen from the present moment. As the first part of the sentence is in Present Tense, modal ‘will’ will be used. Hence, ‘the postman will be’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Maruti likes / adventure / stories, especially / an adventures of Tarzan.
explanation: ‘An’ must be replaced with ‘the. The word "adventures" is plural, so it should not be preceded by the singular article "an”. We generally use the definite article with a specific noun or a particular noun (adventures of Tarzan). Hence, ‘the adventures of Tarzan’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The historians / are a great / asset to the/ field of academia.
explanation: Pinnacle Spot the Error ‘The historians’ must be replaced with ‘historians’ as we generally use definite article ‘the’ with a specific or particular noun. Here, in the given sentence ‘historians’ is a common noun. So, we will not use definite articles before ‘historians’. Hence, ‘historians’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The warrior was waiting for an right time to attack the lion hiding in a cave.
The warrior was waiting for the right time to attack the lion hiding in the cave.
An warrior was waiting for a right time to attack the lion hiding in the cave.
The warrior was waiting for a right time to attack an lion hiding in the cave.
explanation: the lion hiding in the cave. (Correct) (a) The warrior was waiting for an right time to attack the lion hiding in a cave.(Incorrect Article) (c) An warrior was waiting for a right time to attack the lion hiding in the cave.(Incorrect Article) (d) The warrior was waiting for a right time to attack an lion hiding in the cave. (Incorrect Article)

text: We hardly knew nothing / about the manager / who had recently joined.
explanation: ‘Nothing’ must be replaced with ‘anything’. ‘Hardly’ and ‘Nothing’ both are negative words so we can’t use them together. We generally use the pronoun ‘anything’ in negative and interrogative sentences. Hence, ‘ we hardly knew anything’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Anti-party activities / improved my relations /with an opposition.
explanation: Article ‘An’ must be replaced with ‘the’ as Article ‘the’ is used to represent a class or group. Hence, ‘with the opposition’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: You wash / the dishes / and / I dry the same.
explanation: ‘I dry’ must be replaced with ‘I will dry’ as ‘‘Simple Future Tense(Will + V1)’’ is used when discussing a planned action in the future that is related to a present action. Hence, ‘I will dry the same’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: It was a hectic day for Susan with a lot of purchases and a couple of meetings.
It was a hectic day for Susan with the lot of purchase and a couple of meetings.
It was a hectic day for Susan with the lot of purchase and an couple of meetings.
It was the hectic day for Susan with a lot of purchase and the couple of meetings.
explanation: and a couple of meetings.(Correct) (b) It was a hectic day for Susan with the lot of purchase and a couple of meetings.(Incorrect Noun) (c) It was a hectic day for Susan with the lot of purchase and an couple of meetings.(Incorrect Noun) (d) It was the hectic day for Susan with a lot of purchase and the couple of meetings.(Incorrect Article)

text: She is in / an hurry / to meet / her brother.
explanation: ‘An hurry’ must be replaced with ‘a hurry’ as article ‘A’ is used before the words starting from a consonant sound - (a conversation, a story). Hence, ‘She is in a hurry’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Identify the option that rectifies the error in the given sentence. In 2023, she will has been working in the company for three years.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of ‘Future perfect continuous Tense’ and the correct grammatical structure is “Will/shall + have been + V1-ing”. Hence, ‘she will have been’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: They usually allege that there is / a delay in procuring stationery / due to the faulty purchase orders.
options: due to the faulty purchase orders
They usually allege that there is
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: It can / get extreme cold / during / the winters.
explanation: ‘Extreme’ must be replaced with ‘extremely’ as the given sentence needs an adverb to modify the adjective(cold). Hence, ‘It can get extremely cold’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I caught / a white cat / rustling / beneath my room.
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition 'beneath' must be replaced with 'in' as ‘beneath’ is Pinnacle Spot the Error used to indicate a location that is below something and ‘in’ is used to indicate that something is located inside of something else. Hence, 'in my room' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Kids learn / a lot by / their / school activities and homework
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. ‘A lot by’ must be replaced with ‘a lot from’ as the preposition ‘by’ is generally used to indicate the way something is done and the preposition ‘from’ is used to indicate the source of gaining knowledge. Hence, ‘a lot from’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the grammatically correct sentence. A. I would like to spend an evening near pool with a cup of coffee. B. I would like to spend an evening near pool with cup of coffee. coffee. coffee
explanation: cup of coffee. (a) I would like to spend a evening near a pool with a cup of coffee. (Incorrect article) (c) I would like to spend an evening near pool with cup of coffee. (Article missing) (d) I would like to spend an evening near pool with a cup of coffee. (Article missing)

text: If you live / in a foreign country,/ you should/ try and learn language.
explanation: ‘And’ must be replaced with ‘to’ as we generally use an ‘to + infinitive(V1)’ after certain verbs like try, bid, let, make, need etc. Hence, ‘try to learn language’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: There are more than two million/job-seekers who are already / completed their fitness test/for the post since 2020.
options: There are more than two million
explanation: ‘Are’ must be replaced with ‘have’ as we need to use present perfect tense (have + V3) to indicate actions that started in the past and continue into the present. Hence, ‘job-seekers who have already’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He is as concerned as me / regarding / the renewed / examination schedule.
options: He is as concerned as me
explanation: Pronoun ‘Me’ must be replaced with ‘I’ as the conjunction pair “as….as” is used to do comparison between the same ‘Cases of pronoun’. So we need to use the subjective case of pronoun i.e. ‘I’. Hence, ‘He is as concerned as I’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: room / to hand over the packet to her, / she asked me to sit reluctant
options: she asked me to sit reluctant
to hand over the packet to her,
when I quietly entered her room
explanation: ‘Reluctant’ must be replaced with ‘Reluctantly’ as we generally use adverbs to modify or describe verbs(sit). Hence, ‘she asked me to sit reluctantly’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The police could not / hold on the people / for long as they / gathered in large numbers.
explanation: ‘On’ must be replaced with ‘back’ as the “Hold back" is a phrasal verb that means to stop or prevent someone or something. Hence, ‘hold back the people’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The students were / able to get better from / college early so they / went to the movies.
explanation: ‘Better’ must be replaced with ‘back’ as the phrase ‘get back’ means to return. Hence, ‘get back’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The front part is used for carving / the lines and the back end / for scratching of whole areas.
options: the lines and the back end
The front part is used for carving
explanation: Preposition ‘of’ will be removed as scratch is a transitive verb and it will not use any preposition with it. The will be used before “whole”. Hence, ‘For scratching the whole areas’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Where can I find / a good Chinese / restaurant about here?
explanation: ‘About’ will be removed. ‘About’ is not needed. Hence, ‘restaurant here’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Factoring is, of course, different from and superior than / bill discounting, from the point of / view of a small company
options: bill discounting, from the point of
Factoring is, of course, different from and superior than
explanation: Factoring is, of course, different from and superior than ‘Than’ will be replaced by ‘to’ as we generally use the preposition ‘to’ with some Adjectives for comparison (Similar, Superior, Inferior, Equal, Identical). Hence, ‘Factoring is, of course, different from and superior to’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Now its referring to the same / big lug who met his fate / thanks to David's slingshot.
options: big lug who met his fate
Now its referring to the same
explanation: It's is a contraction and should be used where a sentence would read "it is." Its with no apostrophe is the possessive pronoun, like "his" and "her," for nouns without gender. Hence, ‘Now it’s referring to the same’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Much of the art he/ discusses is funny, playing / and mischievous.
explanation: ‘Playing’ must be replaced with ‘playful’ as we need to use a predicative adjective : These adjectives come after linking verbs (e.g., "be," "become," "seem") and describe the subject of the sentence. Hence, ‘discusses is funny, playful’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error’ The police released a statement saying, / “This was one of the most vicious/ attack we have ever seen.”
options: The police released a statement saying,
"This was one of the most vicious
explanation: “One of the + Superlative degree of the adjective(best, worst, etc) + Plural Subject” is grammatically the correct structure. For example, one of the best men, one of the greatest kings, one of the worst phones, etc. Hence, ‘attacks we have ever seen’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: Why is your friend / giving me / weird looks?
explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Participants in our / studies reviewed these / online dating profiles.
explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct.

text: To treat nightmare disorder, / there is a number / of medications and therapies.
explanation: ‘Is’ must be replaced with ‘are’ in the given sentence. According to the subject-verb agreement, ‘A + Number of + Plural nouns’ always takes plural verbs. Hence, ‘there are a number’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It is believed that / difficult tasks demand lot / of our resources.
explanation: We generally use article ‘a’ with ‘lot’ as an expression meaning ‘a larger quantity’ or 'many’ (a lot of books, a lot of experience). Hence, ‘difficult tasks demand a lot’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Your ears are itching / because you are having an / allergic reaction.
explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct.

text: 'Don't you get / involve!' Sandhya / whispered urgently to him.
explanation: ‘Involve’ must be replaced with ‘Involved’ in the given sentence. As we generally use past participles with the verb ‘get’. Hence, ‘involved!’ Sandhya’ will be the most appropriate answer.

text: Never put of / until tomorrow what / you can do today.
explanation: ‘Of’ must be replaced with ‘off’ as the phrasal verb ‘put off’ means to delay doing something. Hence, ‘never put off’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: India is already the third-largest / aviation market in / terms of domestic travel.
explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Shapes that are impossible / to make of machining / can be printed.
explanation: The preposition ‘of’ must be replaced with ‘by’ in the given sentence. The use of the preposition ‘by’ is correct because it is indicating the method by which the shapes are made. While the preposition ‘of’ is used to indicate a part of something. Hence, ‘to make by matching’ will be the most appropriate answer.

text: The Gryffindors trooped back up / to the castle, none of them talking; / it have been another long day.
options: it have been another long day.
to the castle, none of them talking;
explanation: ‘Have’ must be replaced with ‘has’ in the given sentence. According to the subject-verb agreement, a singular subject takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. Here, in the sentence ‘it’ is a singular subject. Hence, ‘it has been another long day’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Our passage across the Arabian Sea / was smooth as the most timid of / navigators could desire.
options: Our passage across the Arabian Sea
was smooth as the most timid of
explanation: Conjunction 'as' will be replaced with 'as...as'. The conjunction 'as' is used to state the reason whereas the conjunction 'as...as' is used to state similarity between two things or situations. The given sentence states the similarity of smoothness between the passage and the desires of the most timid navigator. Hence, 'as smooth as the most timid' is the most appropriate answer.

text: When I have arrived at / the theatre, the show / had already started.
explanation: If two actions took place in the past then the 1st action must be in the Past perfect tense(Had + V3) and the 2nd action must be in the Simple Past tense(V2). Hence, ‘when I arrived at’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Professor Murli’s eyebrows / rose a little higher and his / gaze became distinctly coldest.
options: rose a little higher and his
explanation: ‘Coldest’ must be replaced by ‘colder’ as to maintain consistency, the correct usage would be to use the comparative degree throughout the sentence. In this correction, both "higher" and "colder" are in the comparative degree, indicating a comparison between two states or levels. Hence, ‘gaze became distinctly colder’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Early, during December 2021,/ Lal was appointed as / the Secretary to the Lokpal.
explanation: Pinnacle Spot the Error The error in the sentence is the use of the word "during." Since the sentence specifies December 2021, it implies that Lal was appointed as the Secretary to the Lokpal at some point within that month. However, the word "during" suggests a continuous action or a period of time, which is not appropriate in this context. Hence, ‘Early in december 2021’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In 79 A.D., the Mount Vesuvius blew / its top, burying the ancient / cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum.
options: In 79 A.D., the Mount Vesuvius blew
explanation: Article ‘the’ must be removed as we generally use article ‘the’ with the names of mountains but we do not use ‘the’ if the name includes Mount or Mountain (Mount Olympus, Brokeback Mountain).

text: I hope that / we will arrive at / the ideal trade-off soon.
explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct.

text: If I was a clown, / I would have made / everyone smile.
explanation: ‘Was’ must be replaced with ‘Were’. When expressing unreal or hypothetical situations in the present or future, the subjunctive mood is used, which requires the use of ‘were’ instead of ‘was’ after ‘if’. Hence, ‘If I were a clown’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Peoples might confess / just to get out of / the interrogation room.
explanation: ‘Peoples’ must be replaced with ‘people’ as people is already the plural form and it doesn’t require ‘s’ to make its plural form. Hence, ‘people might confess’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Many female mammals, / including rabbits and cats, ovulate / only when they mate.
explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct.

text: It'd be really cool if you got / on the team, I've never seen you / played badminton, are you good?
options: on the team, I've never seen you
It'd be really cool if you got
explanation: ‘Played’ must be replaced with ‘play’ as we generally use bare infinitives after the verbs such as let, bid, see, hear, watch, observe, etc. Hence, ‘play badminton, are you good’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The kids there were so notorious, the / more I asked them to quiet down, / the more loud they would scream.
options: the more loud they would scream.
more I asked them to quiet down,
The kids there were so notorious, the
