explanation: The phrase ‘the more loud’ will be replaced with the correct comparative degree ‘the louder’. Hence, ‘the louder they would scream’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The Federalists wished to / make the central government / as strong possible.
explanation: ‘As strong possible’ will be replaced with ‘ as strong as possible’. This is because "As...as" is a comparative structure that shows similarity or equality between two elements. It is used to compare two things or actions and indicates that they are of the same degree or level. Hence, ‘as strong as possible’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Can you please / help me to / this project?
explanation: ‘Help me to’ will be replaced with ‘help me with’ as the verb "help" is typically followed by the preposition "with" when indicating assistance or support in accomplishing a task or project. Hence, ‘Help me with’ will be the most appropriate answer.

text: He belted two huge sixers, but / eleven to get of the last two / deliveries was a big ask.
options: eleven to get of the last two
explanation: ‘Get of’ will be replaced with ‘Get off’ as it means to successfully complete or achieve. It conveys the intended meaning that eleven runs were needed to successfully complete the last two deliveries. Hence, ‘Get off’ will be the most appropriate answer.

text: Can you please / pass me that / glittery pen black?
explanation: Adjectives should be written before the noun (pen) that is being qualified. The general order of adjectives before a noun is the following: Opinion, Size, Shape, Condition, Age, Colour,Pattern, Origin, Material and Purpose. ‘Glittery’ represents opinion and ‘black’ is the color. Hence, ‘glittery black pen’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Before he could devote many more / thought to the matter, Pranav / had stepped up to him.
options: Before he could devote many more
explanation: ‘Many more’ will be replaced with ‘much more’ as much is used to describe the quantity of an uncountable noun. The word "thought" is an uncountable noun, which means it cannot be used with ‘many’. Hence, ‘before he could devote much more’ will be the most appropriate answer.

text: I spend a lot of / my time at work helping my / customers find an best outfit.
options: my time at work helping my
explanation: ‘An’ will be replaced with ‘the’ as the adjective ‘best’ is the superlative degree of ‘well’ and we generally use definite articles with superlative degrees. Hence, ‘customers find the best outfit’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: When he buckled down to his / work he became the slyer / and cleverest of diplomats.
options: When he buckled down to his
explanation: ‘The slyer’ will be replaced with ‘the slyest’ as ‘slyer’ is a comparative form and we need a superlative form of the adjective ‘sly’ i.e. ‘slyest’ to match the later part of the sentence. Hence, ‘Work he became the slyest’ will be the most appropriate answer.

text: Neither teahers or / the principal revolted against / the new education policy
explanation: ‘Neither teachers or’ will be replaced with ‘neither teachers nor’ as ‘neither….nor’ is a fixed conjunction pair. Hence, ‘Neither teachers nor’ will be the most appropriate answer.

text: George handing the / hairpin to Ron, / a moment later.

text: Fortunately, he passed the exams / with dint of sheer hard work and diligence.
explanation: ‘By dint of’ is the correct phrase that means by means of something. Similarly, the given sentence states that he passed the exams by means of hard work. Hence, the preposition ‘with’ must be replaced with ‘by’ & ‘by dint of’ becomes the most appropriate answer.

text: These experiments had been going on since several months.
explanation: The given sentence is in ‘Past perfect continuous tense (Sub. + had been + V1-ing + obj. + since/for + time)’. We generally use ‘since’ to denote a point of time and ‘for’ to denote a period of time. Hence, ‘For several months’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Every Saturday, your mother prepares a pudding, isn’t she ?
explanation: According to the “Question Tag rule”, if the statement is positive, the question tag will be negative & Vice-versa. However, the sentence and the question tag must be in the same tense. The given sentence is in simple present tense. So the same tense will be used for the question tag. The given sentence is positive so the question tag will be negative (doesn’t). Hence, ‘doesn’t she’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The people living in coastal areas were evacuated by time.
explanation: Phrase ‘By time’ will be replaced by ‘On time’ as both the phrases look similar but have different meanings. ‘On time’ means at a specific time and ‘By time’ means at the time. Hence, ‘On time’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The gentleman had a suitcase full with wigs, ornaments and dresses.
explanation: ‘Full with’ will be replaced with ‘Full of’ as the phrase ‘Full of’ means completely, including the whole of something. Hence, ‘A suitcase full of’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: You should tell these children to complete their projects himself.
explanation: There is an error of pronoun in the given sentence. The reflexive pronoun ‘Himself’ must be replaced with ‘Themselves’ as there is a plural subject ‘children’ in the sentence. Hence, ‘Their projects themselves’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Open your books at page tenth.
explanation: 'Tenth’ must be replaced with ‘Ten’ as the word ‘Tenth’ is used to denote the position of something and the word ‘Ten’ is used to denote the number. Hence, ‘page ten’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Scarcely had he took the medicine when his headache was gone.
explanation: We generally use (V3) with the helping verb ‘Has/have/had’. Hence, ‘Taken the medicine’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Contented people seldom complaint against their fate.
explanation: ‘Complaint’ will be replaced with ‘Complain’ as we need a verb to make the sentence grammatically correct. Hence, ‘seldom complain’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If you study hard, you surely got selected for the scholarship.
explanation: The given sentence is the first conditional sentence and the correct grammatical structure is (If + simple present tense , Simple future tense). Hence ‘You surely will get selected’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It turned out to be the noisy park party anybody had ever attended.
explanation: Pinnacle Spot the Error ‘Superlative degree’ denotes the form of an adjective or adverb that expresses the highest or a very high degree of quality of a thing, person etc. For example, most, best, worst, greatest, etc. However, we always place the definite article ‘the’ before any superlative adjective. Similarly, in the given sentence, we need to use superlative degree. Hence, ‘The most noisy park party’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The mall just opened and the visitors arrived now.
options: The mall has just opened and the visitors have arrived.
The mall has just been opening and the visitors arrived.
The mall just opens and the visitors arrives.
The mall is just opening and the visitors are arriving.
explanation: The mall has just opened and the visitors have arrived. The given sentence must be in present tense as the adverb ‘Now’ refers to the present time. So, we will use ‘Present perfect tense(Have + V3)’ to make the sentence grammatically correct. Hence, option (a) is the most appropriate answer.

text: After the thieves / had left, / George crept slow / out of his room.
explanation: ‘Slow’ must be replaced with ‘Slowly’ as we need an adverb to describe the verb ‘crept’, not an adjective ‘Slow’. Hence, ‘George crept slowly’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The reduced air pressure on airline flights can lessen the amount of oxygen in passengers' blood for twenty-five percent.
options: The reduced air pressure on airline flights
in passengers' blood for twenty-five percent
can lessen the amount of oxygen
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘for’ must be replaced with ‘to’ because we generally use the preposition ‘to’ after the verb ‘lessen’. Hence, ‘lessen the amount of oxygen in passengers' blood to twenty-five percent’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Marine vertebrates are / valuable for / many reasons.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Sometimes I act / like a fool, and she has / to step into save me.
options: like a fool and she has
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘into’ must be replaced with ‘in’ because ‘step in’ is the correct phrase which means to help somebody in a difficult situation like she helps the narrator in the given sentence. Pinnacle Spot the Error Hence, ‘she has to step in to save me’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: A man tends to one / of the horses after it’s / training at a stud farm.
explanation: “It's” is a contraction and should be used where a sentence normally reads "it is", the apostrophe(‘s) indicates that part of a word has been removed like “It's raining’- is a contraction of - It is raining. Whereas, “Its” with no apostrophe(‘s) is the possessive form of the pronoun ‘it’ which means belonging to it like the dog hurt its tail. Similarly in the given sentence, training is of a man. Hence, ‘the horses after its’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Concern above rising pollution / led to the / formulation of / various action plans.
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘above’ must be replaced with ‘about’ because the verb ‘concern’ generally takes the preposition ‘about’. Hence, ‘Concern about rising pollution’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I am dealing with / some family issues / right now.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: But this immortality / will have purchased / at the price of / his immortal part.
explanation: The verb ‘been’ is missing from the given sentence. Hence, ‘will have been purchased’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Residents should keep an / eye out for strangers / acting suspecting in their areas.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adverb to modify the verb(acting). Hence, ‘acting suspiciously in their areas’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Elizabeth beat her rival with the gold medal in the 2021 summer Olympics.
options: with the gold medal in the
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘with’ must be replaced with ‘for’. Hence, ‘for the gold medal’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: India has joined / the global fight / among tax evasion.
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘among’ must be replaced with ‘against’ because we generally use the preposition ‘against’ after the verb ‘fight’. Hence, ‘against tax evasion’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We usually sleep in bedrooms with the door firmly shuted behind us.
explanation: The given sentence is in the simple present tense so the verb must be used in the simple present form(V1). Hence, ‘firmly shut(V1)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Hundreds of migrants work in private firms in Erode.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Scientists have made dramatic progress in understanding an universe and the mechanisms of biology.
explanation: The ‘universe’ mentioned in the given sentence is specific and we generally use the definite article ‘the’ before any specific or particular noun. Hence, ‘in understanding the universe’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The panel will / investigate the allegations / owing to the concerned officials.
explanation: The phrase ‘owing to’ must be replaced with ‘against’ because we generally use the preposition ‘against’ after the noun ‘allegation’. Hence, ‘allegations against the concerned officials’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He got afflicted with the disease / when he was / a teenager.
options: He got afflicted with the disease
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: I have watched a lot of students excel in online courses, taking fully advantage of the convenience.
options: excel in online courses, taking fully
I have watched a lot of students
explanation: The given sentence needs the adjective ‘full’ to describe the noun ‘advantage’. Hence, ‘excel in online courses, taking full’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Sometimes we interact to people who are closed-minded and not willing to listen.
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘to’ must be replaced with ‘with’ because we generally use the preposition ‘with’ with the verb ‘interact’. Hence, ‘interact with people who are closed-minded’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: New fashion trends / come onto the / scene periodically.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Most of the families in / my research rely at phone calls / for almost all of their communication.
options: for almost all of their communication
my research rely at phone calls
explanation: We generally use the preposition ‘on’ after the verb ‘rely’ and not ‘at’. Hence, ‘my research rely on phone calls’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My friend Jatin usually wears a spectacle.
explanation: Some things are always written in pairs such as a pair of binoculars, a pair of scissors, a pair of spectacles, etc. Similarly, the given sentence talks about wearing spectacles. Hence, ‘a pair of spectacles’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: A tiger’s skull / is similar / to / a lion.
explanation: We generally use apostrophe(‘s) to show possession means something belonging to someone. Similarly, the given sentence talks about a skull which belongs to a lion. Hence, ‘a lion’s’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mylar balloons cause power outages when they come of contact with power lines.
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘of’ must be replaced with ‘in’. Hence, ‘when they come in contact’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Most of the carbon-trapping mechanisms/ that we have identified are/based at limit studies.
options: Most of the carbon - trapping mechanics
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘at’ must be replaced with ‘on’. Hence, ‘based on limited studies’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: There is no denying / that our country is in / an major economic slump.
explanation: the words starting with a Consonant(B,D,F,N,etc.) for example, a dirty shirt, a neglected department, etc. However, the article ‘an’ is used before words starting with a Vowel(A,E,I,O,U) or a Vowel Sound for example, an educated person, an honest policy, etc. Hence, ‘in a major(starting with a consonant) economic slump’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Her comfort was in her children;/ her second son, Rupert,/ was especially dear to her.
options: Her comfort was in her children
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Businesses are asking employees to work from home.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Surgical strike is not the only solution to this problem standing at front of us.
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘at’ must be replaced with ‘in’. Hence, ‘standing in front of us’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I initially thought of including both the mother and the child, but the woman was reluctant to have their pictures take.
options: both the mother and the child, but the woman
was reluctant to have their pictures take
explanation: “Have + V3(third form of the verb)” is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. Hence, ‘was reluctant to have their pictures taken(V3)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In the delicacy and elaborateness / of its ornament, it is the / more splendid church in Italy.
options: of its ornament it is the
explanation: ‘Superlative degree adjective’ denotes the form of an adjective or adverb that expresses the highest or a very high degree of quality of a thing, person, etc. For example, best, worst, greatest, etc. However, we always place the definite article ‘the’ before any superlative adjective. Similarly, in the given sentence, ‘most’ will be the superlative degree adjective. Hence, ‘the most splendid church in Italy’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If your kids sleep well, they are likely to behave better.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: His successful as a lawyer / grew so fast that he soon had / enough money to buy a house.
options: grew so fast that he soon had
enough money to buy a house
explanation: We will replace the adjective(successful) with the noun(success) to grammatically correct the given sentence. Hence, ‘His success as a lawyer’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Soon or later, our efforts will be rewarded.
explanation: We must use the same degree of adjective before and after the conjunction ‘or’. Similarly, a comparative degree adjective(later) is used after the conjunction ‘or’ in the given sentence, so the adjective to be used before it must be in the comparative degree(sooner). Hence, ‘sooner or later’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Rahul sings / very sweet / when he is / in a good mood.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adverb to modify the verb(sings) and not an adjective(sweet). Hence, ‘Rahul sings very sweetly’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: After / a long and fun-filled day, / the children / slept themselves peacefully.
explanation: The use of the reflexive pronoun ‘themselves’ is incorrect according to the grammatical context of the given sentence so it must be removed. Hence, ‘slept peacefully’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The river / flowed besides / the hillock / in our village.
explanation: ‘Besides’ means in addition to something & ‘Beside’ means next to something. Similarly, the given sentence states that the river flowed next to the hillock in our village. Hence, ‘flowed beside’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He has been / excused by the teacher / by the time a formal complaint / for bullying was made.
options: by the time a formal complaint
explanation: “By the time + V2(second form of the verb), Had + V3(third form of the verb)” is grammatically the correct structure for the given sentence. Hence, ‘He had been excused(V3)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Ronaldo is / a famous / player of / the football.
explanation: The definite article 'the' is not used before some words(nouns) like Jail, prison, school, football, cricket, etc. because these nouns are non-specific in the general sense. Hence, ‘player of football’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Whenever he is / on a holiday, / he travels by foot / to the temple nearby.
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘by’ must be replaced with ‘on’ because whenever we go somewhere using our foot we use the preposition ‘on’ before ‘foot’. Hence, ‘he travels on foot’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Me and my friends / often go / to the cinema / together.
explanation: We always put the second person before the first person in a positive sentence according to the order of pronouns. Similarly, in the given sentence, narrator(I) is the first person & his ‘friends’ is the second person. Hence, ‘My friends & I’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It was / the very well-directed film / and we enjoyed it.
explanation: The ‘film’ mentioned in the given sentence is not specific and we generally use the indefinite article ‘a’ before a non-specific noun. Hence, ‘a very well directed’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If the economy fails / this year it reflect badly / on the government.
explanation: The given sentence is a conditional sentence which has a futuristic sense so the verb used must be in the future tense(will). Hence, ‘it will reflect badly’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We stayed / in Jim’s flat / during he was / on holiday.
explanation: ‘When’ is used for talking about the time at which something happens or happened. The given sentence talks about the time at which Jim was on holiday. Hence, ‘when he was’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The unseasonal rain/ caused a lot of damage/ to the crops.
How many / eggs were put / into the basket ?
We have / not met / some of our friends / since six months.
explanation: ‘For’ refers to a specific period of time or a numerical value of time, for example for 2 years, for 4 weeks, for 3 days, etc. However, in the given question, the period of time is 6 months. Hence, ‘for six months’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The policeman asked / many people but / no one was knowing / how the accident happened.
explanation: The given sentence is in the simple past tense so the verb must be used in its past form(V2) and not in the past continuous form(was +V-ing). Hence, ‘no one knew(V2)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This question / is quite too / simple for me / to answer.
explanation: The use of ‘quite’ is irrelevant in the grammatical context of the given sentence as ‘too…to’ is a fixed pair. Hence, ‘is too simple for me to answer’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The manager said, “Could you please confirm me whether you have received all the items that you had ordered?”
explanation: The use of the pronoun ‘me’ is grammatically incorrect in the given sentence so it must be removed. Hence, ‘confirm whether you’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We thought / there was a good idea / to wear snow boots / before we stepped out.
explanation: ‘Idea’ in the given sentence is a singular subject and for it, we will use ‘it’ as a singular pronoun and not ‘there’. Hence, ‘it was a good idea’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: There have been /three breaks-in /in our society/ this month.
explanation: ‘Break-in’ is a phrasal verb which means to enter a building by force, usually in order to steal something. However, the given sentence talks about three attempts so we will use the plural form of ‘break-in’. Hence, ‘three break-ins’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The Taj Mahal / is one of / the most beautiful / creation in the world.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, ‘One of/ Each of/ Most of/ None of + Plural Subject” is grammatically the correct structure. Similarly, the given sentence will have ‘creations’ as a plural subject. Hence, ‘creations in the world’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This park is / the largest bird sanctuary / in the State.
I was angry / on myself / for making / such a silly mistake.
explanation: ‘Angry with someone’ is grammatically the correct phrase for the given sentence. Hence, ‘angry with myself’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We bought / two dozens / mangoes from / the market
explanation: We never write ‘dozens’ if we are using a numerical amount like two, three, etc. before it. For example, ‘two dozens of bananas’ is incorrect but ‘three dozen of mangoes’ is correct. Similarly, the given sentence has ‘two’ as a numerical value. Hence, ‘two dozen’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: You and I / have submitted / your work / on time.
explanation: ‘Our’ is the possessive form of ‘we’ and it means something belonging to us(more than a single person). Similarly in the given sentence, the work belongs to both the persons and not to a single person. Hence, ‘our work’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: Shall / we go / for walking / in the park?
explanation: When we use verbs like walk, talk, ride, drink, etc. as nouns, we put the indefinite article ‘a’ before them as per their sound. For example, we had a talk, let's go for a drive, etc. Hence, ‘for a walk’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Among you and me / she is quite rude / to the boy.
explanation: We use ‘among’ for more than two persons and ‘between’ for two persons. However, there are two persons mentioned in the given sentence. Hence, ‘Between you and me’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I find that / I get myself tired / very easily / these days.
explanation: The use of the reflexive pronoun ‘myself’ is irrelevant according to the grammatical context of the sentence so it will be removed. Hence, ‘I get tired’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If you have / remained calm / you could have / saved the situation.
explanation: If you have “If + had + V3 …. could have + V3(third form of the verb)” is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. Hence, ‘If you had’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I will spend / my rest of remaining / life in my / native village.
explanation: We cannot use ‘rest’ & ‘remaining’ together in a sentence as it becomes the case of superfluousness(not necessary). Hence, ‘remaining’ will be removed from the sentence & ‘the rest of my life’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This dog seems / to be very ferocious, / otherwise, / it is harmless.
explanation: ‘Otherwise‘ is a conjunction that means apart from that. However, ‘But’ is also a conjunction that is used for introducing an idea that contrasts with or is different from what has just been said. Similarly in the given sentence, the statement that the dog is harmless contrasts with its characteristic of being ferocious(violent). Hence, ‘But’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The girl lay down / on the bed / besides her mother / and went to sleep.
explanation: ‘Besides’ means ‘in addition to something’ & ‘Beside’ means ‘at the side of, or next to somebody/something’. However, the given sentence states that the girl lay down on the bed next to her mother and went to sleep. Hence, ‘beside her mother’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He went / to the bed / with a / slight fever.
explanation: We generally use the phrases ‘go to bed’, ‘gone to bed’ or ‘went to bed’. Hence, we will remove the definite article ‘the’ from the given sentence and ‘went to bed’ becomes the most appropriate answer.

text: The city turned out / to be very / different to what / he had expected.
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘to’ after ‘different’ must be replaced with ‘from’ because ‘different’ generally takes the preposition ‘from’ with it. Hence, ‘different from what’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Your name / precedes before / mine / in the list.
explanation: We cannot write ‘precedes’ and ‘before’ together in a sentence as they have similar meanings & that will become a case of superfluousness(not necessary). Hence, ‘before’ must be removed from the sentence to make it grammatically correct.

text: You should / avail this opportunity / to demonstrate / your skills.
explanation: ‘Avail’ always takes the preposition ‘of’ and a reflexive pronoun(myself, yourself, ourselves, etc.) in accordance with the given subject(You). Hence, ‘avail yourself of this opportunity’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He was unable / to help me because / he had been failed / to arrange the money.
explanation: The given sentence is in the simple past tense so the verb must be used in its simple past form(failed) and not in the past perfect form(had been failed). Hence, ‘he failed’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He often / persists to ask / awkward questions / at the board meetings.
explanation: “Persist + in + V-ing” is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. Hence, the preposition ‘to’ must be replaced with the preposition ‘in’ and ‘persists in asking(V-ing)’ becomes the most appropriate answer.

text: His son-in-laws / have enhanced / his business / within a short period.
explanation: We can never write ‘in-laws’ because it is incorrect to add ‘s’ in Pinnacle Spot the Error the suffix(of law). However, we generally write son-in-law for a single male and sons-in-law for more than one male. Similarly, the given sentence talks about two males. Hence, ‘His sons-in-law’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Either of these / two roads / lead to / the post office.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, ‘Either of/ Neither of + Plural Subject + Singular verb’ is grammatically the correct structure. The given sentence has ‘Roads’ as a plural subject and ‘leads’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘leads to’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: His father / prevented him / to go abroad / for higher studies.
explanation: We generally use the preposition ‘from’ with prevent not ‘to’. Hence, we will replace ‘to’ with ‘from’ and ‘from going abroad’ becomes the most appropriate answer.

text: What is the name / of the Swami / whom autobiography / impressed you so much?
explanation: 'Whom' is an object pronoun that refers to the person who was the recipient of an action. However, 'Whose' is a possessive pronoun that refers to the person to whom something belongs. Similarly, the given sentence refers to a Swami to whom the autobiography belongs. Hence, ‘whose autobiography’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The crowd of the migrant worker at the station for the Shramik Special is unforgettable.
explanation: ‘Crowd’ means a large number of people in one place and these people are migrant workers(not a single worker) in the given sentence. However, it is irrelevant to use the definite article ‘the’ as the workers are not specific. Hence, ‘of migrant workers’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Will you / listen me / when I tell you / the details?
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘to’ is missing after ‘listen’. Hence, ‘listen to me’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The crow held back / to the piece / of bread / with its claws.
explanation: ‘Held back’ means to not do something & ‘held on’ means to maintain a grasp on something.Both are phrasal verbs. Similarly, in the given sentence, the crow grasps the piece of bread with its claws. Hence, ‘the crow held on’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The farmer is / cutting the corn / which has ripen / in the fields.
explanation: ‘Has + V3’ is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. However, the V3 form of ‘ripen’ is ‘ripened’. Hence, ‘has ripened’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Obi wanted / to continue on / his idea of / building a modern school.
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. Use the preposition ‘on’ in place of ‘with’. Hence, ‘to continue with’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I was watching a whole scene very carefully.
explanation: The subject ‘whole scene’ is specific & before specific or particular nouns, we use the definite article ‘the’. Hence, ‘the whole scene’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Who has distributed these sweets among the children?
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Mr. Choudhri goes to fly to Germany and France next weekend.
explanation: The given sentence talks about a future action(next weekend), . The structure ‘is going to’ is generally used for future actions. Hence, ‘Mr. Choudhri is going to’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Not get into the car; it has not been cleaned inside.
explanation: The given sentence must start with a verb ‘do’ which is missing. Hence, ‘Do not get’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The man we met was any other than the original owner of the house.
explanation: The phrase ‘any other’ will be replaced with ‘different’ which means not the same person. Hence, ‘was different than’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: “You can meet me always you like,” our teacher told us.
explanation: The word ‘always’ must be replaced with an adverb ‘anytime’ to grammatically correct the given sentence.

text: There is no one else in this house; I can feel the presence.
explanation: If one can feel the presence, it is obvious that there is someone present. Hence, ‘no one’ will be replaced with ‘someone’ to make the given sentence grammatically correct.

text: You look very tired; you would go to bed now.
explanation: There is a modal verb error in the given sentence. The modal verb ‘would’ must be replaced with ‘should’ as the sentence is showing a sense of suggestion. Hence, ‘you should go’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The little baby cried loudly to a new toy.
explanation: ‘Cry for something’ is a phrase that means to express a want or need through crying. Similarly in the given sentence, the child is expressing his need for the toy through crying. Hence, ‘for a toy’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This is the place here Sudhir found the wallet full of money.
explanation: ‘Where’ means in or to what place or position. The given sentence talks about a place where Sudhir found the wallet full of money. Hence, ‘where’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Although we took all precautions but we were unable to avoid getting caught in the heavy rain.
options: Although we took all precautions but
explanation: The ‘precautions’ mentioned in the given sentence are specific & we use the definite article ‘the’ before specific or particular nouns. We need not use the conjunction “but” as the word “although’ at the beginning of the sentence shows the contrast. Hence, ‘Although we took all the precautions ’ is the most appropriate answer. Correct sentence- Although we took all the precautions we were unable to avoid getting caught in the heavy rain.

text: I’m sure that I found the place without any difficulty when I go next time.
explanation: The given sentence shows an action of future tense(next time) so the verb must be used in its future form(will) and not in the past form(found). Hence, ‘I will find the place’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Asking for and giving informations is an important feature of conversations.
explanation: Some Nouns like Cattle, work, Information, Scenery, Furniture, etc. are always written in the singular form so we can't make their plural form. For example, ‘furniture’ is correct but ‘furnitures’ is incorrect. Similarly in the given sentence, ‘informations’ will be replaced with ‘information’.

text: Every country tries to do its good at the Olympic games as they are held in great prestige.
explanation: Replace “its good” by “well”. Good' is an adjective like a good boy, a good book, etc & 'Well' is an adverb like, He performed well. Similarly, in the given sentence, we need an adverb to modify the verb 'do'. Hence, 'well' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Judy solved the difficult problem by her own without anyone’s help.
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘by’ must be replaced with ‘on’. Hence, ‘on her own’ is the most appropriate structure. “On her own” means by herself and unaided.

text: You must avoid riding in a crowded bus / or travelling in a metro / during rush hour / as both are quiet unpleasant experiences.
options: You must avoid riding in a crowded bus
as both are quiet unpleasant experiences
explanation: Quiet is an adjective that means with very little or no noise & ‘Quite’ is an adverb that is used for emphasizing something. However, the given sentence does not talk about any sound or noise. Hence, ‘both are quite unpleasant experiences’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: Won’t you / please come / to help me / along this heavy box?
explanation: The phrase “Would/Will/Can you help me with this______” is grammatically the correct structure that we use when we ask someone for help in doing something. Similarly, in the given sentence, the narrator is asking someone to help him/her lift a heavy bag. Hence, ‘with this heavy box’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: The construction of the new business school is led to a sudden rise of population in our area.
options: a sudden rise of population in our area
explanation: The given sentence is in the present perfect tense so the verb must be used in its present perfect form(has) and not in the present/base form(is). Hence, ‘has led to’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: When she went for a walk / Maya couldn't take off her scarf / because it was / too much windy.
options: Maya couldn't take off her scarf
When she went for a walk
explanation: We use "too much" before uncountable nouns like too much money(uncountable), too much milk, etc. However, "too many" is used before countable nouns like too many shoes(countable), too many books, etc. But, in the given sentence, ‘windy’ is not a noun it is an adjective. So, we will remove ‘much’ before ‘windy’. Hence, either ‘too windy’ or ‘too much wind(noun)’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: We don't really / want a large house; / we are looking for some comfort / and some convenience on a moderate price.
options: and some convenience on a moderate price
we are looking for some comfort
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘on’ will be replaced with ‘at’ because we generally buy something at a low/high price, not on a low/high price. Hence, ‘some convenience at a moderate price’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: Lalitha will go / to sister’s house / in Mumbai / this summer.
explanation: There is a pronoun error in the given sentence. The possessive pronoun ‘her’ that is generally used for a female subject(Lalitha in the given sentence) is missing. Hence, ‘to her sister’s house’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: Several prominent film stars / have appeared on television / on behalf of awareness / about hand hygiene.
explanation: The phrase ‘on behalf of the’ means as a representative of someone or something. However, in the given sentence, article ‘the’ is missing from the phrase. Hence, ‘on behalf of the awareness’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: The concept became / too much clear to me / after my tutor / showed me the diagram.
explanation: The use of the phrase ‘too much’ is not necessary for the sentence because it is used before uncountable nouns like too much money and ‘clear’ is not a noun. Hence, ‘became clearer to me’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: The balloon flew up / as soon as / the man cutting the string.
explanation: The given sentence is in the past tense(flew) so the verb must be used in its simple past form(cut) and not in the present continuous form(cutting). Hence, ‘the man cut the string ’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: Mithila art tradition is passed on / from one generation through a next / by children watching and helping / their mothers and grandmothers.
options: from one generation through a next
Mithila art tradition is passed on
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘through’ must be replaced with ‘to’. Hence, ‘from one generation to the next’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: Electric heaters were providing to all the officers at the guest house.
explanation: The given sentence is in the passive voice so the verb must be used in its past form(provided) and not in the continuous form(providing). Hence, ‘were provided’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: Einstein’s school teachers thought he would never success in life.
explanation: Succeed is a verb that means to manage to achieve what you want. But, success is a noun. However, the given sentence needs a verb. Hence, ‘never succeed’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: That man would have attacked you, if you went that way.
explanation: “If + sub + Had + V3 …….would have + V3” is grammatically the correct structure for the given sentence. Hence, ‘If you had gone’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: The government has announced a gradual reboot of air travel who was halted two months ago due to lockdown.
explanation: Replace “who” with “which”. In the given sentence, the halting of air travel due to lockdown was specific. Hence, ‘which was halted’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: Keep looking, and / you are sure to find the meaning / of the word on that page.
options: of the word on that page
you are sure to find the meaning
explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Most hotels / offer for their guests / complimentary breakfast / during their stay there.
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The use of ‘for’ after ‘offer’ is irrelevant so it should be removed. Hence, ‘most hotels offer their guests complimentary breakfast’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: I'm sorry, sir. / How many is / the fine for / returning the books late?
explanation: ‘Many’ is used for countable nouns, for example how many apples. However, ‘much’ is used for uncountable nouns for example how much money, how much rice, etc. Similarly in the given sentence, fine is uncountable. Hence, ‘how much is the fine for?’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: At the workshop, / they were taught how to nail / the pieces of wood together to create toys.
options: they were taught how to nail
the pieces of wood together to create toys
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: A probe has been ordered / by the incident / that occurred at the celebrations.
explanation: ‘Probe into’ a correct phrase meaning(To begin inquiring into or investigating something). The correct sentence will be as follows: A probe has been ordered into the incident that occurred at the celebrations.

text: If you rent a house near your office, it will save you time as well as also money.
explanation: ‘As well as’ is a conjunction that means in addition. It connects two nouns, pronouns etc. to each other. So, use only ‘money’ in place of ‘also money’.The conjunction 'as well as' is not immediately followed by ' also'.Hence the correct sentence will be as : If you rent a house near your office, it will save you time as well as money.

text: Notwithstanding we were / all busy that weekend / we had to / cancel the outing.
explanation: “Notwithstanding” means “despite or in spite of something” . It is used to indicate an aspect of contrast. So, ‘Notwithstanding’ will be replaced by ‘as’ to make the sentence grammatically correct.

text: Every participant gave so outstanding performance that it became difficult to choose the winner.
explanation: Such is used for emphasizing the degree of something. The given sentence tells about a performance of outstanding degree. Hence, ‘so outstanding performance’ will be replaced by ‘such an outstanding performance’ to grammatically correct the given sentence.

text: The need today is for both sides / to introspect and re-examine the issue carefully / and resolve it amicably.
options: to introspect and re-examine the issue carefully
The need today is for both sides
explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Only five minutes / are allowed / for each speaker / during the function.
explanation: The compound nouns (numerical + noun) are not used as the plural if a noun does the work as an adjective. Here replace ‘are’ with ‘is’ to make the sentence grammatically correct.

text: You need to sign / these important documents / by ink.
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. The preposition ‘by’ must be replaced with ‘in’ because we generally write ‘in ink’ for example fill the form in blue ink, sign the cheque in ink, etc. Similarly, in the given sentence, the documents need to be signed in ink. Hence, ‘in ink’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: She speaks / very highly / of both her / daughter-in-laws.
explanation: We can never write ‘-in-laws’ because adding ‘s’ in the suffix(in-law) is wrong. However, we write daughter-in-law for a single female and daughters-in-law for more than two females. Similarly, the given sentence talks about two daughters-in-law. Hence, ‘daughters-in-law’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: His loyalty / and honesty / are above / suspect.
explanation: The phrase ‘above suspicion’ is used to describe someone who would never be suspected of doing anything wrong. Similarly, the given sentence states that his honesty and loyalty are above suspicion. Hence, ‘suspicion’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: Parul is / ten years / elder than / her sibling.
explanation: The comparative degree ‘elder’ will not be used with ‘than’ because it will become a case of superfluousness(not necessary). Hence, ‘than’ will be replaced with ‘to’ and ‘elder to’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: He is / afraid from / all insects / that crawl.
explanation: Afraid generally takes the preposition ‘of’ and not ‘from’. Hence, ‘afraid of’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: He wanted to know / the reason / why his low score / in Mathematics.
explanation: If an Interrogative sentence(in which a question is asked) is written in the Indirect form(speech), then “Wh-word(why, when, where) + Subject + Verb” is grammatically the correct structure for it. Hence, ‘why his(subject) score was(verb) low’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: This is / only mistake / he has made / in the dictation.
explanation: The article ‘the’ is used to refer to specific or particular nouns & articles ‘a/an’ are used to modify non-specific or non-particular nouns. For example, if someone says, "Let's buy the book," it means a specific book but if someone says, "Let's buy a book," it means any book rather than a specific book. Similarly, the given sentence talks about a specific mistake. Hence, ‘the only mistake’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: I am hearing a strange noise now.
explanation: Stative verbs are those verbs which express a state of condition. They do not refer to a physical action. Sense and emotions like hear, smell, see, love, hate etc are different types of stative verbs. However, these verbs can’t be used in (-ing form) for example, Hear, Smell(Correct) and Hearing, Smelling(Incorrect). Hence, ‘I hear a strange noise’ will be the answer.

text: All of us were a little nervous when we came into this room today.
options: when we came into this room today
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Do you earn so much to make both ends meet?
explanation: The phrase ‘so much’ is used to mention a definite unknown quantity and ‘much’ is used with uncountable nouns. However, when we ask about someone’s earning, we usually ask how much you earn and not how ‘so much’ you earn. Hence, ‘Do you earn much’ will be the correct sentence structure.

text: You cannot lead a healthy life although you stop smoking.
explanation: It is a conditional sentence which has two conditions and starts with a negative sense(cannot). It says one cannot lead a healthy life, one does not quit smoking. Unless is a negative conditional conjunction which means ‘If___not’ and it is used to combine these two conditions. Hence, Unless will replace although.

text: I had to hold on to the wall to steady itself or I could have fallen.
explanation: According to the context of the sentence, the reflexive pronoun ‘myself’ will replace ‘itself’ because the subject(noun)/the narrator is a human being and for living things we use ‘myself’. Hence, ‘to steady myself’ will be the correct sentence structure.

text: The jury are from different parts of the country.
explanation: Jury/Team/Committee are considered as a singular subject and will take a singular verb, until they are divided in their opinion/views. For example, the Jury(Singular subject) has given its decision(United) , the committee(Plural subject) are divided in their opinion(Divided). Similarly in the given question, ‘the jury is(singular verb) from different parts of the country’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: She picked up the books lie on the table and put them on the shelf.
explanation: Lying is a non-finite verb which is acting as an adjective for the books in the given sentence. Hence, ‘Books lying on the table’ will be the correct sentence structure.

text: He is over eighty and dare not read without glasses.
explanation: Dare means to challenge someone for something. According to the context of the sentence, we have to show the inability of the person to see and for ability/inability, we will use ‘can’ and not dare. Hence, ‘cannot read’ will be the correct sentence structure. Pinnacle Sentence Improvement SENTENCE IMPROVEMENT Direction :- [

text: Identify the errors in the given sentence and choose the sentence that rectifies these errors. I have known her for many years. This time, she took unusual decision in unprejudiced way.
options: I have known her for many years. This time, she took an unusual decision in a unprejudiced way.
I have known her for many years. This time, she took an unusual decision in an unprejudiced way.
I have known her for many years. This time, she took a unusual al decision decision in in an unprejudiced way.
I have known her for many years. This time, she took unusual decision in an unprejudiced way.
explanation: unusual decision in an unprejudiced way. Article ‘an’ is used before words starting with a vowel sound (an apple, an umbrella, an American). Similarly, in the given sentence, the words ‘unusual’ and ‘unprejudiced’ start with a vowel sound. Hence, the sentence given in option (b) is correct.

text: My mom made her muffins, but she didn't eat none.
explanation: ‘None’ is not used in a negative sentence. ‘None’ must be replaced with ‘any’ as we use ‘any’ in a negative sentence. Hence, “she didn’t eat any” is the most appropriate answer.

text: Identify the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the given options. Tide pool is a isolated pocket of water that is formed when sea water becomes trapped as tide goes out.
options: A tide pool is a isolated pocket of water that is formed when sea water becomes trapped as a tide goes out.
A tide pool is an isolated pocket of water that is formed when sea water becomes trapped as the tide goes out.
Tide pool is isolated pocket of water that is formed when sea water becomes trapped as a tide goes out.
The tide pool is isolated pocket of water that is formed when sea water becomes trapped as tide goes out.
explanation: when sea water becomes trapped as the tide goes out. Indefinite article ‘a/an’ is used when we talk about a noun in general. Similarly, the given sentence talks about ‘tide pool’ and ‘isolated pocket’ in a general sense. We will use article ‘a’ before ‘tide’ (consonant sound) and article ‘an’ before ‘isolated’(vowel sound). Article ‘the’ will be used before the 2nd ‘tide’. Hence, the sentence given in option (b) is correct.

text: He behaves if he were a king.
explanation: ‘As if’ is used to talk about a situation that may not be true but that is possible. Similarly, in the given sentence, the person may not be a king but he behaves like a king. Hence, ‘behaves as if’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: What do you like to do on your free days other than to watching movies?
explanation: We use a noun, pronoun or a gerund(Ving) after the phrase ‘other than’. Therefore, ‘to’ will be removed. Hence, ‘watching(Ving) movies’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the correct version of the following sentence. He would be meet us next week.
options: He would be meets us next week.
He would not be met us next week.
He will be meet us next week.
He will be meeting us next week.
explanation: The given sentence is in the future continuous tense and follows the structure, “Third person pronoun + will + be + Ving”. Hence, the sentence given in option (d) is correct.

text: While I was waiting for Asha for shopping, I spilled lemonade on my new trousers
explanation: Infinitive(to + V1) is used after the verb ‘wait’. Therefore, ‘for shopping’ must be replaced with ‘to shop(V1)’. Hence, ‘to shop’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Whether she wishes to relocate to Mumbai or continues to live here are her personal decisions.
explanation: ‘Whether … or’ is a pair of conjunctions. According to the “Rule of Proximity”, the verb is supplied according to the subject closest Pinnacle Sentence Improvement to the verb. In the given sentence, the close subject is a verb phrase ‘continues to live’, which denotes a single action. Therefore, singular verb ‘is’ will be used. Hence, ‘is her personal decision’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He gave his heart and soul to make the entire show a success.
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute (replace) the bracketed segment in the following sentence. I look forward (see) you soon.
explanation: There are some phrases that are always followed by a gerund(Ving). Such phrases are ‘with a view to, looking forward to, in addition to, accustomed to, habituated to, be used to, prone to, etc.’ Hence, ‘look forward to seeing’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Harish is clever than wise.
explanation: When we compare two qualities of the same person, the comparative degree is formed by adding ‘more’, not by adding ‘-er’. Hence, ‘more clever than’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The firefighters tried their best to extinguish the fire.
Research in Social Sciences is plagued nowadays on gloomy definitions and measurements.
explanation: ‘By’ is used in passive voice to indicate the doer or agent of the action. Similarly, in the given sentence, ‘by’ has been used to indicate the doer of the action ‘plagued’. Hence, ‘nowadays by gloomy definitions’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Raghav, who studies tourism at present, is planning to go abroad after his graduation.
explanation: Present continuous tense is used to indicate an action that is in progress in the present. ‘Singular Subject + is + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure for it. Hence, ‘is studying’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Placing a huge magnet atop the temple pose to being the biggest hurdle for the masons.
explanation: ‘To + V1’, also known as infinitive, is the correct grammatical structure. The given sentence is in the past tense, therefore, the past form(V2) of the verb will be used. Hence, ‘posed to be’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: One of the most horrified serials of the Indian television industry was broadcast twenty years ago.
explanation: ‘Horrifying’ means causing a feeling of horror. The given sentence states that one of the most horrifying serials of the Indian television industry was broadcast twenty years ago. Hence, ‘most horrifying serials’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Monika said to her mother that, "I have passed the examination."
options: Monika said to her mother that, "I am passed
Monika said to her mother, "I have passed
Monika said to her mother that, "she has passed
explanation: If the reported speech is given in inverted commas(“ ” ), it is called direct speech. However, in the direct speech, we do not use any conjunctions (‘that’, ‘if’, ‘whether’) after the reporting verb (say). Therefore, ‘that’ will be removed from the given sentence. Hence, option (b) is the most appropriate answer.

text: If she had gone to the party, she could have met Amit.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Heba dropped of the club unexpectedly to say hello and catch up.
explanation: The phrasal verb ‘drop by’ means to pay a brief casual visit. The given sentence states that Heba dropped by the club unexpectedly to say hello and catch up. Hence, ‘dropped by the club unexpectedly’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Solving the riddle given by our teacher is farther beyond our capacity.
explanation: Positive degree ‘far’ will be used in this sentence as there is no comparison. Hence, ‘far’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Rohit Sharma is better than more other batsman in the world.
options: as good as the most other batsmen
explanation: ‘More other’ must be replaced with ‘most other’, indicating the majority of other batsmen. Plural noun is used with the adjective ‘other’. The given sentence states that Rohit Sharma is better than the majority of other batsmen in the world. Hence, ‘better than most other batsmen’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: There have been numerous attempts made by the citizens to restore parity.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: The given sentence has an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. India is not on war with Pakistan.
explanation: ‘At war with’ is the correct phrase, which means to be in a situation of war with an enemy nation. Hence, ‘not at’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. The robbers stabbed him by a sharp knife and he started bleeding profusely on the spot.
explanation: ‘With’ is used when there is a physical contact between two things. When a person is stabbed with a knife, the knife enters a person’s body, indicating a physical contact. Hence, ‘with a sharp knife’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The intersection of nature conservation and social justice is evident in efforts to ensure that marginalised communities and other backward classes should have equal access to natural reserves.
explanation: ‘Endeavour’ means an attempt to achieve a goal. ‘Guarantee’ means to ensure that something will happen. The phrase ‘evident in efforts to ensure’ means the same as ‘apparent in endeavours to guarantee’. Hence, ‘apparent in endeavours to guarantee’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I had to choose the best of the two options available.
explanation: ‘Than’ is used when one thing is before the comparative degree and the other comes afterwards. But when we talk about one out of two, ‘of’ is used with comparative degree. The given sentence talks about the one better option out of two options available. Hence, ‘better of’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: After the heavy rains last Thursday, the water in the river raised another three feet.
explanation: ‘Raised’ must be replaced with ‘rose’. ‘Raise’ means to cause something to move upwards. ‘Rose’ means to go upwards or higher. ‘Rose’ is the past form of ‘rise’, indicating simple past tense. Hence, ‘rose another three feet’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Ramgopal is having a very big house in Mumbai.
explanation: ‘Have’ is a stative verb denoting possession. Stative verbs are generally not used in the continuous tense. Rather, we use simple present tense to talk about the present state. ‘Ramgopal’ Pinnacle Sentence Improvement is a singular subject that will take ‘has’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘has’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I have never had and never will be dependent on him.
explanation: In the given sentence, the main verb is ‘be’. With ‘has/have/had’, the third form of the verb is used. The first form of the verb is used with modals (will, shall, can, may, might, could, would, should, must). Hence, ‘never been(V3)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Rahul was angry of his brother as he broke his pen.
explanation: ‘At’ is used with ‘angry’ for a person. ‘Angry at someone’ is the correct phrase. Hence, ‘at’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The pineapple dessert was so delicious that we couldn’t help eat it.
options: so delicious that we couldn’t helping eat it
so that delicious we couldn’t help eating it
so delicious that we couldn’t help eating it
explanation: The phrase “can’t help / couldn’t help” is used when you can not resist doing something. Present participle(Ving) is used after this phrase. Hence, “so delicious that we couldn’t help eating it” is the most appropriate answer.

text: Autumn leaves shuffled beneath him as he wandered through the quiet forest.
explanation: ‘Rustle’ means to make a soft sound, as by moving leaves. ‘Underfoot’ means under your feet as you walk. The given sentence states that autumn leaves rustled underfoot as he wandered through the quiet forest. Hence, ‘rustled underfoot’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If we want to promote national integrity in our country, then we must desist our tendency of taking up with others.
explanation: ‘Taking up with’ must be replaced with the phrasal verb ‘looking down upon’, which means to treat someone as unimportant or not worthy of respect. The given sentence talks about desisting the tendency of looking down upon others. Hence, ‘looking down upon’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: .She confided in me on her anxious, whispering her secrets between sips of coffee.
explanation: Preposition ‘about’ is used to indicate the specific subject or issue. We use a noun after any preposition. ‘Anxiety’ is the correct noun to use here. ‘Anxiety’ means a feeling of worry, nervousness or unease about something. Hence, ‘about her anxiety’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: ‘Spy Family’ is a graphic novel that is a narrative work in which the story is conveyed to the reader using uninterrupted art in a traditional comics format.
explanation: logical order. The given sentence states that ‘Spy Family’ is a graphic novel that is a narrative work in which the story is conveyed to the reader using sequential art in a traditional comics format. Hence, 'sequential art in a traditional' is the most appropriate answer.

text: She has been studying for two o’clock .
explanation: ‘Since’ is used to indicate the point of time when something started. Similarly, the given sentence states the time when she started studying. Hence, “studying since two o’ clock” is the most appropriate answer.

text: Spreading awareness about the rights of the consumers and the relief open to them in case they did not get their money’s worth of goods and service has rightly been identified as the first priority.
options: were unable to get their money’s worth
did not getting their money’s worth
will not get their money’s worth
explanation: The phrase ‘did not get’ means to not be able to get something in the past. ‘Unable’ means to not be able to do something. Hence, “were unable to get their money’s worth” is the most appropriate answer.

text: Pollution levels have increased so largely that they are almost killing us.
explanation: ‘Highly’ means at a high level. The given sentence states that pollution levels have increased so highly that they are almost killing us. Hence, 'highly' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully. (Each participant have) performed well.
explanation: ‘Everyone/each/ every/ nothing/ everything/ anything/ either/ neither’ represents a singular noun. Therefore, singular verbs will be used with them. Hence, ‘Each participant has’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: There are many factories in the operative area of the city.
explanation: ‘Industrial’ means having a lot of factories. The given sentence states that there are many factories in the industrial area of the city. Hence, 'industrial' is the most appropriate answer.

text: I have been living in Hyderabad since I am born .
explanation: ‘Since’ is used to indicate the point of time in the past when something began. Therefore, past tense will be used in the clause beginning with ‘since’. Hence, ‘since I was born’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Rare species of frogs were very quicker identified by Stella.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adverb ‘quickly’ to modify the verb ‘identified’, not an adjective ‘quicker’. Hence, ‘of frogs were very quickly’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He was an irresponsible person to the matter of taking up responsibilities.
options: at the matter of taking up
in the matter of taking up
by the matter of taking up
along the matter of taking up
explanation: ‘In’ is used to indicate a specific situation or circumstance. The given passage states that he was an irresponsible person in the matter of taking up responsibilities. Hence, 'in the matter of taking up' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mayra has the ability for mathematics.
explanation: ‘Aptitude’ means a natural ability to do something. The given sentence states that Mayra has the aptitude for mathematics. Hence, 'aptitude' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the option that can substitute/replace the bracketed word correctly and complete the sentence. They could (always) stay in, or go for a walk.
explanation: ‘Either…or’ is a fixed pair of conjunctions. Hence, ‘either’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Charles Darwin is renowned for his book on evolution, ‘On the Origin of Species’, which laid down a treasure ofsubstantiation that evolution occurs, and projected a mechanism, that is, natural selection, for how it does so.
options: laid into a treasure of substantiation
laid about a treasure of substantiation
laid away a treasure of substantiation
laid out a treasure of substantiation
explanation: ‘Laid out’ means explained or described something in a clear and detailed way. The given sentence states that Charles Darwin is renowned for his book on evolution, ‘On the Origin of Species’, which laid down a treasure of substantiation that evolution occurs. Hence, ‘laid out a treasure of substantiation’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Our legal system must frame proper legal rules for juvenile criminals.
explanation: The given sentence states that our legal system must frame legal rules for young criminals. Hence, ‘young’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The programme on TV was now shown the blurring faces of the inmates of the rehabilitation centre.
options: were now showing the blurred faces of the inmates of the rehabilitation centre.
was now showing the blurred faces of the inmates of the rehabilitation centre
were now showing the blurring faces of the inmates from the rehabilitation centre
was now showing the blurred faces of the inmates upon the rehabilitation centre
explanation: the rehabilitation centre ‘Singular Sub. + was + Ving’ is grammatically the correct structure Pinnacle Sentence Improvement for a sentence which is in the past continuous tense. Hence, ‘was now showing(Ving) the blurred faces of the inmates of the rehabilitation centre’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: When I saw him, I will ask him to return the book he borrowed.
explanation: If ‘when’ is used to denote the time of a future event, it is used in simple present tense. First form of the verb is used with pronoun ‘I’ in the simple present tense. Hence, ‘see(V1) him’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Gourav was no good than a foolish person.
explanation: We use comparative degree with ‘than’ to make comparison. However, ‘better’ is the comparative degree of ‘good’. Hence, ‘no better’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If I was the queen, I would give a handsome sum towards education.
explanation: The phrase ‘If i were’ is generally used in the subjunctive mood to talk about possibilities, wishes, or conditions that are contrary to reality. ‘If I were… (would + V1) / (would have + V3)’ is the correct grammatical structure. Hence, ‘If I were the queen’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Five years later, I was eating this same dish at the same restaurant.
explanation: The given sentence implies that the person ate a dish at a restaurant and five years later, he is eating the same dish at the same restaurant. Therefore, the sentence will be written in simple present tense. Hence, ‘am eating’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Beyond skills, experience, and training, companies search for applicants who display excitement — those they believe shall carry out allocated responsibilities cheerfully and cooperatively.
options: shall take up any designated obligations
should pick up all skills and works
explanation: ‘Execute’ means to carry out fully. ‘Duties’ means responsibility. The given sentence states that beyond skills, experience, and training, companies search for applicants who display excitement — those they believe will execute assigned duties cheerfully and cooperatively. Hence, ‘will execute assigned duties’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The mother asked the child, “Will you tell me who did accompany you to the airport?”
explanation: When a question is part of a sentence, the helping verb is written after the subject, not before the subject. Past form (V2) is used in simple past tense. Hence, ‘who accompanied(V2) you’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Satya is always great to his friends who helped him when he was in trouble.
explanation: ‘Grateful’ means showing appreciation for something done. The given sentence states that Satya is always grateful to his friends who helped him when he was in trouble. Hence, ‘grateful’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The team always anticipate a bowling friendly pitch on their easy victory in the T20 matches.
explanation: ‘For’ is used to indicate the purpose or reason for something. Similarly, the team anticipate a bowling friendly pitch for the purpose of easy victory in the T20 matches. Hence, ‘pitch for their easy victory’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The wedding was put on until January.
explanation: The phrasal verb ‘put off’ means to delay something until a later time. The given sentence states that the wedding was put off until January. Hence, ‘put off’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Everyone called the reporter a daredevil after he came back safely from the war zone.
explanation: fearless person

text: Carnatic music is usually performed by a small troupe of actors, consisting of a principal performer, a melodic accompaniment, and a rhythm accompaniment.
explanation: ‘Ensemble’ means a group of musicians, dancers, or actors who perform together. The given sentence talks about carnatic music, so the correct phrase to use is ‘ensemble of musicians’. Hence, ‘ensemble of musicians’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It is very hard for her to provide the necessities of her family.
explanation: ‘To’ is used to indicate the receiver of an action or object. In the given sentence, ‘her family’ is the receiver of the necessities. Hence, ‘the necessities to her family’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: To the general public, William was best known as a crusader for peace and as an admired critic about social, political and ethical subjects.
options: for peace and as an admired critic by
for peace and as an admired critic on
about peace and as an admired critic about
in peace and as an admired critic about
explanation: ‘On’ is generally used to indicate the topic or subject of discussion. Hence, ‘on’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: No matter how hard work you, your boss will not recognise your efforts.
explanation: ‘Subject + main verb’ is the correct order for the sentence. ‘You’ is the subject and ‘work’ is its main verb. Hence, ‘hard you work’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: As the rulers of the planet, humans like to think that it is the largest creatures that will emerge victorious from the struggle for survival.
options: it is the most large creatures
explanation: ‘Humans’ is a plural noun that will take the plural pronoun ‘they’ and the plural verb ‘are’. Hence, ‘they are the largest creatures’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Experts acknowledged that some counterfeiting of document techniques are virtually impossible to detect.
explanation: ‘Forgery’ means the crime of illegally copying something in order to deceive someone. The given sentence states that experts acknowledged that some forgery techniques are virtually impossible to detect. Hence, ‘forgery’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If it had not rained, they would not postpone the programmes.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of a third conditional sentence and the correct grammatical structure for it is “If + past perfect (had + V3)…….. Would have + V3”. Hence, ‘would not have postponed’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Sivamani is working as an electrician for the past 22 years.
explanation: Perfect continuous tense is used when the time period is given with ‘for/since’. ‘Singular subject + has been + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure for this sentence. Hence, ‘has been working’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Her thinning grey hair was hanging on her bony forehead.
explanation: ‘Straggling over’ means spread out in an irregular way. The given sentence states that her thinning grey hair was spread out irregularly over her bony forehead. Hence, ‘straggling over’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: An intense wish to learn something keeps the nerves active.
explanation: ‘Intense’ means the same as powerful. The given sentence states that a powerful wish to learn something keeps the nerves active. Hence, ‘powerful’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Rohan exercised and ate a lot, lest he should not be weak .
options: lest he would not be weak.
explanation: ‘Not’ will be removed as the use of ‘not’ with ‘lest’ is superfluous. Hence, ‘lest he should be weak’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Bankrupts are those who are incapable to pay their debts
explanation: ‘Incompetent’ means incapable of doing something. The given sentence states that bankrupts are those who are incompetent to pay their debts. Hence, ‘incompetent’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the option that can substitute/replace the bracketed word correctly and complete the sentence. He (seek) for the wallet in his pocket.
explanation: ‘Sought’ is the correct verb to use here. ‘Sought’ is the past form of ‘seek’, indicating simple past tense. Hence, ‘sought’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Do you know where does she reside ?
explanation: When a question is a part of a sentence, the correct structure is “Wh. word + Subject + verb”. ‘She’ is a singular subject that will Pinnacle Sentence Improvement take the singular verb ‘resides’. Hence, ‘where she resides?’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: A computer can’t function without it’s mother board.
explanation: ‘Its’ is a possessive used for things. Here, ‘its’ has been used for a computer. Hence, ‘its’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Transnational linkages, for example, sever the nation-state’s integrity and corrupt state-society relations.
explanation: ‘Cohesion’ means forming a united whole & ‘erode’ means gradually destroy. The given sentence states that transnational linkages, for example, sever the nation-state’s cohesion and erode state-society relations. Hence, ‘cohesion and erode’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: His house is smaller than you .
explanation: The comparison is between two houses, not the house and person. So, we will use a possessive pronoun ‘yours’ instead of ‘you’. Hence, ‘is smaller than yours’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She was foolish enough to think that she be completely safe now.
explanation: The use of the adverb ‘now’ indicates present tense and the present tense form of ‘be’ is ‘is’ for the singular subject (she). Hence, ‘is completely safe’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: No sooner did Mr. Piyahri Mishra finish his chemistry lecture that the students began to leave.
options: so the students began to leave.
then the students began to leave.
and the students began to leave.
than the students began to leave.
explanation: ‘No sooner …than’ is a fixed pair of conjunctions. Therefore, ‘that’ will be replaced with ‘than’. Hence, ‘than the students began to leave’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Sanat has just arrived in Mysore on transfer; he requests his friend Raghu to help him find an appropriate location.
explanation: ‘Rented accommodation’ means a property that is occupied by a tenant who pays rent to the owner, or landlord. The given sentence states that he requests his friend Raghu to help him find a rented accommodation. Hence, 'a rented accommodation' is the most appropriate answer.

text: This book giving us much information about our freedom fighters who lost their lives while serving our motherland.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb. At the end of a singular verb, s/es is used. In the given sentence, ‘this book’ is a singular subject that will take ‘gives’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘gives us much information’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The food intolerance industry has grown dramatically in the previous decade, chiefly because of a boost in Coeliac and Crohn’s disease cases, as well as increasing awareness among health-conscious clients.
options: pretty much entirely because of a boil-down
explanation: ‘Owing to’ means because of & ‘primarily’ means mainly. ‘Rise’ means increase in number. The given sentence states that the food intolerance industry has grown dramatically in the previous decade, owing primarily to a rise in Coeliac and Crohn’s disease cases, as well as increasing awareness among health-conscious clients. Hence, ‘owing primarily to a rise’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Aesthetic value is specifically a way in which we can get positive conclude value from the world at large.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adjective (conclusive) to describe the noun ‘value’, and not the verb ‘conclude’. Hence, ‘can get positive conclusive value’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Ranjith failed in all his exams as he had been addicted of social media.
options: as he had been addicted at
as he had been addicted on
as he had been addicted in
as he had been addicted to
explanation: ‘To’ is a fixed preposition used after the verb ‘addicted’. Hence, ‘as he had been addicted to’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The cynical investors believed in every word the analysts said.
explanation: ‘Credulous’ means willing to believe or trust too readily. The given sentence states that the credulous investors believed in every word the analysts said. Hence, 'credulous' is the most appropriate answer.

text: It is nothing else your pride which makes you say such a thing.
options: else but your pride which make
else but your pride which makes
explanation: ‘Nothing … but’ or ‘Nothing else … but’ means only. The given sentence needs the conjunction ‘but’ after ‘nothing else’ to make it grammatically correct. Hence, ‘else but your pride which makes’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mr. Adhil called back but he wasn’t able to find the scooter part he needed.
options: called down but he wasn’t able to
called off but he wasn’t able to
called around but he wasn’t able to
called up to but he wasn’t able to
explanation: ‘Call around’ means to call multiple people to find information about something. The given sentence states that Mr. Adhil called around but he wasn’t able to find the scooter part he needed. Hence, 'called around but he wasn’t able to' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. We need to _____ a solution to this problem before it gets worse.
explanation: ‘Come up with’ means to suggest or think of an idea or plan. The given sentence states that we need to come up with a solution to this problem before it gets worse. Hence, 'come up with' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Nina has not yet learned how to straighten up and fly right.
options: forget the wrongdoings of the others
improve her absurd behaviour and act seriously
be professional in flying the aircraft
remember the past and prepare for the future
