explanation: The phrase ‘straighten up and fly right’ means to get serious and stop acting absurd anymore. The given sentence states that Nina has not yet learned how to improve her absurd behaviour and act seriously. Hence, 'improve her absurd behaviour and act seriously' is the most appropriate answer.

text: I had not only helped her by giving hints but also with providing her links.
explanation: The same part of speech is used after pair conjunctions such as ‘not only…but also’. There is a preposition followed by gerund(providing) after ‘but also’. Therefore, ‘not only’ will be placed before the preposition ‘by’. Hence, ‘helped her not only by’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Positive self-talk have a great affect on one’s self-worth.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb. In the given sentence, ‘positive self-talk’ is a singular subject that will take ‘has’ as a singular verb. Also, the adjective ‘great’ needs a noun to qualify its meaning. Hence, ‘has a great effect’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Arushya purchased the most good of all the suits kept in the shop.
explanation: ‘Best’ is the correct superlative degree of ‘good’. Hence, ‘the best’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Even if you’ve never heard his name, you’ve probably met someone with his words tattooed in their skin or heard them sung at a music concert.
explanation: ‘On’ is used to indicate the surface in contact with the object. Similarly, the tattoo lies on the surface of the skin. Hence, ‘tattooed on their skin’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the option that can substitute/replace the bracketed word correctly and complete the sentence. If he runs, he (get) there in time.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of the first conditional sentence and the correct grammatical structure is “if + simple present…….will +V1”. Hence ‘will get(V1)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Ashoka was the greatest than all the Mauryan Emperors .
explanation: ‘Than’ is used with comparative degree while ‘of’ is used after the superlative degree. ‘The + superlative adjective + of + plural noun/pronoun’ is the correct structure. Hence, 'of the Mauryan Emperors' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the option that can substitute/replace the bracketed word correctly and complete the sentence. I said I (don't) understand.
explanation: The given sentence is in the past tense, so it must have the verb of past tense. ‘Did’ is a helping verb of simple past tense. Hence, didn’t is the most appropriate answer.

text: I picked up my little clock and it began to dance gracefully.
explanation: ‘Chime’ means (of a bell or clock) make melodious ringing sounds. The given passage states that I picked up my little clock and it began to chime prettily. Hence, ‘chime prettily’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The chair I have bought recently is costly than what I bought last year.
explanation: We use a comparative degree with ‘than’ to make a comparison between two things. ‘Costlier’ is the correct comparative degree of ‘costly’. Hence, ‘is costlier’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: RN Right’s literary works helped redefine discussions in race relations in America in the mid-20th century.
explanation: ‘Of’ means relating to something. The given sentence states that RN Right’s literary works helped redefine discussions of race relations in America in the mid-20th century. Hence, 'of race relations in America' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Verity is a good virtue for human life.
explanation: ‘Verity’ means the state of being true. The given sentence states that truth is a good virtue for human life. Hence, 'Truth' is the most appropriate answer.

text: The chief guest concluded his speech as he requested to stop by the organisers.
explanation: The second clause of the sentence is in the passive voice as the doer of the action is given using the preposition ‘by’. ‘Was + V3’ is the correct structure for the passive voice of simple past tense. Hence, ‘he was requested’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully. We will have to (put the meeting away) as the Director is not well.
explanation: The phrasal verb ‘put off’ means to postpone or delay a meeting. The given sentence states that we will have to put the meeting off as the Director is not well. Hence, ‘put the meeting off’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I am down with her complaints.
explanation: ‘Fed up with’ means being irritated or frustrated. The given sentence states that the person is frustrated or annoyed with someone's complaints. Hence ‘fed up with’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The little boy cried with pain when he burnt his fingers.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: The skunk had a conspicuous spinal stripe.
explanation: ‘Noticeable’ means easily seen or noticed. The given sentence states that the skunk had a conspicuous spinal stripe. Hence, 'noticeable' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Rahul had strong pain in his stomach.
explanation: Strict- someone who sticks to a particular set of rules.

text: Select the most appropriate option that can replace the bracketed word segment in the following sentence. Children should avoid giving out personal details online (which will) identify them or their location.
explanation: ‘Could’ is used to indicate possibility. The given sentence states an advice to children that they should avoid giving out personal details online that could identify them or their location. Hence, ‘that could’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The company do not broke the law at any time.
explanation: ‘Do/does/did + V1’ is the correct grammatical structure. Hence, ‘does not break’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He was not happy until he gave up his job and live as a fakir in the forests.
options: until he gave up his job and lived
until he gives up his job and lived
unless he gave up his job and lives
until he gave up his job and lives
explanation: The given sentence is in the simple past tense so the verb must be used in the simple past form(V2). However, the past form of ‘live’ is ‘lived’. Hence, ‘until he gave up his job and lived(V2)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Dhruv’s anger blazed of uncontrollably.
explanation: ‘Blaze up’ is the correct phrasal verb to use in this sentence. ‘Blaze up’ means (an emotion) to become stronger or more extreme. The given sentence states that Dhruv’s anger blazed up uncontrollably. Hence, 'anger blazed up' is the most appropriate answer.

text: This win could enhance to be a historic turning point in the fortunes of the team.
explanation: ‘Prove’ is the correct verb to use in this sentence. ‘Prove’ means to show a particular result after a period of time. The given sentence states that this win could prove to be a historic turning point in the fortunes of the team. Hence, ‘prove’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mothers have great animosity for their children.
explanation: ‘Affection’ means a strong feeling of love and care. The given sentence states that mothers have great affection for their children. Hence, ‘affection’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Sonam’s cat used to chase the mouse into the kitchen and knock through a tower of pots and pans.
options: knock over a tower of pots
knock out a tower of pots
knock away a tower of pots
knock inside a tower of pots
explanation: ‘Knock over’ is the correct phrasal verb to use in this sentence. ‘Knock over’ means to hit or push something, especially accidentally. The given sentence states that Sonam’s cat used to chase the mouse into the kitchen and accidentally hit a tower of pots and pans. Hence, 'knock over a tower of pots and pans' is the most appropriate answer.

text: A soldier of the tenth legion leaped into the water as soon as the ship touches the shore.
options: the ship was touch the shore
explanation: ‘Touch’ must be replaced with ‘Touched’. The given sentence is Pinnacle Sentence Improvement in the past tense so it must have the verb in the past form(V2) and not in the present form (touches). Hence, ‘the ship touched(V2) the shore’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We feel warm on the subject
explanation: ‘Warmly’ means in a very friendly way. The given sentence states that we feel warmly about the subject. Hence, ‘warmly about’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The dictator ordered the traitor were jailed.
explanation: The given sentence uses the passive form of the verb after the noun ‘traitor’ because ‘traitor’ is the receiver of the action(jailed). ‘Be + V3’ is the correct passive structure. Hence, ‘to be’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the option that corrects the following sentence. He has broken his leg yesterday.
options: He had broke his leg yesterday.
He have broken his leg yesterday.
He has broke his leg yesterday.
explanation: ‘Subject + V2’ is grammatically the correct structure for a sentence which is in the simple past tense. Hence, the sentence given in option (d) is correct.

text: Please take many as you want.
explanation: ‘As much as’ is the correct phrase to use here. ‘As much as’ is used to indicate an amount equal to something else. Hence, ‘as much’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Rimjhim received a children’s very illustrated colourful atlas on her 10th birthday.
options: an very illustrated colourful children’s atlas
a very colourful illustrated children’s atlas
a very illustrated colourful atlas children
a colourful very illustrated children’s atlas
explanation: very colourful illustrated children’s atlas

text: The Privacy Shield establishes a process to allow companies to transfer consumer data from European Union countries to the United States in compliance in EU law.
explanation: ‘With’ is a fixed preposition used with ‘comply/ compliance’. Hence ‘in compliance with’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This book provides an unrestrained account of the natural resources in India.
explanation: ‘Exhaustive’ means complete and including everything. The given sentence states that this book provides an exhaustive account of the natural resources in India. Hence, ‘exhaustive’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the option that will improve the given sentence by using the most appropriate verb. That Macbook belong to Xavier.
options: That Macbook is belong to Xavier.
That Macbook is belonged to Xavier.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. At the end of a singular verb, s/es is used. In the given sentence, ‘That Macbook’ is a singular subject that will take ‘belongs’ as a singular verb. Hence, the sentence given in option (c) is correct.

text: It will take two hours to walk across the forest.
explanation: ‘Through’ means from one side to the other. The given sentence states that it will take two hours to walk through the forest. Hence, ‘through’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We set up on the journey early in the morning.
explanation: ‘Set off’ is the correct phrasal verb to use here. ‘Set off’ means to begin a journey. The given sentence states that we set off on the journey early in the morning. Hence, ‘set off’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: You can be sentenced for trespassing on someone else’s property
The wizard, while performing an item, accidentally set his own hat on fire and prompted the fire alarm to go on.
options: the fire alarm to go above
the fire alarm to go off
the fire alarm to go under
the fire alarm to go away
explanation: The phrasal verb ‘go off’ means to start to ring loudly. The given sentence talks about the alarm ringing loudly due to the hat on fire. Hence, ‘the fire alarm to go off’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In every country of the world, primary caregivers are the women of children and elders.
options: women are the caregivers primary of
the women primary caregivers are of
women are the primary caregivers of
primary caregivers women are of the
explanation: A caregiver is a paid helper who looks after a child. So, the noun ‘caregivers’ will be used before the noun ‘children’. So, the correct phrase is ‘primary caregivers of children and elders’. ‘Women’ is a plural subject of the sentence, which takes the plural verb ‘are’. Hence, ‘women are the primary caregivers of’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The woman lost much to her body weight due to diabetes.
options: off her body weight due to
from her body weight due to
for her body weight due to
of her body weight due to
explanation: ‘Of’ is used to indicate a part or portion of something. Similarly, in the given sentence, the woman lost a part of her body weight due to diabetes. Hence, ‘of her body weight due to’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate option that can replace the bracketed word segment in the following sentence. An (imperfect positioning) of the Sun, Earth and Moon results in the Moon passing through only part of Earth's umbra, resulting in a partial lunar eclipse.
explanation: ‘Alignment’ means arrangement in correct relative positions. The given sentence talks about the imperfect relative positions of the Sun, Earth and Moon which results in a partial lunar eclipse. Hence, ‘imperfect alignment’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The new chief is gifted at the power of eloquence.
explanation: ‘With’ is a fixed preposition used with the adjective ‘gifted’. The phrase ‘gifted with’ means having an exceptional talent or natural ability. Hence, ‘gifted with’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The recent cloudburst completely dismantled the village and its people.
explanation: Took up- to begin a new activity. Took back- to regain possession of something. Took after- to resemble someone, usually in appearance or behavior.

text: The annual seed festival hosted in Auroville promote sharing of traditional knowledge and sustainable farming practices.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb. At the end of a singular verb, s/es is used. Similarly, ‘The annual seed festival’ is a singular subject that will take ‘promotes’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘promotes sharing of traditional’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The sudden declaration of war between two countries led to a disarray.
explanation: ‘Disarray’ means lack of order or sequence, which is synonymous with the phrase ‘disorderly situation’. Hence, ‘disorderly situation’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Greta Thunberg’s tirade against environmental degeneration shocked the world leaders.
explanation: ‘Tirade’ means a long angry speech of criticism or accusation. Hence, ‘long and angry speech’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He lived on the bank of a mighty river, broad and deep, that have always silently rolling on to a vast undiscovered ocean.
explanation: ‘Singular Sub (mighty river) + was + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence which is in the past continuous tense. Hence, ‘which was always silently rolling(Ving)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If you are thinking about investing in share markets, isn’t it make sense to find an expert ?
explanation: The given sentence is in the simple present tense and ‘does + V1’ is the correct structure for it as the subject ‘it’ is singular. Hence, doesn’t it is the most appropriate answer.

text: The novel highlights the place of the endangered species in the rainforest.
explanation: ‘Plight’ means a difficult or dangerous situation. The given sentence states that the novel highlights the plight of the endangered species in the rainforest. Hence, ‘plight’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I gave my best dress to her on condition that she return it the very next day in a clean condition.
options: on the condition that she would return
on the conditions that she had return
on the condition that she return
explanation: ‘Would’ is a modal used to indicate expected future when seen from the past. As per the given sentence, the person gave a dress in the past and expected her to return it later. Hence, ‘on the condition that she would return’ is the most appropriate Pinnacle Sentence Improvement answer.

text: The boy watched a sci-fi movie in the lieu of playing in the game zone.
explanation: Article ‘the’ is not used in the phrase ‘in lieu of’. A noun or gerund(Ving) is used with it. In the given sentence, a gerund(playing) has been used with it. Hence, ‘in lieu of’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate option to correct the sentence by using meaning of the undelined word. In the winter season, the poor woman needed a refuge where she could live freely and independently.
The revolt of the labourers will be considered as an epoch in the world history.
explanation: ‘Epoch’ means a period of time that is very important in history. The given sentence states that the revolt of the labourers will be considered as an important period in the world history. Hence, ‘important period’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: A newer, more effective computer system was installed in place of the obsolete one.
explanation: ‘Obsolete’ means out of date, which is synonymous with ‘outdated’. Hence, ‘outdated’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I had to write a letter of mistake to my father for the blunder I made.
explanation: ‘Apology’ means a statement saying that you are sorry for something. The given sentence states that I had to write a letter of apology to my father for the blunder I made. Hence, ‘apology’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the option that corrects the following sentence. All tickets of the FIFA World Cup have been sold away.
options: All tickets of the FIFA World Cup have been sold out.
All tickets of the FIFA World Cup have been sold among.
All tickets of the FIFA World Cup have been sold into.
All tickets of the FIFA World Cup have been sold across.
explanation: The correct phrasal verb is ‘sold out’ which means having all available tickets sold completely. Hence, ‘sold out’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Employers in many developing countries report that a lack of skilled workers is a major and increasing bottleneck for their operations, affected their capacity to innovate.
explanation: A present participle phrase(Ving) is used to describe an action the noun is doing. In the given sentence, ‘affecting their capacity’ describes the action resulting from ‘lack of skilled workers’. Hence, ‘affecting their capacity’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Planets in our solar system close and big for them to twinkle.
explanation: ‘Too + adjective + to + V1(twinkle)’ is the correct grammatical structure. ‘Close’ and ‘big’ are adjectives. Hence ‘are too close and big’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He asked his father when would come the next letter.
explanation: The correct structure of a clause is ‘Subject + modal + main verb’. ‘The next letter’ is the subject of the clause, so it will be followed by modal ‘would’ and the main verb ‘come’. Hence ‘the next letter would come’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Although I have a lot of work to do, I am determined to finish it all by the end of the day so that I can enjoy my weekend not having any imminent due dates.
options: not with any pressure of due date
explanation: ‘Looming deadline' means a deadline that is coming soon and must be met. ‘Imminent due date’ means a due date that is about to happen very soon. Hence, ‘without any looking deadlines’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Vihaan is clumsy at dancing.
The crux of the study has been delineated by the researcher.
explanation: ‘Crux’ means the most important or central point of something. Hence, ‘central point’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Since my friend was not feeling well, she asked me to come over and take care of her.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Yoga may manage pain and helping reduce stress.
explanation: ‘May’ is a modal that will take the first form of the verb, ‘help’. ‘Help in + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure. Hence, ‘help in reducing’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He has grown into a beautiful youth.
explanation: ‘Beautiful’ must be replaced by ‘handsome’. We generally use ‘handsome’ to describe men and we use ‘beautiful’ to describe women. Hence, ‘into a handsome youth’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We are decorate the living-room at the moment.
explanation: The phrase ‘at the moment’ describes an action happening right now. And we generally use present continuous tense (is/am/are + V-ing) to denote an action happening in the present. Hence, ‘We are decorating’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate option that can replace the bracketed word segment in the following sentence. Men (allowed) for Olympic artistic swimming for the first time at the 2024 Paris Games, the IOC confirmed on Thursday.
explanation: ‘Eligible’ means qualified to participate in a sport. The given sentence is talking about the sport of swimming. Hence, ‘are eligible’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: As there was no one to look thorough the orphan, he had to take refuge in the orphanage.
explanation: ‘Look after’ must be used in place of ‘look through’. ‘Look after’ is a phrasal verb which means to take care of someone. The given sentence states that there was no one to take care of the orphan. Hence, ‘look after’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: There is an old rivalry between the three families for ages.
explanation: ‘Between’ must be replaced by ‘Among’. We use ‘among’ for more than two entities and ‘between’ for two entities. However, there are three families mentioned in the given sentence. Hence, ‘among the three families’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It is my custom to get up early in the morning.
explanation: ‘Habit’ means something that you do often and regularly. The given sentence states that it is my habit to get up early in the morning. Hence, ‘habit’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: There was enough room in the spacious flat for all of our furniture.
explanation: ‘Roomy’ means having a lot of space. The given sentence states that there was enough room in the roomy flat for all of our furniture. Hence, ‘roomy’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I consider that every matter must be considered in every point of view.
explanation: ‘From’ is used to show somebody’s point of view. Hence, ‘from every point’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Once bitten, thrice shy.
explanation: ‘Once bitten, twice shy’ is an idiom which means you are frightened to do something again because you had an unpleasant experience doing it the first time. Hence, option (a) is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the option that can substitute the bracketed word segment meaningfully. Writing can instill a number of emotions (as in a reader).
explanation: ‘Within’ means inside. The given sentence states that writing can instill a number of emotions within a reader. Hence, ‘within a reader’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Professor Singh is not in the office today. I ask you try call him tomorrow.
explanation: ‘Suggest’ to mention an action for other people to consider. ‘Suggest’ is a stative verb, so it will be used in the simple present tense, rather than present continuous tense. Hence, ‘suggest you try calling’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Bill Gates' fortune was bequeathed for the old age home.
explanation: ‘To’ is used to indicate the receiver of an action or thing. In the given sentence, ‘to’ has been used to indicate the receiver of Bill Gate’s fortune. Hence, ‘to the old age home’ is the correct answer.

text: Choose an appropriate word that can substitute the bracketed word and complete the sentence meaningfully. He never (talks) the truth.
explanation: ‘Speak the truth’ is the correct phrase. Hence, ‘speaks’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The small size of his store makes it impossible for him to stock all the items.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: He scores good marks in exams as he is quite meticulous.
Select the option that will improve the given sentence by using the most appropriate verb. Alexa have being working as a teacher for five years now.
options: Alexa was been working as a teacher for five years now.
Alexa has been working as a teacher for five years now.
Alexa has being working as a teacher for five years now.
Alexa is being working as a teacher for five years now.
explanation: Alexa has been working as a teacher for five years now. The given sentence is in the present perfect continuous tense and follows the structure ‘Singular subject + has been + Ving’. Hence, the sentence given in option (c) is correct.

text: Grasslands should not be foraged and some places are to be closed for grazing.
options: over-grazed and some areas should be
explanation: ‘Overgrazed’ means to eat too much grass in an area, which damages the environment. To maintain consistency with the first part, ‘should’ has been used again in the second part. Hence, ‘over-grazed and some areas should be’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Things that do not come from the ground not safe to compost.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘things’ is a plural subject that will take ‘are’ as a plural verb. Hence, ‘are not safe’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: UNICEF builds partnerships across the global community on accelerate gender equality.
explanation: ‘To + V1’ is the correct grammatical structure. Hence, ‘global community to accelerate(V1)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Allusive handwriting creates a poor impression.
explanation: ‘Illegible handwriting’ means writing that is difficult to read because it is unclear. The given sentence states that illegible handwriting creates a poor impression. Hence, ‘Illegible handwriting’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mr. Sen is clever enough to handle his professional hazards.
explanation: ‘Intelligent’ means someone who is smart or knowledgeable. The given sentence states that Mr. Sen is intelligent enough to handle his professional hazards. Hence, ‘intelligent’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The housing loan taken by Ramesh effected his daily expenses adversely.
explanation: ‘Effected’ must be replaced with ‘affected’ as the given sentence needs a verb. Hence ‘by Ramesh affected’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Although uncountable files stack up on the tables of government officials, they prefer doing their work at a more leisure pace.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adjective to describe the noun ‘pace’. ‘More leisurely’ is the comparative form of the adjective ‘leisurely’. Hence, ‘at a more leisurely pace’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. It was a privvilege to receive the award from the President.
explanation: ‘Privilege’ is the correct spelling.

text: Select the most appropriate option that can replace the bracketed word segment in the following sentence. Classical buildings in ancient Greek and Roman times were (characteristically built) from marble or some other attractive, durable stone.
explanation: ‘Typically’ means in a way that shows the characteristics of a particular kind of thing. The given sentence states that classical buildings in ancient aGreek and Roman times were typically built from marble or some other attractive, durable stone. Hence, ‘typically built’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We shall rehearse thrice before the final performance at least we make errors in the dialogues.
explanation: ‘Lest’ is used in order to prevent something from happening. The given sentence talks about rehearsing thrice in order to prevent errors in the dialogues. Hence, ‘lest we make errors’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This newly arisen evidence could have proved to finally put the culprit behind bars.
explanation: Evidence does not need to be proved. Evidence itself is proof that something happened or is true. Hence, ‘is proof’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If you give away smoking, your health will improve.
explanation: The phrasal verb ‘give up’ means to stop doing something. The given sentence states that if you give up smoking, your health will improve. Hence, ‘give up’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: There was some drawing-pins in my desk.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘drawing pins’ is a plural subject that will take ‘are’ as a plural verb. Hence, ‘There are some’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The common masses have waited for three hours to meet the king in the royal court.
explanation: Present perfect continuous tense is used when the time period is given using the preposition ‘for’. ‘Plural Sub. + have been + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure for this sentence. Hence, ‘have been waiting’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This serum contains ingredients enabling the hair to grow.
options: that enable the hair to grow
explanation: 'That' is a relative pronoun used to introduce a relative clause, which provides additional information about a noun. Here, the clause provides additional information about the ingredients. Hence, ‘that enable the hair to grow’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She argued against the unnecessary split in the committee.
Had you been to Dubai, I would also go with you.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of a third conditional sentence and the correct grammatical structure for it is “had + Subject + been …….. would have + V3”. Hence, ‘I would have gone(V3)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the word segment from the options that can substitute the bracketed word segment meaningfully. Telangana artists (are know for the amazing bronze castings).
options: Have been knew to the amazing bronze castings
Are known for their amazing bronze castings
Is known to the amazing bronze castings
Have to know the amazing bronze castings
explanation: The given sentence is a passive voice of simple present tense and the subject ‘Telangana artists’ is plural. ‘Plural Subject + are + V3’ is the correct grammatical structure for it. Hence, ‘are known for the amazing bronze castings’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It has been found that the trees are being destroyed by a moth.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: No sooner did we reach at the party that it began to rain.
explanation: ‘That’ must be replaced by ‘than’. ‘No sooner…than’ is a fixed conjunction pair. Hence, ‘than it began to rain’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The interdisciplinary approach utilised in this study facilitates comprehensive understanding of the complex phenomenon under investigation.
options: will have facilitated a comprehensive understanding
explanation: The given sentence is in the simple past tense, so the verb must be used in the simple past form(V2). Hence, ‘facilitated(V2) a comprehensive understanding’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He passed away in the year 1950 at 10 a.m. on 13 July.
options: in the year 1950 at 10 a.m. on 13 July
on 13 July at 10 a.m. in the year 1950
at 10 a.m. on 13 July in the year 1950
in the year 1950 on 13 July at 10 a.m.
explanation: The correct order is time followed by day, month and then the year. Hence, ‘at 10 a.m. on 13 July in the year 1950’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I was in Oman around two months.
explanation: ‘Around’ must be replaced with ‘for’ as ‘for’ is used to indicate a period of time. Hence, ‘for two months’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The meeting closed with a vote of thanks.
explanation: ‘Concluded’ means to bring something to an end or finish, particularly in a formal context. The given sentence states that the meeting concluded with a vote of thanks. Hence, ‘concluded’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: At his wit’s end, he decided to return to his parents as he was unable to cope up with the stress of adjusting at a new place.
Peter was the last to know that she had been cheating of him
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. ‘Cheat on someone’ is the correct phrase. Hence, 'cheating on him' is the most appropriate answer.

text: The film was made in Botswana, whose wildlife parks is larger to those in Kenya.
explanation: ‘Wildlife parks’ is a plural subject that will take ‘are’ as a plural verb. ‘Than’ is used with a comparative degree to make a comparison. Hence, ‘are larger than’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I opened the box beneath the table and took of a book, the Materia Medica.
explanation: The phrasal verb ‘take out’ means to remove something from somewhere. The given sentence states that I opened the box and took out a book, the Materia Medica. Hence, ‘took out’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Do not later about the street.
explanation: The correct phrase is ‘loiter around’ which means to hang around or stay in an area without any specific purpose. Hence, ‘loiter around’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The experienced surgeon handled the delicate procedure with care and precision.
explanation: ‘Experienced’ must be replaced with ‘seasoned’ which means highly experienced and skilled, especially after many years of practice. The given sentence states that the seasoned surgeon handled the delicate procedure with care and precision. Hence, ‘seasoned’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Planning to go for a movie just before the final-year examination is nothing but skating on thin ice.
Shakespeare is greater than any other English poet.
explanation: ‘Shakespeare’ is a late (not alive) English poet. So, we need to use the past form(V2) of the verb to indicate the simple past tense. Hence, ‘was greater than’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I prefer walking than riding.
explanation: ‘To’ is a fixed preposition used after the verb ‘prefer’. Hence, ‘walking to riding’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Youth is the time when the seeds of character is sown.
options: the seeds of character had been sown
the seeds of character were sown
the seeds of character will have been sowing
the seeds of character are sown
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a plural subject always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘seeds’ is a plural subject that will take ‘are’ as a plural verb. Hence, ‘the seeds of character are sown’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: An awkward neither grammatically accurate sentence is the result of centre implanting.
explanation: ‘But’ is used to indicate a contrasting idea. Similarly, the word ‘awkward’ contrasts with the idea ‘grammatically accurate’. Hence, ‘awkward but grammatically’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The referee declared that the participant who will score the highest points in the tally will take away the cash prize of ₹50 lakh.
options: who can score the highest point
who could score the highest point
who settles scores the highest point
explanation: ‘Scoring the highest points’ is a general rule or condition for taking away the cash prize of ₹50 lakh. Simple present tense is used to state a general truth or condition. ‘Singular Sub. + V1-s/es’ is the correct grammatical structure. Hence, ‘who scores the highest point’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My friends are on a trip to the world.
explanation: ‘To’ is used for a fixed or particular location. Whereas ‘around’ is used with ‘world’. Hence, ‘around the world’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The Government must strive to provide a/an fair and square deal to the citizen of its country.
The culprit had been shot from the back by the police inspector.
explanation: Here, ‘in’ will be used to indicate that the bullet that was shot by the police inspector hit the back of the culprit. Hence, ‘in’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Though Kalpana listened to Sheetal carefully, she knew that she should take it with a grain of salt.
options: regard it as exaggerated and not completely true
be do it meticulously as taking salt
accept it as really useful and worthy
explanation: and not completely true.

text: The author’s writing style is characterised by its poetic language.
explanation: ‘Lyrical’ means poetic and romantic. The given sentence states that the author’s writing style is characterised by its poetic language. Hence, ‘lyrical language’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Read the books of APJ Abdul Kalam, who was a scholar.
explanation: man of letters

text: My friend vanished when the goons came to fight with me.
explanation: ‘Vanish’ means to disappear suddenly and completely. ‘Goon’ means a thug hired to commit acts of violence or intimidation. Hence, ‘disappeared when the thugs came’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If I was very rich, I would spend all my time and money for the poor.
explanation: The phrase ‘If I were’ is used to refer to an imaginary situation. ‘If I were … would + V1’ is the correct grammatical structure. Hence, ‘If I were very rich’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Last night, I failed to sleep because of some familiar issues that couldn't be avoided.
No sooner had she finished her breakfast that she had received a phone call from her boss, informing her that she needed to come to work immediately.
explanation: ‘No sooner…than’ is a fixed conjunction pair. If there are two actions in the past, the 1st action is written in past perfect tense (had + V3) and the 2nd action is written in simple past tense(V2). Hence, ‘than she received(V2)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: After he leave, we discussed his suggestion.
explanation: If two actions happened in the past, 1st action is written in past perfect tense(had + V3) and 2nd action is written in simple past tense(V2). The action of leaving happened first. Hence, ‘he had left(V3)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Though very informative, Shweta's article was mercilessly rejected of the editor.
explanation: ‘By’ is used in passive voice to indicate the doer of the action. Similarly, ‘editor’ is the doer of the action of rejecting. Hence, ‘was mercilessly rejected by’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mathew decided to complete the marathon to prove that he is still fit as a fiddle in his eighties.
options: an owner of a fit horse
explanation: fit and energetic person

text: My son will carry out my business in my absence.
explanation: ‘Carry on’ means to continue a task or an activity. The given sentence states that my son will carry on my business in my absence. Hence, ‘carry on’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It is a fact that the same judgement can often be taken by more than one way.
explanation: The phrasal verb ‘take in’ means to understand something that you read or hear. The given sentence states that it is a fact that the same judgement can be taken in more than one way. Hence, ‘be taken in more than’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The company plans to expand its business to the international market.
explanation: ‘Expand’ means to increase the extent or scope of something. The given sentence states that the company plans to increase its business to the international market. Hence, ‘to increase’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He always used to say that he was not a beggar by choice and if someone could employ him, he would like to eat.
explanation: The given sentence talks about a person who is not a beggar by choice. This means he would love to work if somebody could employ him. Hence, ‘love to work’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The manager, decided at last to bring the stenographer to book for her illegal money transactions after trying to ignore it several times.
options: bring her for a detailed investigation
make her accountable for her conduct
place her in a safe supportive position
explanation: ‘Bring someone to book’ is an idiom which means to hold someone accountable for something they have done. Hence, ‘make her accountable for her conduct’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In yesterday’s fire accident, her feets are burnt badly.
explanation: ‘Yesterday’ indicates past tense. ‘Feets’ is incorrect as ‘feet’ is the correct plural form of ‘foot’. Hence, ‘her feet were’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate option with correct usage of the preposition to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The Centre of Excellence for Data Analytics (CEDA) provides quality data analytic services to various government departments on all levels as well as to public sector units at the Centre and in states.
options: various government departments at all levels
various government departments from all levels
various government departments in all levels
various government departments through all levels
explanation: ‘At’ is used to indicate the position, rank or level of something. Hence, ‘various government departments at all levels’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: You have tears, prepare to shed them now.
explanation: ‘If’ is used to provide the condition under which something happens. Similarly, in the given sentence, having tears is the condition for shedding tears. Hence, ‘If you have tears’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully. The minister promised to provide free laptops to the public if his (party came in power).
explanation: ‘To come into power’ means to form the government. The given sentence states that the minister promised to provide free laptops to the public if his party forms the government. Hence, ‘party forms the government’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This is the group of leaders in whom the ruling government has placed its trust.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: During the preparation for competitive exams, Meena avoided going to parties.
explanation: The phrase ‘steer clear of’ means to deliberately avoid something. Hence, ‘steered clear of’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The woman to who I sold my house was a criminal.
explanation: ‘To’ is a preposition and we generally use an objective case pronoun after any preposition. Therefore, ‘who’ must be replaced with ‘whom’. Hence, ‘to whom I sold’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: A sharp fall in the price of jute have led the poor jute farmers to the brink of starvation.
options: have lead the poor jute farmers
has led the poor jute farmers
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘A sharp fall’ is a singular subject that will take ‘has’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘has led the poor jute farmers’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We should not underestimate the signification of female education.
explanation: ‘Significance’ is the correct word to use here. ‘Significance’ means importance or meaningfulness. The given sentence states that we should not underestimate the significance of female education. Hence, ‘underestimate the significance’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Half of the property given to his sons by the businessman last year.
options: Half of the property has been given
Half of the property was given
Half of the property is given
explanation: The given sentence is in the passive voice as the doer of the action is given after the preposition ‘by’. The phrase ‘last year’ indicates simple past tense. ‘Singular Sub. + was + V3’ is the correct grammatical structure for the passive voice of simple past tense. Hence, ‘Half of the property was given(V3)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Even after becoming bankrupt, Charlie is able to maintain an outward show.
explanation: E.g.- Even though he was worried, he kept up appearances and smiled.

text: Amit is also a chip off the old block like his brother, Tandon.
options: resembling his parents in character and appearance
talking to others tough like a stone
getting ready for the future endeavours
explanation: character and appearance.

text: Reena decided not to go to work today because she was feeling sick.
He wanted to visiting the Golden Temple in Amritsar.
explanation: ‘To + V1’ , also known as an infinitive, is the correct grammatical structure. Hence, ‘wanted to visit(V1)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: His interpretation of the facts was impressive.
explanation: We generally use a noun, pronoun or a gerund(Ving) as the subject of a sentence. Hence, ‘understanding(Ving) of realities’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given idiom. A piece of biscuit
explanation: E.g.- For him, fixing computers is a piece of cake.

text: Had I known that you were planning to visit me, I should have done all the necessary arrangements.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of the third conditional sentence and ‘’(if + Sub. + had + V3)/(Had + Sub. + V3) … would have + V3’ is the correct grammatical structure for it. Therefore, ‘should’ must be replaced with ‘would’. Hence, ‘I would have made(V3)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: What exactly have the teachers being doing wrong ?
explanation: ‘Have been + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure for the sentence which is in the present perfect continuous tense. Hence, ‘teachers been doing(Ving)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If his father will give money, he will buy a sports bike.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of the first conditional sentence and ‘if + Simple Present Tense… will + V1’ is the correct grammatical structure for it. ‘Father’ is a singular subject that will take ‘gives’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘If his father gives money’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I have been living without a lot of money since I lost my job.
options: as genuine as a three-dollar bill

text: The road is too busy for elderly people that they cannot cross safely.
options: that it is impossible for them to cross
that it cannot be crossed properly.
that it is difficult to cross.
explanation: ‘Too + adjective/ adverb + to + V1’ is the correct grammatical structure. Hence, ‘to cross(V1) safely’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate option with correct usage of the preposition to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The core part in Artificial Intelligence (AI) is knowledge engineering, machine learning, machine perception, and robotics.
options: The core part from Artificial Intelligence
The core part with Artificial Intelligence
The core part of Artificial Intelligence
The core part on Artificial Intelligence
explanation: indicate a part or component of something. The given sentence talks about the core part of Artificial Intelligence. Hence, ‘The core part of Artificial intelligence’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The veteran footballer was expected for reach here by 10 o’clock, the notice said.
explanation: There are some verbs that are followed by an infinitive(to + V1). These verbs are ‘agree, decide, appear, expect, fail, afford, wish, aim, etc’. Hence, ‘expected to reach(V1) here’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mr. Patel is likely to win the elections in the sweeping majority.
explanation: ‘By’ is used to indicate the amount or extent of something. In the given sentence, ‘by’ has been used to indicate the amount of majority in the elections. Hence, ‘elections by a sweeping majority’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Not a word didn’t they speak to the others about the sad turn of events.
explanation: The given sentence talks about the sad turn of events in the past. ‘Did + V1’ is the correct grammatical structure for the sentence which is in the simple past tense. Hence, ‘did they speak(V1)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Before she began, she asked the teacher whether she write with a pen or a pencil.
explanation: ‘Should’ is used to indicate what is probable. Pen and pencil are probable ways to write. Hence, ‘she should write’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The Sumo wrestler seemed to be incapable in being tired.
explanation: ‘Of’ is a fixed preposition used after ‘capable / incapable’. Hence, ‘incapable of being fired’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My grandmother helps us in all the problems. She has a remedy for all the diseases.
explanation: Service- the occupation or function of serving. Fanatic- a person who is extremely interested in something. Heretic- a person whose religious beliefs are believed to be wrong or evil.

text: He is feeding a male dog and female dog
options: a male dog and lady dog
explanation: A female dog is called a bitch. Hence, ‘a dog and a bitch’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: What flavour ice cream do you want?
explanation: ‘Of’ is used to show one thing related to another. Similarly, flavour is related to ice cream. Hence, ‘flavour of ice cream’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The quality of students of an educational institute is of great importance and a crucial starting point
options: The quality of students in an educational institute is in great importance and a crucial starting point.
The quality of students in an educational institute is of great importance and is a crucial start point
The quality of students in an educational institute is of great importance and a crucial starting point.
explanation: of great importance and a crucial starting point. The phrase ‘students of an educational institute’ must be replaced with ‘students in an educational institute’. We generally use the preposition ‘in’ to indicate the presence or location of something inside something else. The given sentence talks about the quality of students present in an educational institute. Hence, option (d) is the most appropriate answer.

text: The serenity of the river was a sight to behold.
explanation: The phrase ‘a sight to behold’ means a person is extremely pleased to see it. Hence, ‘pleasant to see’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Inspite mother’s milk is vital to a child’s health, a number of FMCG companies wrongly advertise artificially prepared infant formulas as being the best for the child.
explanation: ‘Though’ is used to express contrast between two ideas. The given sentence states that mother’s milk is vital to a child's health, which contrasts with the advertisement of artificially prepared infant formulas. Hence, “Though mother’s milk” is the most appropriate answer.

text: She asked me where my hometown is and where I worked.
explanation: The given sentence is in the past tense, therefore, we will use the helping verb of past tense. ‘Is’ must be replaced with ‘was’. Hence, ‘hometown was’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Ice melts fastly in the sun.
explanation: ‘Fastly’ is an incorrect word. ‘Fast’ is an adverb which modifies the verb ‘melts’. Hence, ‘melts fast’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: All the kith and kin of my deceased landlady were present to attend her funeral.
You have hurt so many people. Now, it is time to get a taste of your own medicine.
options: to be treated the way you have treated others
to be in a risky situation
to lose control in a situation
to benefit from two different opportunities
explanation: the way you have treated others.

text: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what is expected out of me.
options: avoiding to talk about the issue
explanation: issue.

text: I have been yet to go to the flower exhibition at Delhi University.
explanation: The given sentence is in the active voice as the subject ‘I’ is the being considered the doer of the action. Therefore, ‘been’ will be removed from the sentence. ‘Have to’ is a semi-modal and takes Pinnacle Sentence Improvement the first form of the verb(go) after it. Hence, ‘have yet’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the option that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the following sentence meaningfully. You all need to (get into) the books prescribed in your syllabus.
explanation: ‘Go through’ is a phrasal verb which means to study something in detail. The given sentence states that you all need to go through the books prescribed in your syllabus. Hence, ‘go through’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She faced a session of abuse after insisting that she was too beautiful to be liked.
explanation: ‘Tirade of abuse’ is the correct phrase to use here. It means a long angry speech in which someone criticies a person. The given sentence states that she faced a tirade of abuse after insisting that she was too beautiful to be liked. Hence, ‘tirade of abuse’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This secret will remain between you and I.
explanation: A preposition takes an objective case pronoun after it. ‘Between’ is a preposition that will take ‘me’ instead of ‘I’. Hence, ‘between you and me’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The plot of the story effects the character and their growth.
explanation: The given sentence needs a verb, not the noun ‘effects’ for the subject ‘the plot of the story’. ‘The plot of the story’ is a singular subject that will take ‘affects’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘affects the character’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The enigma of quantum mechanics remains inscrutably elusive despite of decades of intensive research by the world's leading physicists.
explanation: ‘Despite’ does not take ‘of’. Therefore, ‘of’ will be removed. Hence, ‘despite decades of’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The train left before I reached the station.
explanation: If two actions took place in the past then the 1st action must be in the Past perfect tense (Had + V3) and the 2nd action must be in the Simple Past tense(V2). In the given sentence, ‘train leaving’ is the first action, so it will be written in past perfect tense. Hence, ‘had left(V3) before I reached(V2)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She met my cousin, whose she later married.
explanation: ‘Whom’ is a relative pronoun used for the object in a relative clause. In the underlined part, ‘whom’ has been used for the person she married. Hence, ‘whom she later married’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I decided to call out to various bookstores in the area to see if any of them had the book I needed.
explanation: The phrasal verb ‘call around’ means to phone different people or places. The given sentence states that I decided to make phone calls to various bookstores in the area to see if any of them had the book I needed. Hence, ‘call around’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This lesser known heritage building is so beautiful as the Red Fort.
options: This less known heritage building is much beautiful than the Red Fort.
This heritage building is as beautiful as the Red Fort.
This lesser known heritage building is very much beautiful as the Red Fort.
This lesser known heritage building is as much beautiful as the Red Fort.
explanation: beautiful as the Red Fort. ‘So…as’ is used with ‘not’ to show that two things are not equal. ‘As…as’ or ‘As much… as’ is used to show that two things are equal in certain respects. According to option (d), the lesser known building and the Red fort are equally beautiful. Hence, option (d) has the correct sentence.

text: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of the parts may contain an error. Select the option that rectifies the error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. It was the home minister of the country who took the decision to change a laws pertaining to migration of people from one state to another.
explanation: Article ‘a’ must be replaced with ‘the’. The ‘laws’ mentioned in the given sentence are specific and we generally use the definite article ‘the’ before any specific or particular noun. Hence, ‘the laws pertaining’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. The film received critical acclaim for being a more innovative movie of the year.
explanation: ‘More’ must be removed as there is no comparison in this sentence. Article ‘a’ must be replaced with article ‘an’ as we use ‘an’ before words starting with a vowel sound (an apple, an umbrella, an MBA). Hence, ‘an innovative’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I will definitely return your notes at Saturday evening.
explanation: Preposition ‘by’ is used to indicate a deadline or a specific time before which the action will be completed. The given sentence states that the notes will be returned by evening. Hence, ‘return your notes by’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My sister resembles to my mother a lot in looks and in temperament.
explanation: The verb ‘resembles’ does not take the preposition ‘to’ after it. Hence, ‘resembles’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Effective communication is a skill that can significant enhance your personal and professional life.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adverb(significantly) to modify the verb (enhance) and not an adjective (significant). Hence, ‘which can significantly enhance’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We have received no information so far to the main island.
explanation: ‘From’ is used with ‘receive’ to indicate the source destination or sender. In the given sentence, ‘the main island’ is the source destination from which no information has been received so far. Hence, ‘so far from’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: When he was falsely accused of embezzlement, he was beside himself in anger.
explanation: ‘Be beside oneself’ is a phrase which means to be in an extremely emotional state. The given sentence states that the person was in an extreme state of anger. Hence, option (a) is the most appropriate answer.

text: She is married with a rich businessman and has enough money to splurge on luxuries.
explanation: ‘To’ is used after the verb ‘married’ in the passive voice. Hence, 'is married to' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Sherpas have prospered and come along the way from being just porters to becoming mountaineers.
explanation: The phrase ‘come a long way’ means to make significant progress or improvement. The given sentence states that Sherpas have prospered and made significant progress from being just porters to becoming mountaineers. Hence, ‘come a long way’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: You have a lot of coconut trees in your village, do you ?
explanation: According to the “Question Tag rule”, if the statement is positive, the question tag will be negative & Vice-versa. However, the sentence and the question tag must be in the same tense. Similarly, the given sentence is positive so the question tag will be negative(don’t). Hence, ‘don’t you?’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: By next summer, I will have completed my internship and will have returned to school.
explanation: If two or more verbs are of the same tense then the helping verb is written only once before the first verb. In the given sentence, ‘will have’ is a helping verb of future perfect tense and has been used for both verbs (‘completed’ and ‘returned’). Hence, ‘returned to school’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Tomorrow, they will be take a flight to their dream vacation destination.
explanation: ‘Will be / shall be + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure of Future continuous tense. Hence, ‘will be taking (Ving) a flight’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: As bombs keep falling on Gaza, hundreds of thousands of children have been order to flee their homes.
explanation: ‘Subject + has/have + been + V3’ is the correct grammatical structure for passive voice of Present perfect tense. ‘Ordered’ is the correct third form of ‘order’. Hence, ‘have been ordered(V3) to flee’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The pollution level ought to keep under control.
explanation: Passive voice is used when the action is performed upon the subject, not by the subject. ‘Ought to + be + V3’ is the correct passive form. Hence, ‘ought to be kept(V3) under’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This is the challenge task I have ever encountered.
explanation: Definite article ‘the’ is used for a specific or particular thing and before a superlative degree adjective. ‘Most challenging’ is the correct superlative degree of ‘challenging’. Hence, ‘most challenging’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Ashoka was not only a great warrior but also a very wiser ruler.
explanation: ‘Very’ is a positive adverb and takes a positive degree adjective after it. Hence, ‘wise’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Cinema provides the most universal entertainment.
explanation: There are some adjectives that can not be written in comparative or superlative degree. These adjectives are called absolute or non-gradable adjectives. Some examples are universal, absolute, complete, perfect, empty, full, etc. Hence, ‘a universal’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He is taller and most handsome than his friend.
explanation: If two or more adjectives are joined with a conjunction, these adjectives are written in the same degree. In the given sentence, ‘and’ joins two adjectives, out of which one is comparative degree(taller). Therefore, the second adjective will also be written in comparative degree. ‘More handsome’ is the correct comparative degree of ‘handsome’. Hence, ‘more’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Lots of kids (was visualised) crossing the road when the bus arrived.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘lots of kids’ is a plural subject that will take ‘were’ as a plural verb. Hence, ‘were seen’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The use of chemicals, insecticides and pesticides began after the Green Revolution.
options: A practice of chemicals, insecticides and pesticides
The custom of chemicals, insecticides and pesticides
Consumption of chemicals, insecticides and pesticides
The usage of chemicals, insecticides and pesticides
explanation: ‘Use’ means the act of utilizing something for a specific purpose while ‘Usage’ means the customary or habitual manner in which something is utilized. Hence, ‘The usage of chemicals, insecticides and pesticides’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Identify the sentence that correctly uses the indefinite article.
options: There are three cars parked outside: a Mercedes, an Jaguar and an Fiat.
There are three cars parked outside: an Mercedes, a Jaguar and a Fiat.
There are three cars parked outside: a Mercedes, a Jaguar and a Fiat.
There are three cars parked outside: a Mercedes, an Jaguar and a Fiat.
explanation: Jaguar and a Fiat.(Correct) (a) There are three cars parked outside: a Mercedes, an Jaguar and an Fiat.(Incorrect Article) (b) There are three cars parked outside: an Mercedes, a Jaguar and a Fiat.(Incorrect Article) (d) There are three cars parked outside: a Mercedes, an Jaguar and a Fiat.(Incorrect Article)

text: He is faster than smarter.
explanation: When there is a comparison between two qualities of a single person or thing, we do not use normal comparative degree. E.g.- more smart than beautiful(not ‘smarter than beautiful’). Similarly, the given sentence compares two qualities, ‘fast’ and ‘smart’. Hence, ‘more fast and smart’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The Taj Mahal is one of the much popular seven wonders of the world.
explanation: “One of the + Superlative degree adjective + Plural Subject” is grammatically the correct structure. For example, one of the best men, one of the greatest kings, one of the worst phones, etc. Hence, ‘most’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She trusted her husband but he stabbed her in the neck when he usurped her inheritance.
explanation: ‘Stabbed her in the back’ is the correct idiom that means to be unfaithful or disloyal to. The given sentence states that she trusted her husband but he was unfaithful to her when he usurped her inheritance. Hence, ‘stabbed her in the back’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I like to read books, but my brother prefers to watching movies.
explanation: We generally use an infinitive(V1) with the preposition ‘to’. Hence, ‘to watch’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This case is serious. You need to look into this matter; otherwise, the situation will get out of control soon.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: The village Seoni is located 113 km away from the capital city of MP, Bhopal.
options: adjacent from city capital of MP, Bhopal
proximate from capital of MP, Bhopal
near from the city capital of MP, Bhopal
far from the capital city of MP, Bhopal
explanation: ‘Far’ means situated at a distance or away from a place. Hence, ‘far from the capital city of MP, Bhopal’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Kiran's teacher was doubtful on her success.
explanation: ‘Of’ is a fixed preposition used after the word ‘doubtful’. Hence, ‘doubtful of’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Harry is the one sitting on the corner.
explanation: ‘In’ is used to indicate the location or position of an object or a person. Similarly, in the given sentence, ‘corner’ is the position of Harry. Hence, ‘in’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The Board of Film Analysts vituperated the novice Indonesian film-maker and cancelled its nomination for the 'Golden Globe Award'.
options: dealt in a delicate and polite manner
recognised and praised the talent of
censured with harsh and abusive language
explanation: language.

text: Naina is leaving and I am think to apply for her job.
explanation: ‘Am’ is a helping verb of Present Continuous Tense and ‘is/am/are + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure. ‘About’ is Pinnacle Sentence Improvement used to introduce the topic or subject of discussion or consideration. Also, we always use a gerund (Ving) after a preposition. Hence, ‘thinking(Ving) about applying(Ving)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Malati has a difficult job, but she does it good.
explanation: The given sentence needs an adverb(well) to modify the meaning of the verb ‘does’, not an adjective(good). Hence, ‘well’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He travelled the whole world, but found piece at home.
explanation: ‘Piece’ means a portion of an object or a material while ‘peace’ means a state of being calm and free from any kind of worry or disturbance.The word ‘peace’ makes the sentence meaningful. Hence, ‘peace’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Farmers have harvested wheat by using whatever labour that was available to them.
explanation: ‘Limited’ means a small quantity or number of something. The given sentence states that farmers have harvested their wheat by using a small number of labourers. Hence, ‘by using limited labour’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: You can become confident to speak English within one year.
explanation: ‘In’ is used after the word ‘confident’ to show the specific area or subject in which someone is confident. Hence, ‘confident in speaking’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The unexpected turn beside the project put the company in a big financial crisis.
explanation: ‘In’ is used to indicate involvement while ‘beside’ is used to show that two things are close to each other. The given passage talks about the impact of unexpected change in the project. Hence, ‘in the project’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Politics and money go together in this country.
The decision to engage in an armed conflict is tacit.
The cat climbed a tree and perched itself on a branch.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Fifty rupees feels too much for such a pen.
explanation: ‘Feels’ is used for the sense of touch or emotion and ‘seems’ is used to show what something appears to be. The word ‘seems’ makes the sentence meaningful. Hence, ‘seems’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Despite of an injury, he won the match.
explanation: ‘Despite’ means in spite of and it doesn't take any preposition with it. Hence, ‘Despite’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Lily has dedicate her life towards becoming a doctor.
explanation: “Has/Have/Had + V3(third form of the verb)” is the correct grammatical structure. However, the third form of ‘dedicate’ is ‘dedicated’. Hence, ‘has dedicated(V3)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Health insurance are important today since anyone can face a medical emergency without warning.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb. Similarly, ‘Health insurance’ is a singular subject that will take ‘is’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘is important’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It was a quite afternoon, so Dan decided to take a nap.
explanation: ‘Quite’ is used to emphasize the degree or extent of something and ‘quiet’ describes something that makes no noise. Similarly, in the given sentence, it is stated that it was a quiet afternoon. Hence, ‘a quiet’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: People say different things at different times.
options: say diverse things at different times
says whimsical things at different times
should say fanciful things at different times
says delectable things at different times
explanation: ‘Different’ is used to indicate that two or more things are not the same or not alike in some way. whereas ‘diverse’ means a wide range of differences within a group or a set of things. Hence, ‘say diverse things at different times’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Andrew will playing basketball at the college tournament.
explanation: ‘Is/am/are + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure for Present Continuous Tense. ‘Andrew’ is a singular subject that will take ‘is’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘is playing(Ving)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Selling, purchasing, and using an illegally copied product is a criminal offence.
explanation: pirated

text: With all their little comforts destroyed, the survivors were thrown still farther back into barbarism.
options: still a little farther into barbarism
explanation: ‘Farther’ is used to indicate the physical distance while ‘further’ is used to indicate the figurative/metaphorical distance. Hence, ‘still further back into barbarism’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He said that I have finished my work.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of indirect speech as the conjunction 'that' has been used after the verb 'said'. As per the rules of Indirect speech, the pronouns 'I' and ‘My’ change into 'He' and ‘His’ and ‘Present perfect (have + V3) changes to past perfect (had + V3). Hence, 'he had finished his homework' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Many great people born in that small village.
explanation: We generally use the passive voice when the subject is unknown or unimportant. According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a plural subject always takes a plural verb. Similarly, ‘people’ is a plural subject that will take ‘were’ as a plural verb. Hence, ‘were born’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It is true that learning English is essential for professionals to survived the national and international competitions.
explanation: ‘For’ is used to indicate the purpose or reason of something. Similarly, the given sentence states the purpose of learning English. We generally use gerund(Ving) after a preposition(for). Hence, ‘for surviving(Ving)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Peer pressure is bound to effect most of us both positively and negatively.
explanation: We generally use the first form of the verb(V1) after the preposition ‘to’. ‘Affect’ is the verb form of the noun ‘effect’. Hence, ‘to affect(V1) most of us’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The pandemic has challenged education systems to ensure learning continuity, substantially increasing the demands placed on teachers.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Mohan unknowingly altered salt instead of sugar to the dessert making it taste terrible.
explanation: ‘Alter’ means to change the form of something & ‘add’ means to put in an additional element or ingredient. The word ‘added’ is a more precise and clear choice in this sentence. Hence, ‘added salt instead of sugar’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: No sooner did he finished his examination than he left for his cricket training centre.
options: no sooner than he did finished
explanation: “Do/does/did + V1“ is the correct grammatical structure. Hence, ‘no sooner did he finish’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The Delhi administration is seriously worried about the warning to civic health posed by the polluted waters of Yamuna.
explanation: The phrase ‘the threat to civic health’ means the potential danger or risk to the well-being and overall health of a city. Hence, ‘the threat to civic health’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The food was too salty eat this morning.
explanation: ‘Too + adjective + to + V1’ is the correct grammatical structure. Hence, ‘to eat(V1)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: You are always try with jump over the wall.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of Present Continuous Tense(Plural Sub. + are + Ving). We generally use the preposition ‘to’ with the verb ‘try’ for an activity. Hence, ‘trying(Ving) to jump’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: They are sell their company's products to people.
explanation: We use ‘V-ing’ with the helping verb ‘is/am/are’ in the Present Continuous Tense. Hence, “are selling(V-ing) their company’s” is the most appropriate answer.

text: Virtual reality is the creation of a virtual environment presented to our senses in such a way that we experience it as if we were really there.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Larger emissions of greenhouse gases lead to higher concentrations in the atmosphere.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: No sooner had the sun risen over the horizon when the birds began to chirp and the squirrels started to scamper around the park.
explanation: ‘No sooner….than’ is a fixed conjunction pair. Hence, ‘than the birds began’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I considered Geography as an easier subject.
explanation: ‘An easier’ must be replaced with ‘an easy.’ We need to use a positive degree of adjective as there is no comparison of ‘geography’ with another subject in the given sentence. Hence, ‘an easy’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Rashmi works at the hospital, don't she?
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb and a plural subject always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘she’ is a singular pronoun that will take ‘does’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘doesn’t she’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the word segment which substitutes the bracketed word correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. I (am here) since 1981.
explanation: We generally use Perfect Tense or Perfect Continuous Tense when the time period(for) or the starting point(since) of an action is given in a sentence. 'Be' is a stative verb and stative verbs can not be used in continuous tense. Therefore, Present Perfect Tense(has/have + V3) will be used. Hence, 'have been(V3) here' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Teenage is that phase of life when you are proposed to the world outside.
explanation: ‘Proposed’ means to suggest or put forward an idea while ‘exposed’ means to be introduced to something new or unfamiliar. The given sentence states during teenage years, Pinnacle Sentence Improvement individuals are introduced to the world. Hence, ‘exposed’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Opu was lying in bed waiting for the sun having rose.
options: waited for the sun having rose
waiting for the sun to rise
explanation: We generally use the infinitive form of the verb “to + V1” to combine two actions. Similarly, in the given sentence, the two actions are ‘waiting’ and ‘rising’. Hence, ‘waiting for the sun to rise’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Newton, after seeing the apple falling from a tree, began to wonder whether if it moved towards the earth and not upwards towards the sky.
explanation: The phrase 'began to wonder why' means started thinking about the reason behind the happening of some event. The given sentence states that Newton started thinking about the reason for the fall of the apple towards the Earth, not towards the sky. Hence, 'began to wonder why' is the most appropriate answer.

text: This film is a non-stop riot that many cite as one of the funny films of all time.
explanation: “One of the + Superlative degree adjective (best, worst, etc) + Plural Noun” is grammatically the correct structure. For example, one of the best men, one of the greatest kings, one of the worst phones, etc. Hence, ‘funniest’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If I hand her a flower and say, "Give it to mamma," she take it to her mother.
explanation: According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a singular subject always takes a singular verb. Similarly, ‘she’ is a singular pronoun that will take ‘takes’ as a singular verb. Hence, ‘takes it’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The new chairman of the company announced attracted bonus for the employees on the occasion of the new year.
options: announced an attractive bonus for the employees
announcing attracted bonus for the employees
announced attracting bonus for the employees
explanation: ‘Attracted’ must be replaced with the adjective ‘attractive’ as we need to use an adjective to qualify the noun ‘bonus.’ Hence, ‘announced an attractive bonus for the employees’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Rishi asked Karan will he get a new football for him ?
options: would he get a new football for him?
if he would get a new football for him.
if would he get a new football for him?
if he will get a new football for him?
explanation: In indirect speech, we generally use ‘if’ while changing the interrogative sentence and ‘will’ is changed into ‘would’. Also, the interrogative sentence is changed into an assertive sentence. Hence, ‘if he would get a new football for him’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If you need any help tomorrow, let him knows.
explanation: ‘Let + objective case pronoun(me/him/us) + V1’ is the correct grammatical structure. Hence, ‘let me know(V1)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Helena loves to dig and played in the dirt like any other child.
explanation: According to the ‘Rule of Parallelism’, two or more verbs must be in the same form if they are connected with one another.
