Similarly, in the given sentence, ‘and’ connects two verbs 'dig(V1)’ and ‘played’. Therefore, ‘play(V1)’ must be used in place of ‘played’. Hence, ‘play in the dirt’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The development of skills can contribute to structural transformation and economic growth in enhance employability and labour productivity and helping countries to become more competitive.
explanation: ‘By’ is a preposition that indicates the means or method by which something is done. A preposition is always followed by a gerund(V1-ing). Hence, ‘by enhancing employability’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I used a variety of sources to find the more cheap flight.
explanation: We generally use article ‘the’ with a superlative degree and the correct superlative degree of ‘cheap’ is ‘cheapest’. Hence, ‘cheapest’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: His claim to be the smartly kid in the school was a bit hyperbole !
explanation: We generally use a superlative degree adjective with the definite article ‘the’. The correct superlative adjective of ‘smartly’ is ‘smartest’. Hence, ‘smartest’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The rise in temperature is playing havoc with India's rainfall which is pertinent for India's agriculture sector.
explanation: ‘Significant’ means important. The given sentence states that the rise in temperature is playing havoc with India’s rainfall which is significant for India’s agricultural sector. Hence, ‘rainfall which is significant’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Rahul's sister says that my brother is the best dancer in the city.
options: her brother is the best dancer in the city
my brother was the best dancer in the city
her brother was the best dancer in the city
his brother was the best dancer in the city
explanation: The main subject in the sentence is ‘Rahul’s sister’ which is feminine gender. ‘Her’ is used for feminine gender. Hence, ‘her brother is the best dancer in the city’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: A wonder in the plant kingdom, the Great Banyan Tree of the AJC Bose Botanical Garden at Shibpur in Howrah, occupies a unique position in the world records.
options: being occupied a unique position of
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: It has raining very hard and he has a very large umbrella to keep off the rain-drops.
explanation: Time period is not given in the sentence, so we can not use Present Perfect Continuous Tense. Rather, we will use Present Continuous Tense(Singular Sub. + is + Ving) in the given sentence. Hence, 'is raining' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Adyasha would have been looked gorgeous in ethnic apparel.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of active voice and the correct grammatical structure is ‘would have + V3’. Hence, ‘would have looked(V3)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In today’s world, technology must be used for feed the changing forces in society.
options: must had been used to feed
must have been used to feed
explanation: We generally use an infinitive(V1) with the preposition ‘to’. Hence, Pinnacle Sentence Improvement ‘must be used to feed(V1)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She can draw very well and just as creative.
explanation: We use ‘and’, ‘or’ and ‘but’ to connect two parts of sentences which are similar in grammatical status. Similarly, in the given sentence, 'and' connects the adverb 'well' with another adverb 'creatively'. Hence, 'as creatively' is the most appropriate answer.

text: I have been in Chennai since a week, but I am planning to return now.
explanation: “For” is used for a fixed period of time(countable) like 2 years/3 months/4 days/8 hours and for an activity that happened in a recent time. Similarly, in the given sentence, we can count ‘a week’(one). Hence, ‘for a week’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Peter was brought in the penalty area.
explanation: The phrasal verb ‘bring down’ means to cause someone to fall down. The given sentence states that somebody caused Peter to fall down in the penalty area. Hence, ‘was brought down in the’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Mahesh's attitude annoyed me and I blew into.
options: annoyed me and I blew over
annoyed me and I blew off
annoyed me and I blew down of
annoyed me and I blew up
explanation: The phrasal verb ‘blow up’ means to lose temper or express anger. The given sentence states that Mahesh’s attitude annoyed me so much that I lost my temper. Hence, ‘annoyed me and I blew up’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I don't think he can dance as wellest Elena.
explanation: ‘As...as’ is a comparative structure used to compare two things and ‘as + adjective/adverb + as’ is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. Hence, ‘as well as’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Since the storm knocked in the power, we've been using candles to light our home.
options: the storm knocked out the power
the storm knocked over the power
the storm knocked away the power
explanation: The phrasal verb ‘knock out’ means to cause a failure or disruption. The given sentence states that the storm caused a power failure, so they're using candles for lighting. Hence, ‘the storm knocked out the power’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: If we had moved to Italy when I was a child, I will had an Italian accent.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of a third conditional sentence and the correct grammatical structure for it is “If + past perfect(had + V3) …….. Would have + V3”. Hence, ‘I would have had’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Lewis can handle many of the European languages with its dialectical varieties fluently
explanation: Possessive pronoun ‘Its’ is used for a singular noun and ‘their’ is used for a plural noun. Similarly, ‘European languages’ is a plural noun and it will take ‘their’ with it. Hence, ‘with their dialectical varieties’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Despite having a broken leg, Sarah managed to finish the marathon on record time.
options: finish the marathon in record time
finish a marathon on record time
finish the marathon to record time
finish the marathon at record time
explanation: The phrase ‘in record time’ means within a remarkably short amount of time. Preposition ‘In’ specifies the time frame for the action of finishing the marathon. Hence, ‘finish the marathon in record time’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It is nothing but pride.
explanation: ‘Nothing else’ is used to emphasize a quality or feature that one has. Similarly, in the given sentence, there is emphasis on the quality of pride. Hence, ‘nothing else’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Sujata has not and can never in the good books of her principal as she lacks honesty.
options: has not been and can never be
has not been and can never been
has not be and can never be
has not be and can never been
explanation: ‘Singular Sub. + has + V3’ and ‘Modal(can) + V1’ is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. Hence, ‘has not been(V3) and can never be(V,)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I have been living in this country since last several years but have never experienced any discrimination.
explanation: ‘Since’ is used to denote a point of time like since 1960. ‘For’ is used for a fixed period of time(countable) like 2 years/3 months/4 days/8 hours. Hence, ‘for the last several years’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He got appreciation from every people in a country and abroad.
options: from one and all in the country and abroad
from one or all in a country and abroad
from one and all from a country and abroad
from one and all in country and abroad
explanation: The phrase ‘one and all’ conveys the idea that he received appreciation from everyone. Also, article ‘the’ will be used before the country. Hence, ‘from one and all in the country and abroad’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The mermaid murmured that it had been very difficult for her to live far from human civilisation.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Although he was exhausted from working all day, John continues to study for his upcoming exam.
options: will continue to study for his upcoming exam
has been studying for his upcoming exam
continued to study for his upcoming exam
continues studying for his upcoming exam
explanation: The given sentence contains a verb in past form i.e. “was exhausted” so we will use simple past tense(V2) in the latter part. Hence, ‘continued to study for his upcoming exam’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: One cannot exactly predict the way she behaves in public gatherings
explanation: of something. Predict - to forecast or foretell an event or outcome. Deliberate - to think carefully and consider all aspects before making a decision. Precipitate - to cause something to happen suddenly or unexpectedly. Proliferate - to cause something to happen suddenly or unexpectedly.

text: The most important fruit in Kinnaur is apricot. It is possible to get it at everyplace in huge amount.
options: found for a huge amount everywhere
found everywhere in a huge amount
found everywhere with a huge amount
find everywhere in a huge amount
explanation: The phrase "found everywhere in a huge amount" conveys the same meaning more clearly and grammatically. Hence, ‘found everywhere in a huge amount’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Can you please make sure that all the guest are gathered on the stage before the performance begins?
explanation: We use plural nouns after ‘all’ and the preposition ‘by’ means near or close to something. Hence, ‘guests are gathered by’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She makes sure that all the newly realised books are available in her personal library.
explanation: ‘Released’ means to make something available for public use & ‘realised’ means to become aware of or understand something. The phrase ‘the newly released books’ means the new books which are now available for the public. Hence, ‘the newly released books’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The fall of Ranjith for the petty material benefit was really ignominious.
explanation: ‘Reprehensible’ means deserving blame or strong criticism & ‘Ignominious’ means deserving shame or disgrace. The given sentence states that the fall of Ranjith for the petty material benefit was really deserving of shame. Hence, ‘reprehensible’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The people who live here have had the same kind of lifestyle until hundreds of years.
explanation: ‘Until’ must be replaced with ‘for’ as we generally use preposition ‘for’ to indicate a fixed period of time(countable). Hence, ‘for hundreds of years’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: All colleagues of Rohit except Joseph have commemorated the elective courses they are planning to offer.
explanation: ‘Consider’ means to think carefully about something, before making a decision. The given sentence states that all colleagues of Rohit except Joseph have thought carefully about the courses. Hence, ‘have considered the elective courses’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: As the orchestra began to play, the audience was transported to another world, enthralled by the psychological effects of the music and the skill of the musicians, who performed each note with precision and passion.
options: swept away by the emotive power
taken in by the effect on emotions
explanation: Pinnacle Sentence Improvement The phrase ‘swept away by the emotive power’ means being deeply moved by intense emotions. The given sentence states that the audience was emotionally moved by the music and the skill of the musicians. Hence, ‘swept away by the emotive power’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I need to put out my clothes before I leave for work this morning otherwise, I will be restless when I return.
explanation: The phrase ‘put away’ means to place something in an appropriate or usual place. The given sentence states that I need to put my clothes in a proper place before leaving for work, or I will be restless when I return. Hence, ‘need to put away’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: As the storm raged outside, the children huddled together under blankets, listening to the sound of the rain hitting the windows hard and hoping that the power wouldn't go out.
explanation: hard.

text: Pooja could feel the anger building off inside her.
explanation: The phrase ‘building up’ means becoming stronger or more intense. Hence, ‘building up inside her’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The health-care system is in transition at those moment.
explanation: The phrase ‘at the moment’ means ‘right now’ or ‘currently.’ Hence, ‘at the moment’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The fields are full of crops existing in large quantities.
explanation: ‘Abundant’ means available in large quantities. Hence, ‘that are abundant‘’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She will accept his love proposal if he will express impressively.
explanation: The given sentence is an example of Type 1 conditional and the correct grammatical structure is “if + simple present…….will +V1”. Hence ‘if he expresses’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Could you please tell me which movie you would like to watch tonight ?
explanation: The phrase ‘would like to’ is a polite way of expressing our preference or intention to do or have something. Similarly, we use the phrase ‘wish to’ to express our desire or intention to do something. Hence, ‘you are wishing to watch’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In according to his advice I took this medicine.
explanation: ‘In accordance with’ is the correct phrase. ‘In accordance with’ means following or obeying a rule, law or advice. Hence, ‘accordance with’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I am trying to study, if it is impossible with all this noise.
explanation: We generally use the conjunction ‘but’ to express a different opinion or idea. Hence, ‘but it is impossible’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Can you please tell me where is the city park.
explanation: Whenever Wh. Words(like who, whom, where, why, how, etc) are written in the middle of a sentence, the helping verb and the main verb are written after the subject. E.g. - I do not know where she lives. Therefore, ‘is’ will be used after the subject ‘city park’. Hence, ‘where the city park is’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: This hill is a nice place to meditate because one can enjoy solitude.
options: is a nice place to be meditation
is an excellent place to meditates
is a nasty place to meditate
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: No less than eight pedestrians were killed in the accident.
explanation: ‘Fewer’ is used when we are comparing countable objects i.e. pedestrians. Hence, ‘No fewer than’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: How do you think the internet has influenced how we utilise news and media?
options: has managed the patterns we ingest
has revoked the way we interact
has impacted the way we consume
explanation: The word "consume" means to take in information or media and the phrase "has impacted the way we consume" states the idea of change in the way we take in digital content. Hence, ‘has impacted the way we consume’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Meenakshi called out for the neighbourhood to get support for her campaign.
explanation: The phrase ‘call around’ means making calls or contacting different individuals or locations. The given sentence states that Meenakshi contacted or reached out to various people or places within her neighborhood to seek support for her campaign. Hence, ‘called around the neighbourhood’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Despite facing numerous obstacles and setbacks, the determined entrepreneur refused to give up on her dream of creating a successful startup that would transform the sector.
explanation: ‘Revolutionise’ means to bring about significant change or transformation in something, which has the same meaning as the phrase “that would transform the sector”. Hence, ‘that would revolutionise the industry’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Amal brightened of when they said he could go with them.
explanation: ‘Brightened up’ is a phrasal verb that means to become happier or more cheerful. Hence, ‘brightened up when they’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The company is planning to cut back few employees.
explanation: ‘Lay off’ means to discharge an employee temporarily or permanently because of shortage of work or funds. The given sentence states that the company is discharging some employees. Hence, ‘lay off some’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: From a recent research, evident is it that a lot more women have been opting for professional courses.
options: it is evident that more a lot women
it is evidently that a lot more women
it is evident that a lot more women
it is evidence that a lot more women
explanation: ‘Subject + Verb + Object/Complement’ is the correct grammatical structure of a sentence. Hence, ‘It is evident that a lot more women’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She is the least reliablest person of all.
explanation: ‘Least / most reliable’ is the correct superlative degree of ‘reliable’. Hence, ‘least reliable’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The young artist spent countless hours perfecting her craft, trying with various methods and mediums, and honing her creative vision until she had produced a stunning collection of works that showcased her unique talent and perspective.
explanation: The phrase ‘experimenting with different techniques’ means trying out various methods to achieve a goal. The given sentence states that the young artist spent countless hours trying out various methods and mediums. Hence, ‘experimenting with different techniques’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The students were restored to complete the assignment by Friday.
explanation: ‘Expect’ means to think that something will happen. The word ‘expect’ makes the sentence meaningful. Hence, ‘expect’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The GDP of the country has growth rapidly since independence.
explanation: ‘Has/have/had + V3’ is the correct grammatical structure. Hence, ‘has grown(V3) rapidly’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She had an ability to persuade others.
explanation: Impress- to make a strong impact or influence on someone. Persuade- to convince or influence someone to do something. Halt- to pause or to stop for a short period of time. Suppress- To stop or prevent something. Outrage- to make someone angry by repeating an inappropriate behaviour.

text: We must remember that what we teach our children is what we inculcate in them.
explanation: repeatedly teaching. Inculcate- to gradually introduce something in a person's mind. Endanger- to put someone or something at risk or in a dangerous situation. Inspire- to motivate or encourage someone. Import- to bring in goods or services from another country.

text: The fact that God created man in his personal view by giving him an intellectual spirit elevates him above the beasts of the field.
explanation: The phrase "in his own image" is commonly used to describe the belief that God created human beings with characteristics or attributes resembling his own. Hence, ‘own image’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The frog adopts itself to live both in water and on land.
explanation: ‘Adapt’ means to become adjusted to new conditions. In the given sentence, the frog is adjusting or modifying itself to live both in water and on land. While, ‘Adopt’ means to legally take (another's child) and bring it up as one's own. And ‘Adept’ means a person who is skilled or proficient at something. Hence, ‘frog adapts itself’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Natwar was a fraudster who always tried to fooling others.
explanation: something false. Fooling- tricking someone into believing something that is not true. Betraying- to be disloyal to someone or something. Cheating- to act dishonestly or unfairly in order to gain an advantage. Revealing- to make something known that was previously hidden.

text: The Indian independence movement sought to establish the conceptions of freedom and social welfare as the goals of an independent Indian state, resulting in Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.
explanation: The phrase "concept of liberty" means the idea of freedom which includes making your own choices and living your life the way you want. The given sentence states that the Indian Independence movement attempted to establish the concept of liberty and social welfare. Hence, ‘concepts of liberty’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Carolina opened a savings account to save money for later.
explanation: The idiom 'for a rainy day' means saving money or resources for our future needs. Hence, 'for a rainy day' is the most appropriate answer.

text: The management is not beware of this fact.
explanation: The phrase ‘beware of’ means to be aware of something. This phrase can not be used with a stative verb (‘is’ in this sentence). Therefore, ‘beware of’ must be replaced with ‘aware of’ to make a grammatically correct structure. Hence, ‘Aware of’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Last week's rain ravaged the whole city.
explanation: Ravaged - to cause great damage to something or someone. Pinnacle Sentence Improvement Reaffirmed - to state something again clearly and firmly. Rescinded - to state that a law or decision is no longer valid. Retracted - withdrawn or taken back, typically a statement or promise.

text: National development is defined as an improvement in people's daily arrangements, the provision of fundamental necessities to citizens such as food, education, social services, medical help, and so on, as well as an increase in per capita income.
explanation: The phrase 'living conditions' means the overall quality of life, including things like housing, health, education, income, safety, and the environment. The given sentence states that national development is defined as the improvement in the overall quality of people's lives. Hence, 'living conditions' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Please ask the dog to get of my couch.
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the sentence. Preposition ‘of’ must be replaced with ‘off’ as the phrase ‘get off’ means to leave a particular place or position. Hence, ‘get off my’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The mob drove on the rampage and looted several shops in the locality.
explanation: ‘Drove’ must be replaced with ‘went’ as the phrase ‘go on a rampage’ means to rush around in a wild or violent way, causing damage or destruction. Hence, ‘went on rampage’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I don’t wear the sunglasses at the moment.
explanation: The phrase ‘at the moment’ describes an action happening right now. And we generally use present continuous tense(is/am/are + V-ing) to denote an action happening at the current moment. Hence, ‘I’m not wearing’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Her hopes for building her own house were beaten when she lost her jewellery box.
explanation: ‘Beaten’ must be replaced with ‘dashed’ as ‘dashed’ means destroyed or ruined. Hence, ‘house were dashed when’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Irene went to office every single day by walk.
explanation: The phrase ‘on foot’ is used when a person travels by walking. Hence, ‘every single day on foot’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In times of difficulty, she preys for an oracle to guide her.
explanation: ‘Preys’ must be replaced with ‘prays’ as ‘pray’ means to talk to God or a higher power. While ‘Prey’ means an animal that is caught and killed by another for food. Hence, ‘prays’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In today's digital age, information is widely available to everyone by many means of media such as television, newspapers, films, and social media.
explanation: The term ‘means’ means a method used for doing something such as means of transport. Whereas the term ‘forms’ means a particular type of variety of something. In the given sentence, various types of media have been listed, such as television, newspapers and films. Hence, ‘via various forms’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Abhijeet feels extremely tired after working all day long.
Disability was viewed as God's retribution for wickedness in the past.
explanation: The phrase “retribution for wickedness” means punishment for wrongdoing. Hence, ‘punishment for wrongdoing’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Many noticeable people were present at the function.
explanation: ‘Noticeable’ means capable of being noticed or seen easily while ‘Notable’ means worthy of notice or attention due to some special quality or significance. Hence, ‘notable’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Brian remained silent during the board meeting, though Rahul was unaware that he had an ace up his sheath the entire time.
explanation: The idiom "an ace up his sleeve" means having a secret plan or advantage that is kept hidden until the right moment to use it. Hence, ‘an ace up his sleeve’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Bajrang is in extreme pain in his teeth.
explanation: Ache - a continuous, dull pain or discomfort in a part of the body. Hurt - to experience physical or emotional pain or distress. Sting - to cause a sharp, sudden pain, often from a bee or insect bite.

text: The players distributed the reward between themselves.
explanation: We use ‘among’ for more than two persons and ‘between’ for two persons. However, there are more than two persons (players) mentioned in the given sentence. Hence, ‘among themselves’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Greenhouse gases trapped beside Earth's atmosphere cause global warming.
explanation: The phrase ‘trapped inside’ means trapped within something. Similarly, In the given sentence, greenhouse gases are trapped within the Earth's atmosphere. Hence, ‘trapped inside’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Arthur has some strange ideas, but on this occasion, I am inclined to agree with him.
explanation: Inclined - willing or likely to do something. Conflicted - having opposing feelings. Refused - declined or said no to something. Conspired - planned secretly to do something harmful or unlawful.

text: During the wedding ceremony, the bride seemed even quieter and more diffident than usual.
options: Giving a false or misleading impression
Shy due to lack of confidence.

text: Parents should tell their children to exercise great care when crossed busy roads
explanation: If 'when' is used without the subject and the auxiliary verb 'be', it always takes the present participle form(V-ing) of the verb. Hence, 'crossing(V-ing)' is the most appropriate answer.

text: This compartment is reserved for military person.
explanation: "Military personnel" refers to individuals who are part of the armed forces or military services of a country. So, we will use ‘military personnel’ in place of ‘military person’. Hence, ‘military personnel’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Abraham Lincoln has been the sixteenth president of the United States and save the Union at the American Civil war.
explanation: ‘Save’ must be replaced with ‘saved’ as we need to use ‘Simple Past Tense(V2)’ to denote actions that happened in the past Hence, ‘saved the union during’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My friend Meera and her mother is visiting me this weekend.
explanation: According to the Subject-Verb agreement rule, If two subjects are connected with conjunction ‘and’ then they will be treated as a plural subject and will take a plural verb only. Hence, ‘are visiting’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The commanders entered by force into terrorists' camp.
explanation: The phrase “broke into” means to enter somewhere by force. Hence, ‘broke into’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The young boy displayed an aptitude on scientific research.
explanation: There is a prepositional error in the given sentence. Preposition ‘on’ must be replaced with ‘for’ as Aptitude for" used to describe someone's natural ability or skill in a particular field or activity. Hence, ‘aptitude for’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He had given me that book in 1999.
explanation: ‘Had given me’ must be replaced with ‘gave me’ as “Simple Past Tense(V2)” is used to state facts that were true in the past. Pinnacle Sentence Improvement Hence, ‘gave(V2) me’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: There is a charm on the midnight air which all cannot experience.
explanation: Preposition 'in' is used to indicate the presence or location of something within a certain place or condition. Similarly, in the given sentence 'charm' is a quality that is present in the midnight air. Hence, 'in the midnight air' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Being a practiced liar, it was totally normal for him to utter a complete and blatant lie.
explanation: Falsehood - a complete and blatant lie. Blasphemy - disrespectful or offensive words or actions towards religious beliefs. Whooper - someone who tells big lies or makes exaggerated claims. Perjury - telling a lie after promising to tell the truth, especially in a court of law.

text: Pintu has been advised to reduce smoking by his family doctor.
explanation: The phrasal verb ‘cut down’ means to reduce. Hence, ‘cut down’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The heavy medications and strong drugs at the sanatorium will surely turn a patient completely lifeless and unresponsive.
explanation: ‘Cadaverous’ means something that is extremely pale, gaunt, and resembling a lifeless or dead body in appearance. Hence, ‘cadaverous’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I worked hard so that I might success.
explanation: ‘Modal verbs’ are auxiliary verbs(also called helping verbs) like can, will, could, shall, must, would, might, and should. However, after a modal verb, we generally use the first form of the verb (V1). Hence, ‘might succeed(V1)’ is the most appropriate structure.

text: The stranger stood quietly for few moments.
explanation: 'Few' means negligible or zero whereas 'a few' means a small but considerable number of something. Therefore, ‘few’ must be replaced with ‘a few.’ Hence, ‘for a few moments’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He did not stop until it was remarked that he was speaking at length about trivial things.
explanation: Twittering - bird sounds. Littering - carelessly dropping trash, creating a mess.

text: The question was raised for discussion before the members during the assembly session.
explanation: The phrase ‘came up’ means to be raised, as in a discussion. Hence, ‘came up’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The rebels laid up their arms
explanation: The phrase “laid down” means surrendering or putting something down. Hence, ‘Laid down’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She has gained a lot of fame but still she is very realistic and sensible.
explanation: down to it- focused on the task at hand. down to bottom- at the lowest point. down to drown- to sink under water and die.

text: He was advised for walking alone in the neighbourhood.
explanation: The verb ‘advise’ is often followed by the preposition ‘against’ when giving a warning to avoid something. Hence, ‘advised against’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The volunteers of the organisation refused point blank of do what was requested.
options: refused in point blank of doing
explanation: ‘Of’ must be replaced with ‘to’ as ‘refused point blank’ is an idiom and it should be followed by ‘to + infinitive(V1).’ Hence, ‘refused point blank to do’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Students were asked to write the historical events in the order of their occurrence.
explanation: chronological order - in the order of their occurrence. Aesthetic order - organize things in a way that emphasizes their beauty. Historic order - arranging things based on their historical importance or relevance. Diachronic order - organizing things based on their evolution or changes over time

text: Raju did very well in the exam, he must study well.
explanation: We need to use present perfect tense (have + V3) to indicate the action that was completed in the past but has connection to the present. The given sentence states that Raju did very well in the exam, he must have studied well. Hence, ‘must have studied(V3) well’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select "no substitution required". The unit twitched like a bird (preening it's plumage and becomes motionless).
options: preening its plumage and became motionless
preening it's plumage while becoming motionless
to preen it's plumage and becomes motionless
explanation: Possessive form of the pronoun ‘It’ will be used i.e. ‘Its’ and of 𝑉2 ‘become’ will be used as the first clause of the sentence is in the past tense. Hence, ‘Preening its plumage and became motionless.’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required". No, they are normal people, (although they perceive the world different).
options: but they perceive the world differently
from they perceive the world differently
while they perceive the world different
explanation: Conjunction ‘but’ will be used instead of ‘although’ as we use ‘but’ to connect ideas that contrast and adverb ‘differently’ will be used to describe the verb ‘perceive’. Hence, ‘but they perceive the world differently’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: At the grocery store, coffee is in an same aisles as tea.
explanation: Article ‘the’ is used to refer to specific or particular nouns. Similarly, the given sentence talks about a specific noun (aisle). Hence, ‘the same aisle as’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required. The rodeo is (great way to unite soldier's skills and build) esprit de corps.
options: a great way to unite soldiers' skills and build
great way to unite soldier's skills and building
a great way to unite an soldier's skill and build
explanation: We generally use article ‘a’ to refer to a nonspecific or general noun. Hence, ‘a great way to unite soldiers' skills and build’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The waiter giving the diners some complimentary mints.
explanation: ‘Giving’ will be replaced by ‘gave’ as we generally use past indefinite(V₂) to describe completed actions or events that occurred in the past. Hence, ‘gave’ is the most appropriate Pinnacle Sentence Improvement answer.

text: The water leaked in with a hole in the roof.
explanation: ‘With’ must be replaced with ‘through’ as we generally use the preposition (through) indicating movement or passage from one side or location to another. Hence, ‘through a hole’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required". This looks (like one of those unwelcome social summons which call upon a man) either to be bored or to lie.
options: like one of those unwelcome social summonses which call upon a man
like one of these unwelcome social summons that call upon a man
like one of those unwelcome social summon that call upon a man
explanation: which call upon a man ‘Summons’ must be replaced with ‘Summonses’ as we use plural nouns (summonses) with ‘these/those’. Hence, ‘like one of those unwelcome social summonses which call upon a man’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given. She ran 12 kms at a stretch, (which are a greater) distance for a rookie.
explanation: ‘Which are a greater’ must be replaced with ‘which is quite some’ in the given sentence. whom are part of the cricket crowds, some of whom are presumably born in England
who are part of the cricket crowds, some of whom are presumably born in England
explanation: the relative pronoun must be ‘who’ and if it is followed by a noun or pronoun, then the relative pronoun must be ‘whom’. Hence,‘who are(verb) part of the cricket crowds, some of whom are presumably born in England’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: There has been a noticeable fall in the number of children dying from malnutrition.
explanation: The given sentence is grammatically correct.

text: Dad said that, “She would have been a great sister if she was just a bit more careful”.

"She would have been a great sister if she were just a bit more careful”
“She would have been a greatest sister if she was just a bit more careful"

text: The number of women working outside homes has been steady increasing.
explanation: modify the verb(increasing) and not an adjective(steady). Hence, ‘has been steadily increasing’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Edward II is tragic than some other plays by the dramatist.

text: Bloomberg Businessweek is not more popular than some other business magazines in the US.

The preposition ‘into’ used after the verb ‘looking’ is incorrect & it must be replaced with the correct preposition ‘for’ because ‘looking for’ which means to search something is the correct phrase. Hence, ‘looking for his book’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Navika is a superb and impressive child in her class.
explanation: Splendid - very good, excellent Dazzling - causing strong admiration Vivid - having or producing a strong, clear picture in your mind

text: I went to Paris regularly.
explanation: ‘An adverb of time’ can tell us about when an action happens. Moreover, late, tomorrow, today, everyday, weekly, yearly, yesterday, last month, tonight, last week, immediately, etc. are some adverbs of time. Similarly, the given sentence is in the past tense(went), and for that, we will use an adverb of time in the past tense. Hence, ‘yesterday’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The new shop that opened last week are hardly sufficient stock of the products that it advertised about.
explanation: According to the Rule of Inversion, the verb always be used after the adverbs like Hardly, Scarcely, Barely. Hence, ‘hardly had(verb)’ is the most appropriate answer.

explanation: The given sentence needs an adjective ‘populous’ and not a verb ‘populated’. Hence, ‘populous’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Last before year, Shirley got very good grades.
explanation: ‘The year before last’ means during the year before the previous one. The given sentence states that Shirley got very good grades in the year before the previous one. Hence, ‘The year before last’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Oscar is the most prestigious award which is introduced to good actors in that year.
explanation: Oscars are ‘awards’ which are generally awarded and not introduced. Moreover, we will use a superlative degree adjective(best) for the actors getting the award. Hence, ‘awarded to best’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of the adverb of frequency.
options: Radha goes to Nagpur with great affection.
Radha goes to Nagpur for her office work.
Radha goes to Nagpur to meet her uncle.
explanation: An adverb of frequency is a word that can be placed after the noun or pronoun in a sentence to give more information about the verb, adjective or another adverb. Some examples of adverbs of frequencies are rarely, often, always, never and sometimes. Similarly, ‘often’ as an adverb of frequency is perfectly used in option ‘c’. Hence, ‘Radha often goes to Nagpur’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Rita will never have changed her job if she would have been promoted.
explanation: The given sentence is in the past tense so the verb must be used in the past form(V2). Hence, ‘would(V2) never have’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Santa Claus stays at the North Pole when he isn’t out deliver gifts for Christmas.
explanation: “Preposition(out) + V-ing” is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence. Hence, ‘out delivering(V-ing)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The intern should take a right choice in choosing the right job for her.
explanation: We generally use the verb ‘make’ with choice and not ‘take’. Hence, the correct phrase for the given sentence is ‘make a right choice’ that means to make the right decision.

text: Old people acquire experience through age.
explanation: We generally use the verb ‘gain’ before experience and not ‘acquire’. The given sentence is a fact so simple present tense will be used. Hence, ‘gain experience’ is the correct phrase.

text: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.
options: By means of rope ladders they scaled the wall.
Along with means of rope ladders they scaled the wall.
in means of rope ladders they scaled the wall.
Of means of rope ladders they scaled the wall.
explanation: ‘By means of’ is a phrase that means with the help of something. The given sentence states that they scaled the wall with the help of rope ladders. Hence, ‘By means of rope ladders they scaled the wall’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.
explanation: ‘Fond of something’ means having feelings of affection for something. Similarly, the given sentence states that Children have feelings of affection for sweets. Hence, ‘Children are fond of sweets’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.

Ashok was to the bus stop.
Ashok was on the bus stop.
Ashok was at the bus stop.
explanation: We generally use the preposition ‘at’ to describe a particular position/place. Similarly, the bus stop is the particular position/place in the given sentence. Hence, ‘Ashok was at the bus stop’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Unemployment has become a fiery question of the day.
explanation: ‘A burning question’ means an urgent or crucial issue under heated discussion. The given sentence states that unemployment has become an urgent or crucial issue of the day. Hence, ‘become a burning question’ is the most appropriate answer.

explanation: ‘Talked’ means to discuss something serious or important. Talked about is phrasal verb. The given sentence states that they talked about the political turmoil in the state. Hence, ‘talked’ is the most appropriate answer.

Hence, ‘celebrated across the country’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The rate of interest for the loan went out all our calculations .
explanation: The preposition ‘out’ must be replaced with ‘beyond’ because ‘go/went beyond calculations’ is the correct phrase that means something that you cannot count. Hence, ‘beyond all our calculations’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Shyama does not laugh, nor she smiles.
explanation: contain the verb ‘does’ for the correct grammatical context. Hence, ‘nor does she smile’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The MNC is about to be bankrupt, according to reliable sources.

text: Computers and mobile phones have become a necessary and important part of our lives.
explanation: must have or do. The given sentence states that computers and mobile phones have become a necessary and essential part of our lives. Hence, ‘an essential’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Many companies displaced playing income tax last year.
explanation: ‘Evade’ means to manage to escape from or to avoid meeting somebody/something. The given sentence states that many companies did not pay income tax last year. Hence, ‘evaded paying’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We have only just enough money to live on now, and if my husband loses his job, we’ll really be up again it.
explanation: ‘Up against’ is a phrase that means in a difficult situation. The given sentence states that we have only just enough money to live on now, and if my husband loses his job, we’ll really be in a difficult situation. Hence, ‘be up against it’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Blind by a dust storm, they fell into disorder.
explanation: A participle(‘ed) is that form of the verb which partakes of the nature of both of a Verb and of an Adjective and a phrase which is introduced by a participle is called a participial phrase. Similarly, in the given sentence, 'blinded' will be the past participle and the phrase that it governs is 'blinded by a dust storm'. Hence, ‘Blinded’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He was not able to adopt himself to the new environment of the hostel.
explanation: ‘Adopt’ means to accept or start to use something new and ‘Adapt’ means to change yourself or something according to conditions. The given sentence states that he was not able to change himself according to the new environment of the hostel. Hence, ‘able to adapt himself’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: You must aware of friends who speak against you.
explanation: ‘Aware of’ means conscious(having knowledge) of something and ‘Beware of’ means to be cautious and alert to risks or dangers. In the sentence it has been stated that “You must beware of (cautious of) friends who speak against you”. Therefore, ‘Beware of’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The percentage of employees who called in sick and the number of employees who left their jobs within 2 years (were reflective of the level of job satisfaction).
options: are reflective of the level of job satisfaction
is reflective of the level of job satisfaction
has reflected the level of job satisfaction
were reflective on the level of job satisfaction
explanation: The given sentence is in the simple present tense so the verb must be used in the simple present form(V1). Hence, ‘are(V1) reflective of the level of job satisfaction’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: They decided to have a meeting to discuss about the project.
explanation: We do not use ‘about’ with the verb ‘discuss’ as it is a transitive verb that requires a direct object. Hence, ‘to discuss the project’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The bus is now full of passengers, it will leave soon.
explanation: The given sentence is in the present tense and we often use the present continuous tense to talk about the future, especially about future plans. Hence, ‘is going to leave’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: As Simon had already been to the park, he lead the way for the other children.
explanation: If two actions took place in the past then the 1st action must be in the Past perfect tense(Had + V3) and the 2nd action must be in the Simple Past tense(V2). Therefore, ‘Led(V2) the way’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Between Raima and Saima, the former is intelligent, while the latter is beautiful.

text: They are cautious about their car as it’s door is broken
explanation: (It’s) is a contraction of the words it and is/has and ‘Its’ is the possessive form of the pronoun ‘It’ which is used to refer to the noun ‘Car’. Hence, ‘As its’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He is a weak student and somehow pulled over the exams.
explanation: ‘Pulled through’ is a phrase that means to succeed in surviving a difficult period. The given sentence states that he is a weak student and somehow succeeded to survive/pass the exams. Hence, ‘pulled through’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Identify the sentence that correctly uses the indefinite article.

'Amateur' is a noun which refers to a person who takes part in an activity as a hobby or for pleasure and not as an job.
'Amateur' is a noun which refers to an person who takes part in an activity as a hobby or for pleasure and not as a job.
'Amateur' is a noun which refers to a person who takes part in a activity as a hobby or for pleasure and not as a job.

Hence, ‘Amateur' is a noun which refers to a person who takes part in an activity as a hobby or for pleasure and not as a job’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: His last trip around the world taking a toll on his health.

text: The application of the medicine seemed to lesson his pain.

text: You can have a comfortable journey only then you are getting your seats reserved in advance.

text: Extreme sadness and pitiful cries of people filled the whole atmosphere.

text: He pays me six dollars the month of this house.

text: She was stuck in his imagination for many a hour as a force to be reckoned with.

text: A. Suddenly I noticed smoke pouring in through the seams of the ceiling. B. Groping our way to the front door we all ran out into the front yard. C. The smoke began to fill the room so quickly that we could barely see. D. I ran to the neighbours to call the fire department. E. Further, Sentence D states that the narrator ran to the neighbors to call the fire department & Sentence F states that the narrator saw his/her mother run back into the house. So, F will follow D. Going through the options, option a has the correct sequence.

text: A. The mountaineers set up a camp at a height of 15000 feet. B. Then they started climbing. C. They struggled up a steep slope and stopped at a height of 20000 feet. D. There they stayed for a week to get accustomed to the climate.

text: A. Combining Vitamins A, C and D3 with Zinc and Probiotics gives a good flu-fighting remedy. B. Vitamin C plays a vital role in maintaining the body’s natural defence. C. It also supports a healthy immune system. D. People with low vitamin C are at a much greater risk of getting infections.

text: A. I pointed them out to my companion. B. The woman’s face was familiar but I could not recall who she was. C. At the very next table to ours, sat Lady Edgware and Brian Martin. D. As I was doing so, another couple came and joined them.

So, B will follow D. Going through the options, only option a has the correct sequence.

text: A. That is why, when a person shows off we say, ‘as vain as a peacock’. B. It gives us the impression of being a very proud bird. C. But the fact is that the peacock is not vain, it displays its plumage to attract the peahen. D. When the peacock dances, it spreads its feathers.

text: A. “Today, respect is shown in different ways,” she said, “students have a more questioning bent of mind.” B. Vidya Subramaniam occupies a small but privileged place in the dance world that has seen the old guard giving place to the new. C. So, A will follow C. Going through the options, option c has the correct sequence.

text: A. It was known as Lolark Ghat earlier and was renamed in honour of the saint. B. In 1941, industrialist B.D. Birla undertook the renovation of the ghat. C. Birla undertook the renovation of the ghat. So, B will follow A. Going through the options, option b has the correct sequence.

text: A. Saranda forests, in Singhbhum, are a huge catchment for rivers and streams in this state. B. If these forests are opened up for mining purposes the remaining rivers and streams will dry up. C. The state of Jharkhand faces water scarcity every summer. D. text: Technology has made it possible for us to reach out to more students, and it has also made it possible for us to deliver the same lessons in a much more ________ manner.
explanation: ‘Resourceful’ means to able to find and use different ways to achieve your goals. The given sentence states that technology has also made it possible for us to deliver the same lessons in a much more resourceful manner. Hence, ‘resourceful’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: You can tell yourself that you would be willing to lose everything you have in order to get something you want: all of those things you're willing to lose are what make you _________.
explanation: ‘Recognisable’ means easy to identify or recognise. The given sentence states that all of those things you’re willing to lose are what make you recognisable. Hence, ‘recognisable’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate form and tense of the bracketed verb in the following sentence to fill in the blank. I'm busy today. I'd rather we _______ (has) the meeting tomorrow.
explanation: Simple past tense is used after “would rather / ’d rather” when the subjects are different. In the given sentence, the subjects ‘I’ and ‘we’ are different. Therefore, past form(V2) of the verb will be used. Hence, ‘had(V2)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The difference between a male and a female still ______ in our society. In this era where women have such great achievements in every field, still in some sections of our community, a man is always termed as superior to women.
explanation: ‘Persist’ means to continue to exist. The given sentence states that the difference between a male and a female still persists in our society. Hence, ‘persists’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Their plan of acquisition was _______ flawed from the very beginning; it was bound to fail.
explanation: ‘Fatally’ means in a way that leads to failure. The given sentence states that their plan of acquisition was fatally flawed from the very beginning. It was bound to fail. Hence, ‘fatally’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It may seem _______ that the hours of women's chores at home have not declined inspite of the availability of many appliances (gas, electric ranges, washing machines, etc.)
explanation: ‘Perplexing’ means difficult to understand. The given sentence states that it may seem perplexing that the hours of women’s chores at home have not declined in spite of the availability of many appliances (gas, electric ranges, washing machines, etc.) Hence, ‘perplexing’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The seven _______ for accreditation were presented in a seminar organised by the university.
explanation: The given sentence needs a plural noun after the plural word ‘seven’. ‘Criteria’ is the plural form of ‘criterion’. Hence, ‘criteria’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The business operates ________ the same way as the other businesses did.
explanation: The phrase ‘much the same’ means very similar. The given sentence states that the business operates much the same way as the other businesses did. Hence, ‘much’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The tree lost many of its ________ in the heavy rain and storm.
explanation: ‘Branch’ is one of the parts of a tree which grows out from the main trunk. The given sentence states that the tree lost many of its branches in the heavy rain and storm. Hence, ‘branches’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: A dam is a barrier that stops the flow of water and results in the creation of a______.
explanation: ‘Reservoir’ means a place for storing liquid. The given sentence states that a dam is a barrier that stops the flow of water and results in the creation of a reservoir. Hence, ‘reservoir’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Spending quality time with friends and family is also_____ to have a healthy daily routine. These happy moments release happy hormones in the body.
explanation: ‘Obligatory’ means required to be done. The given sentence states that spending quality time with friends and family is also obligatory to have a healthy daily routine. Hence, ‘obligatory’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: ________, I'm going to walk my dog.
explanation: ‘Now’ is used in present continuous tense to indicate an activity that is currently happening or going to happen. Hence, ‘now’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate article
options: to fill in the blanks. I was in ______ state of unconsciousness Pinnacle Fill in the blanks for about half ________ hour.
explanation: Article ‘A’ is used before the words starting with a consonant sound - (a conversation, a story). Whereas, the article ‘An’ is used before the words starting with a vowel sound(an imminent danger, an apple). In the given sentence, ‘state’ starts with a consonant sound and ‘hour’ starts with a vowel sound. Hence, ‘a ; an’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The rising rate of inflation is making life very hard for ________ poor.
explanation: When article ‘the’ is used before an adjective, it becomes a common noun and refers to all those denoted by the adjective. ‘The poor’ refers to all the people who are poor. Hence, ‘the’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He has not ___ returned the money.
explanation: ‘Yet’ is used in present perfect tense with ‘not’ to indicate that something has not happened till this time. Similarly, in the given sentence, the person has not returned the money till this time. Hence, ‘yet’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It’s funny how every time he fails to apply the _________ and _______ the glass.
explanation: ‘Brakes’ are the components of a vehicle used to stop it. ‘Break’ means to shatter something into pieces. The given sentence states that it’s funny how every time he fails to apply that brakes and breaks the glass. Hence, ‘brakes; breaks’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: His family lives _______ Mahu in Madhya Pradesh.
explanation: ‘At’ is used to indicate a specific place within a larger location. Similarly, ‘Mahu’ is a specific place in Madhya Pradesh. Hence, ‘at’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Accepting how wonderful you truly are and incorporating this _______ into your attitude and personality is perhaps one of the most difficult things to do in life.
explanation: ‘Insight’ means an accurate and deep understanding. The given sentence states that accepting how wonderful you truly are and incorporating this insight into your attitude and personality is perhaps one of the most difficult things to do in life. Hence, ‘insight’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Please put the dishes in the _______ after you finish eating.
explanation: ‘Sink’ means a basin in a kitchen for washing dishes. The given sentence states a request to put the dishes in the sink after you finish eating. Hence, ‘sink’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My grandparents live in a beautiful house _________ the countryside.
explanation: ‘In’ is used for larger, more general locations, such as cities, states, countries, etc. ‘Countryside’ is a general location, meaning the land and scenery of a rural area. Hence, ‘in’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Leif Erikson is a Viking ________ believed to have sailed from the Green Lands to Vinland. Vinland is now thought to be the northern tip of Canada's Newfoundland island where ________ found evidence of Erikson's ________ in 1960s.
explanation: settlement ‘Explorer’ means someone who travels to places about which very little is known. ‘Archaeologist’ is a scientist who studies human history by digging up human remains and artifacts. ‘Settlement’ means a place where people come to live. The given sentence states that Leif Erikson is a Viking explorer. Vinland is now thought to be the northern tip of Canada’s Newfoundland island where archaeologists found evidence of Erikson’s settlement in 1960s. Hence, ‘explorer; archaeologists; settlement’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate idiom/phrase to fill in the blank. My car __________ on the way to college yesterday.
explanation: ‘Broke down’ is the past form of the phrasal verb ‘break down’, which means to stop working. The given sentence states that my car broke down on the way to college yesterday. Hence, ‘broke down’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The manager swiftly overtook him, ____________ effortlessly past the skinny Englishman, with a practiced ease.
explanation: ‘Sliding’ means moving smoothly and effortlessly. The given sentence states that the manager swiftly overtook him, sliding effortlessly past the skinny Englishman, with a practised ease. Hence, ‘sliding’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The charismatic leader's speeches were known for their ________ impact on motivating people to take positive actions.
explanation: ‘Profound’ means very great or intense. The given sentence states that the charismatic leader’s speeches were known for their profound impact on motivating people to take positive actions. Hence, ‘profound’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The rising interest in and concern about animal welfare resulted in legislative laws and the formation of The Animal______Committee in many nations.
explanation: ‘Ethics’ means moral principles that govern a person's behaviour or the conducting of an activity. The given sentence states that the rising interest in and concern about animal welfare resulted in legislative laws and the formation of The Animal Ethics Committee in many nations. Hence, ‘ethics’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate degree of comparison to fill in the blank. Work in this office is done in the_____way.
explanation: Article ‘the’ is used before the superlative degree. ‘Least efficient’ is the correct superlative degree of ‘efficient’. Hence, ‘least efficient’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The coaches decided to______ the regulations more strictly because the candidates were not paying attention during their training sessions.
explanation: ‘Enforce’ means to cause a law or rule to be obeyed. The given sentence states that the coaches decided to enforce the regulations more strictly because the candidates were not paying attention during their training sessions. Hence, ‘enforce’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: There was no one left in the world whom they could call _______.
explanation: ‘Theirs’ is a possessive pronoun used with the pronoun ‘they’. ‘Their’ is a possessive adjective used with a noun. As there is no noun after the blank, we can not use possessive adjective. Hence, ‘theirs’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I begin to pronounce the sequence of words and numbers that will prevent her from giving him a piece of her ______.
explanation: ‘Give someone a piece of one’s mind’ is an idiom which means to speak to someone in an angry or critical way. The given sentence states that I begin to pronounce the sequence of words and numbers that will prevent her from giving him a piece of her mind. Hence, ‘mind’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Due to_______ 'eve teasing', parents conclude that it is not worth the danger of sending their daughters to school.
explanation: ‘Widespread’ means happening in many places. The given passage states that due to widespread ‘eve teasing’, parents conclude that it is not worth the danger of sending their daughters to school. Hence, ‘widespread’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I could _____ the reason for being _____.
explanation: ‘Find’ means to discover something by chance. ‘Fined’ means charged with an amount of money as a punishment for not obeying a rule or law. The given sentence states that I could find the reason for being fined. Hence, ‘find; fined’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She was a ______, ______, _______ astronaut.
explanation: The correct order of adjectives is- opinion, size, origin. ‘Smart’ is an adjective expressing an opinion. ‘Tall’ indicates size. ‘Indian’ indicates origin. Hence, ‘smart, tall, Indian’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The writer's __________ prose resonated with readers, evoking powerful emotions.
explanation: ‘Eloquent’ means giving a clear and strong message. The given sentence states that the writer’s eloquent prose resonated with readers, evoking powerful emotions. Hence, ‘eloquent’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Michael Jackson is known as the King of Pop. He ________ his own genre of music, Pop. His music is spreading its influence and popularity ________ the world.
explanation: ‘Dominate’ means to be the most important person or thing in a field. The phrase ‘around the world’ means everywhere in the world. The given sentence states that Michael Jackson is known as the King of Pop. He dominates his own genre of music, Pop. His music is spreading its influence and popularity around the world. Hence, ‘dominates; around’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He is going to ______ the campaign against excessive use of _______ in local production units.
explanation: ‘Lead’ in the 1st blank means to guide in a direction. ‘Lead’ in the 2nd blank means a very heavy, soft, dark grey poisonous substance. The given sentence states that he is going to lead the campaign against excessive use of lead in local production units. Hence, ‘lead’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Despite facing numerous challenges, the team successfully ______ the project ahead of schedule.
explanation: ‘Completed’ is the correct verb to use here, indicating simple past tense. ‘Successfully’ is an adverb which modifies the verb completed. Hence, ‘completed’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The assignment was ______ early in the morning.
explanation: ‘Due’ means expected at a certain time. The given sentence states that the assignment was due early in the morning. Hence, ‘due’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The teacher asked the students to remain ____, but the noise continued to ____. She finally had to raise her voice to gain control.
explanation: ‘Quiet’ means not making any noise or disturbance. ‘Rise’ means to increase in amount or level. The given sentence states that the teacher asked the students to remain quiet, but the noise continued to rise. She finally had to raise her voice to gain control. Hence, ‘quiet; rise’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: With the increasing reliance on digital systems, ensuring robust cybersecurity measures is __________ to protect against online threats.
explanation: ‘Paramount’ means more important than anything else. The given sentence states that with the increasing reliance on digital systems, ensuring robust cybersecurity measures is paramount to protect against online threats. Hence, ‘paramount’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Vinod had a ________ escape in the car accident
explanation: The phrase ‘narrow escape’ means a situation in which an accident or other unfortunate incident is only just avoided. The given sentence states that Vinod had a narrow escape in the car accident. Hence, 'narrow' is the most appropriate answer.

text: The group of travellers were wonderstruck by the ________ of the coin.
explanation: The given sentence states that the group of travellers were wonderstruck by the weight of the coin. Hence, ‘weight’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Two of the fugitives managed to remain free by adeptly avoiding the _________ of the police.
explanation: ‘Pursuit’ means the act of following someone to try to catch him. The given sentence states that two of the fugitives managed to remain free by adeptly avoiding the pursuit of the police. Hence, ‘pursuit’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: We have postponed this movie outing too many times, so we are going tomorrow, come _____ or shine.
explanation: The given sentence states that we have Pinnacle Fill in the blanks postponed this movie outing too many times, so we are going tomorrow, come rain or shine. Hence, ‘rain’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: He had _____ the ______ into smaller clips.
explanation: ‘Clipped’ means cut short neatly & ‘clipping’ means an article cut from a newspaper or magazine. The given sentence states that he had clipped the clipping into smaller clips. Hence, ‘clipped, clipping’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: After years of fights with his neighbour Ram, Shekhar decided to hold out the _______ and invited Ram for tea.
explanation: ‘Olive branch’ is an idiom which means an offer or gesture of conciliation or goodwill. The given sentence states that after years of fights with his neighbour Ram, Shekhar decided to hold out the olive branch and invited Ram for tea. Hence, ‘olive branch’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: To __________ the ticket, Amith had to visit the travel agency many times.
explanation: ‘Confirm’ means to be sure of something. The given sentence states that to confirm the ticket, Amith had to visit the travel agency many times. Hence, ‘confirm’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Kamal is not willing to purchase a house on the 12th floor of a sea-side apartment, as she is fearful of heights. She is suffering from ___________.
explanation: ‘Acrophobia’ is an irrational fear of heights. The given sentence states that Kamal is not willing to purchase a house on the 12th floor of a sea-side apartment, as she is fearful of heights and she is suffering from acrophobia. Hence, ‘acrophobia’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Ram went to _____ an ice cream.
explanation: The given sentence states that Ram went to buy an ice cream. Hence, ‘buy’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank. They _______ their house for the past two months, and it’s finally starting to look fantastic.
explanation: Perfect continuous tense is used with ‘for/since’ indicating the period of time. ‘Plural subject (they) + have been + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure of present perfect continuous tense. Hence, ‘have been renovating’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The US ________ building was built in the year 1800.
explanation: ‘Capitol’ means the building in which the US Congress meets. The given sentence states that the US capitol building was built in the year 1800. Hence, 'capitol' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Sharat is always ___________ about showing up for work because he believes that tardiness gets us nowhere.
explanation: ‘Punctual’ means doing something at the agreed or proper time. The given sentence states that Sharat is always punctual about showing up for work because he believes that tardiness gets us nowhere. Hence, 'punctual' is the most appropriate answer.

text: Raj is very interested in studying human psychology, so he decided to pursue his master’s degree in __________.
explanation: The given sentence talks about the interest of Raj in studying human psychology. Hence, ‘psychology’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The mother couldn’t ______ such an insult from her son in front of the others.
explanation: ‘Bear’ means to tolerate or accept something. The given sentence states that the mother couldn’t bear such an insult from her son in front of the others. Hence, ‘bear’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank. Akshaya __________ hard for the entrance exam and received a high score.
explanation: The given sentence is in the past tense, so it must have the verb in the past form(V2). Hence, ‘studied(V2)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I like bread made up of corn ______.
explanation: ‘Flour’ means powdered grain, especially of wheat. The given sentence states that I like bread made up of corn. Hence, ‘flour’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank. The team ____________ the championship before their star player got injured.
explanation: If two actions took place in the past then the 1st action must be in the Past perfect tense(Had + V3) and the 2nd action must be in the Simple Past tense (V2). The first action is winning the championship. Hence, ‘had won (V3)’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Yesterday, I ate only a ____ of apples for my dinner.
explanation: ‘Pair’ means a set of two things. The given sentence states that yesterday, I ate only a pair of apples for my dinner. Hence ‘pair’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: In both countries we have leaders of_____ ability.
explanation: ‘Exceptional’ means much greater or better than usual. The given sentence states that we have leaders of exceptional ability in both countries. Hence ‘exceptional’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: It took 4 hours straight to _______the deal with the regional company.
explanation: ‘Close’ is the correct verb to use with ‘deal’. ‘Closing the deal’ means to make a successful business arrangement with someone. Hence, ‘close’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate option that can best replace the bracketed word to fill in the blank. His ________ stature was not a measure of his overall personality. (scrawny)
explanation: ‘Scrawny’ means unattractively thin and bony. The given sentence states that his thin stature was not a measure of his overall personality. Hence, ‘thin’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. ________is a red-coloured root vegetable.
explanation: vegetable that grows in the ground and is usually cooked and eaten cold Beat - to defeat somebody Bit - a small amount or piece of something. Bead - a small, round ball of glass, plastic, or wood that is used for making jewellery.

text: Both the criminals were cruel and ______.
explanation: ‘Brutal’ means savagely violent. The given sentence states that both the criminals were cruel and brutal. Hence, ‘brutal’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: I was in the________ of a meeting when somebody called me.
explanation: The phrase ‘in the middle of’ means involved in some activity. The given sentence states that I was involved in a meeting when somebody called me. Hence, 'middle' is the most appropriate answer.

text: After a day long trek, we were so tired that we were ready to _________.
explanation: sleep.

text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. Ravi is _______.
explanation: ‘Bald’ means having no hair. The given sentence states that Ravi is bald. Hence ‘bald’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The two brothers ______when their father died.
explanation: that ends a relationship.

text: The teacher asked the students to ______ electricity by switching off lights when they left the room.
explanation: The given sentence states that the teacher asked the students to save electricity by switching off lights when they left the room. Hence ‘save’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate article to fill in the blank. _________ bed you sleep in is broken.
explanation: ‘Bed’ mentioned in the given sentence is specific and we generally use the definite article ‘the’ before any specific or particular noun. Hence, ‘the bed’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She could easily eat the _____biryani by herself.
explanation: ‘Whole’ means all of something. The given sentence states that she could easily eat the whole biryani by herself. Hence, ‘whole’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate option that collocates with ‘wish’ to fill in the blank. The genie asked Aladdin to ______a wish.
explanation: ‘Make’ is the correct verb to use with ‘wish’. The phrase ‘make a wish’ means to wish for something. The given sentence states that the genie asked Aladdin to make a wish. Hence, ‘make’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She ________ gracefully and greeted the interview committee with respect.
explanation: The given sentence states that she smiled gracefully and greeted the interview committee with respect. Hence, ‘smiled’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: My sister's paintings were ________at the national museum.
explanation: ‘On display’ is the correct phrase used to indicate that something is being shown for public viewing. Similarly, my sister’s paintings were being shown for public viewing at the national museum. Hence, ‘on display’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Many developing nations are having a _________economy these days.
explanation: ‘Booming’ means experiencing rapid growth. The given sentence states that many developing nations are having a booming economy these days. Hence ‘booming’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The movie ‘Desperate Ghosts’ was watched by my younger brother and he was _______ horror.
explanation: ‘Filled with’ is to express that someone experiences a strong emotion or feeling. The given sentence states that the movie ‘Desperate Ghosts’ was watched by my younger brother and he was filled with horror. Hence, ‘filled with’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The boxer was knocked out cold by a powerful________ punch to the jaw.
explanation: ‘Right’ means done in the correct way. The given sentence states that the boxer was knocked out cold by a powerful right punch to the jaw. Hence, ‘right’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: A sailor was______through the high tides.
explanation: ‘Singular Sub + was + Ving’ is the correct grammatical structure for the given sentence which is in the past continuous tense. Hence, ‘sailing’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The _______in my shoelace created a lot of trouble.
explanation: ‘Knot’ means a join made by tying together the ends of a string. The given sentence states that the knot in my shoelace created a lot of trouble. Hence ‘knot’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. Namita still cannot ________ the pain of her cat’s untimely demise.
explanation: ‘Bear’ means to tolerate. The given sentence states that Namita still cannot bear the pain of her cat’s untimely demise. Hence ‘bear’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The crowd gave them a_____of applause.
explanation: ‘Round of applause’ is a phrase which means to show appreciation by clapping your hands repeatedly. The given sentence states that the crowd gave them a round of applause. Hence ‘round’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Fill in the blank using the correct collocation. We need to_______a decision on the housing project tomorrow morning.
explanation: We generally use the verb ‘make’ or ‘take’ with the noun ‘decision’. ‘Make a decision’ means to make a choice about something. Hence, ‘make’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Complete the given sentence with an appropriate homophone from the given options. It is better to focus on your ________ than to wander aimlessly.
explanation: ‘Career’ means a profession or occupation chosen as one's life's work. The given sentence states that it is better to focus on your career than to wander aimlessly. Hence ‘career’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. The mechanics tried a lot to get that car _______ from the accident spot.
explanation: ‘Tow’ means to pull or drag a vehicle by means of a rope or cable. The given sentence states that the mechanics tried a lot to get that car towed from the accident spot. Hence ‘towed’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The new construction sites have______ attack by the environmentalists.
explanation: ‘Come under’ is the correct phrasal verb to use here. ‘Come under attack’ means to be attacked. The given sentence states that the new construction sites have come under attack by the environmentalists. Hence, ‘come under’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: She went on a shopping spree with her friend and made him _______ the fat bill.
explanation: The given sentence states that she went on a shopping spree with her friend and made him pay the fat bill. Hence, ‘pay’ is the most appropriate answer.

text: The captain dropped the trophy while he ________the victory with his teammates
